definition_zh: 大量存在；充满；富于；盛产
definition_en: to exist in large numbers or quantities, or to be full of something
core_image: 水从容器边缘漫出来，四周到处都是
scene: 雨后的草坡上，蘑菇一丛丛冒出来。 Mushrooms abound on the wet hillside after rain.
sceneCN: 这里 abound 是「大量存在」（第 1 个义项：某物数量很多地出现）；句意为雨后湿润的山坡上蘑菇大量生长。

pos.zh: 大量存在；众多
富于；充满

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「丰富；充裕」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「丰富的；大量的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「丰富地；大量地」

senses.title: To exist in large numbers
senses.definition: of things, to be present in large numbers or quantities
senses.definitionCN: 指事物以很大的数量出现
senses.example: Wild flowers abound in this valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷里野花繁盛。
senses.why: Latin abundare meant 'to overflow'; what abounds is so plentiful that it spills over the edges of the container.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abundare 意为「溢出」；abound 的东西多到从容器边缘漫出来。

senses.title: To be rich in something
senses.definition: to have a great deal of a particular quality or thing
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量的某种性质或事物
senses.example: The region abounds in mineral resources.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区矿产资源丰富。
senses.why: A place that overflows with a resource is described with in or with, the container and its contents named together.
senses.whyCN: 一个充满某种资源的地方用 in 或 with 来连接，容器与内容被一起说出。

senses.title: Of animals: to be numerous
senses.definition: of animals or plants, to occur in great numbers in a habitat
senses.definitionCN: 指动植物在某一栖息地大量出现
senses.example: Deer abound in these forests.
senses.exampleCN: 这些森林里鹿群众多。
senses.why: Living things that fill a habitat are pictured as filling a vessel to overflowing.
senses.whyCN: 填满栖息地的生物，被想象成把容器装到溢出。

senses.title: Of talk or rumour: to circulate widely
senses.definition: of stories, rumours, or ideas, to be widespread
senses.definitionCN: 指说法、传闻或观念广泛流传
senses.example: Rumours abound about the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 关于合并的传闻四起。
senses.why: Words and stories can also overflow a community, spreading faster than anyone can count.
senses.whyCN: 话语与故事也会漫过一个社群，传播得比谁数得都快。

senses.title: Of a place: to produce plentifully
senses.definition: of a region or farm, to yield large crops or products
senses.definitionCN: 指地区或农场产出大量作物或产品
senses.example: The orchards abound with apples in autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天果园里苹果累累。
senses.why: The overflow image turns agricultural: the harvest is more than the baskets can hold.
senses.whyCN: 溢出的意象转向农业：收成多到篮子装不下。

senses.title: To be filled with problems
senses.definition: to be full of something undesirable, such as errors or complaints
senses.definitionCN: 充满不想要的东西，如错误或抱怨
senses.example: The report abounds with errors.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告错误百出。
senses.why: The same 'full to overflowing' pattern works for defects, which crowd a text as water crowds a jar.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「满到溢出」结构也适用于缺陷，它们挤满文本，像水挤满罐子。

senses.title: Of resources: to be plentiful
senses.definition: of resources or supplies, to be available in large amounts
senses.definitionCN: 指资源或供给以大量形式存在
senses.example: Clean water abounds in the northern valleys.
senses.exampleCN: 北部山谷中清洁水源充裕。
senses.why: Plenty is measured as volume: a resource that abounds is one whose supply spills past demand.
senses.whyCN: 充裕以体量来衡量：abound 的资源就是供给溢过需求。

senses.title: Of ideas: to spring up
senses.definition: of ideas or possibilities, to appear in great number
senses.definitionCN: 指想法或可能性大量出现
senses.example: New ideas abound at the start of a project.
senses.exampleCN: 项目开始时新想法层出不穷。
senses.why: Abstract things are imagined as a flow that rises and spreads, so an active period is one where ideas abound.
senses.whyCN: 抽象事物被想象成上涨漫开的流，因此活跃时期就是想法 abound 的时期。

intro.en: Abound comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to overflow', built from a prefix and the word for a wave.
intro.cn: abound 来自一个意为「溢出」的拉丁语动词，由前缀与表示「波浪」的词构成。

items.en: The root *wed- is reconstructed with the sense 'water'; it also lies behind English water and wet.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *wed- 被重构为「水」之义；英语 water 与 wet 也源自它。

items.en: unda meant 'a wave, water', and it produced undulate and inundate.
items.cn: unda 意为「波浪、水」，衍生出 undulate 与 inundate。

items.en: undare meant 'to rise in waves, flow', a verb of water moving in volume.
items.cn: undare 意为「波浪涌起、流动」，是一个表示水大量运动的动词。

items.en: ab- 'away, from' plus undare formed abundare, 'to overflow, be plentiful'.
items.cn: ab-（离开）与 undare 构成 abundare，意为「溢出、丰盛」。

items.en: Old French abonder carried the sense 'to be plentiful' into medieval use.
items.cn: 古法语 abonder 把「丰盛」之义带入中世纪用法。

items.en: English abound keeps the two patterns abound in and abound with, and extends to rumours, errors, and ideas.
items.cn: 英语 abound 保留 abound in 与 abound with 两种结构，并扩展到传闻、错误与想法。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adjective, and adverb from the same family, plus two water-root words; the second gathers verbs for being plentiful.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的名词、形容词与副词，以及两个同「水」词根的词；第二组收表示丰盛的动词。

entries.definition: The noun meaning a very large quantity of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「丰富、充裕」，指某物数量极大。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning existing in large quantities.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「丰富的、大量的」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'plentifully or very clearly'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「丰富地、大量地」，也可表示「十分清楚地」。

entries.definition: To flood or overwhelm, from the Latin word for a wave.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「淹没、使应接不暇」，来自表示波浪的拉丁词。

entries.definition: To move in waves, from the same Latin noun unda.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「波动、起伏」，来自同一个拉丁名词 unda。

entries.definition: To be full of things, especially living things, moving in great numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「充满、涌动」，尤指大量生物活动。

entries.definition: To move or gather in large numbers, like bees.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「成群移动、蜂拥」，像蜜蜂一样大量聚集。

entries.definition: To increase rapidly in number.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「激增、迅速繁殖」。

entries.definition: To grow or develop well and plentifully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「繁茂、兴旺」，生长或发展得很好很多。

entries.definition: To be so full that contents spill over.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「溢出」，满到内容物漫出。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the two fixed patterns abound in and abound with and the water image; the abstract hooks picture the overflow.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 abund in 与 abound with 两个固定结构及水的意象；抽象记忆点想象溢出。

normal.en: Abound in and abound with are the two patterns; in names the place, with names the contents.
normal.cn: abound in 与 abound with 是两个结构；in 引出地点，with 引出内容。

normal.en: Abundance is the noun and abundant the adjective, both from the same overflow image.
normal.cn: 名词是 abundance，形容词是 abundant，二者都来自同一个「溢出」意象。

normal.en: Rumours abound and opportunities abound are common news and business phrases.
normal.cn: rumours abound 与 opportunities abound 是常见新闻与商业短语。

normal.en: The Latin source is undare, 'to flow in waves', so abound is water overflowing a rim.
normal.cn: 拉丁来源是 undare（波浪流动），因此 abound 就是水漫过边缘。

normal.en: The -s form abounds is used with singular subjects such as wildlife.
normal.cn: -s 形式 abounds 与 wildlife 等单数主语连用。

abstract.en: Picture a barrel filled until water runs down its sides.
abstract.cn: 想象木桶被装到水从桶壁流下。

abstract.en: Picture mushrooms pushing up through wet grass in every direction.
abstract.cn: 想象蘑菇从湿润的草丛里向四面八方冒出来。

abstract.en: Picture a room so full of talking people that voices spill into the street.
abstract.cn: 想象房间挤满说话的人，声音漫到街上。

examples.en: Fish abound in these cold rivers.
examples.cn: 这些寒冷的河流里鱼群繁多。

examples.en: The internet abounds with misleading claims.
examples.cn: 网络上充斥着误导性说法。

examples.en: Examples of this pattern abound in the corpus.
examples.cn: 这种模式的例子在语料库中大量存在。

sensesIntro.en: The senses all grow from 'overflow': things, animals, words, crops, resources, and ideas can all fill a space past its edges.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都从「溢出」生长出来：事物、动物、言语、作物、资源与想法，都能把空间装到漫出边缘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water running over the rim of a full vessel
core.cn: 核心意象：水从装满的容器边缘漫出

branches.en: Things, animals, and crops fill a place beyond counting.
branches.cn: 事物、动物与作物把一处空间装到数不清。

branches.en: A place or supply is rich in a resource, named with in or with.
branches.cn: 某地或供给富于某种资源，用 in 或 with 引出。

branches.en: Words and rumours fill a community and spread widely.
branches.cn: 言语与传闻充满社群并广泛传播。

branches.en: Undesirable things such as errors crowd a text.
branches.cn: 错误等不想要的东西挤满文本。

branches.en: Ideas rise and spread in an active period.
branches.cn: 在活跃时期，想法涌起并扩散。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem abund-, the noun ending -ance, and the adjective and adverb endings -ant and -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 abund-、名词后缀 -ance，以及形容词与副词后缀 -ant、-ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin abundare and unda are the direct source of abound and its family, so the Latin entries record both the verb and the wave noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abundare 与 unda 是 abound 及其词族的直接来源，因此拉丁条目同时记录动词与「波浪」名词。

definition_zh: 严格的；严谨的；严密的；严苛的；严酷的
definition_en: carried out with great care and strict standards, leaving no step unchecked
core_image: 实验室里每份样本都要两个人各自核对，记录上少一行就整批重做
scene: 实验室里，每一批样本都要两人分别核对，任何一步记录不全就得重做。 The trial's rigorous protocol required two independent checks for every sample.
sceneCN: 这里指标准严格、不留缺口（第 1 个义项：严格而彻底的）；句意为该试验的严谨规程要求每份样本都做两次独立核对。图中可辨识物件：样本架、双人核对表、签名栏、重做标记。

pos.zh: 严格的；严谨的；严密的；严酷的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「严格地；严谨地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「严格；严谨」
由同一拉丁词干构成，义为「严格；严酷；严谨」
由同一拉丁动词的另一形容词形式构成，义为「坚硬的；僵化的」
由「僵硬的」加名词尾构成，义为「刚性；僵化」

senses.title: Strict and thorough
senses.definition: done with great care and with no step left unchecked
senses.definitionCN: 以极大的仔细进行，每一步都被核查
senses.example: The safety review was rigorous, and nothing was signed off on trust.
senses.exampleCN: 安全审查十分严格，没有任何一项是靠信任签字的。
senses.why: The Latin root means stiffness, and a stiff procedure does not bend to convenience.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「僵硬」，僵硬的程序不会为图方便而弯折。

senses.title: Demanding testing
senses.definition: testing carried out under hard, controlled conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在严苛且有控制的条件下进行的测试
senses.example: The battery underwent rigorous testing at high and low temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 电池在高温与低温下接受了严苛测试。
senses.why: Tests are rigorous when the conditions are harder than ordinary use.
senses.whyCN: 当条件比日常使用更苛刻，测试就是严苛的。

senses.title: A proof with no gaps
senses.definition: a proof in which every step is justified
senses.definitionCN: 每一步都有依据的证明
senses.example: A rigorous proof does not rely on a diagram that merely looks right.
senses.exampleCN: 严密的证明不依赖一张只是看起来正确的图。
senses.why: In mathematics the word means the argument cannot be loosened anywhere.
senses.whyCN: 在数学里，这个词意味着论证在任何一处都不能放松。

senses.title: Hard training
senses.definition: training that is physically or mentally severe
senses.definitionCN: 在体力或心力上都很艰苦的训练
senses.example: Rigorous training prepared the crew for a month at sea.
senses.exampleCN: 严酷的训练让船员为海上一个月做好了准备。
senses.why: Training borrows the word because a strict method also trains the will.
senses.whyCN: 训练借用这个词，因为严格的方法也在训练意志。

senses.title: Standards without shortcuts
senses.definition: standards that admit no exceptions for convenience
senses.definitionCN: 不为方便开例外口子的标准
senses.example: The journal applies rigorous standards to every submission, even invited ones.
senses.exampleCN: 该期刊对每篇投稿都适用严格标准，受邀稿也不例外。
senses.why: A standard is rigorous when the exception costs more than the rule.
senses.whyCN: 当例外的代价高于规则，标准才是严格的。

senses.title: Analysis that checks its assumptions
senses.definition: analysis that tests its own assumptions rather than assuming them
senses.definitionCN: 检验自身假设、而不是直接假定成立的分析
senses.example: A rigorous analysis of the survey must first ask who was not asked.
senses.exampleCN: 对这项调查的严谨分析，首先要问谁没有被问到。
senses.why: The analysis turns the strictness on itself, which is the highest form of the method.
senses.whyCN: 分析把严格对准自身，这是该方法最高的形态。

senses.title: Selection by hard tests
senses.definition: choosing only those who pass demanding tests
senses.definitionCN: 只让通过高要求测试者入选
senses.example: The fellowship uses a rigorous selection process with three rounds of review.
senses.exampleCN: 这项奖学金采用三轮评审的严格筛选流程。
senses.why: Selection is rigorous when the gate, not the label, does the choosing.
senses.whyCN: 当做出选择的是门槛而不是标签，筛选才是严格的。

senses.title: Enforcement without leniency
senses.definition: applying a rule fully, with no relaxed exceptions
senses.definitionCN: 完整执行规则，不作宽松的例外
senses.example: Rigorous enforcement of the smoking ban changed behaviour within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 禁烟规定的严格执行在一个月内改变了行为。
senses.why: Enforcement completes the word: the rule now has hands as well as words.
senses.whyCN: 执行补全了这个词：规则如今不光有条文，还有手。

intro.en: Rigorous comes from Latin rigor, stiffness or hardness, from rigere, to be stiff, with an adjective ending that reached English through French. The physical stiffness became a moral and methodological one: a standard that will not bend. The same root also gives rigid and rigor mortis.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 rigor「僵硬、坚硬」，出自 rigere「僵直」，加形容词尾后经法语进入英语。身体上的僵硬变成了道德与方法的僵硬：不肯弯折的标准。同一词根还给出 rigid 与「尸僵」一语。

items.en: Rigere meant to be stiff or numb, said of limbs and of cold.
items.cn: 这个词意为僵直、麻木，用于肢体，也用于寒冷。

items.en: Rigor named stiffness, hardness and, by extension, severity of rule or climate.
items.cn: 这个词指僵硬、坚硬，并引申指规则或气候的严酷。

items.en: Later Latin formed an adjective meaning full of stiffness or severity.
items.cn: 后起拉丁语构成形容词，意为「充满僵硬或严酷的」。

items.en: French carried the adjective into the language of law and method.
items.cn: 法语把该形容词带入法律与方法的语言。

items.en: English applied it to rules, proofs and training.
items.cn: 英语把它用于规则、证明与训练。

items.en: Research methods fixed phrases such as rigorous testing; the first date of each is uncertain.
items.cn: 科研方法固定了「严苛测试」等说法；各自首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the stiffness root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of strictness. The note warns that vigorous looks like a relative but comes from a different root.
note.cn: 第一组共享「僵硬」词根或形近；第二组指其他「严格」的说法。这里提醒：形近的「精力充沛」一词出自另一词根，并非同族。

entries.definition: Strictness or severity, and in medicine, a chill.
entries.definitionCN: 指严格或严酷，医学上指寒战。

entries.definition: Stiff and unable to bend, literally or in attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 指僵硬不能弯，字面或态度上皆可。

entries.definition: In a strict and thorough way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以严格而彻底的方式。

entries.definition: The quality of being strict and thorough.
entries.definitionCN: 指严格而彻底的性质。

entries.definition: Full of energy and strength; its root means to be lively, not stiff.
entries.definitionCN: 指精力充沛、强健；其词根意为「有生气」，并非「僵硬」。

entries.definition: Insisting on exact obedience to rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指坚持对规则的精确遵守。

entries.definition: Complete, with no part left out.
entries.definitionCN: 指完整、没有遗漏任何部分。

entries.definition: Showing extreme attention to small details.
entries.definitionCN: 指对细小处极度注意。

entries.definition: Tight and demanding, often of rules or conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 指紧而苛刻，多用于规则或条件。

entries.definition: Demanding a great deal of effort or precision.
entries.definitionCN: 指要求大量努力或精确。

entries.definition: Harsh in force or treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 指在力度或对待上严厉。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two signature lines, the frozen joint, the long proof and the three-round review.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两行签名、冻僵的关节、冗长的证明与三轮评审。

normal.en: A rigorous process has two signatures where one would do.
normal.cn: 严谨的流程在一个签名够用的地方放两个。

normal.en: Rigid means the joint will not bend; rigorous means the rule will not bend.
normal.cn: 「僵硬的」说关节不弯，「严格的」说规则不弯。

normal.en: A rigorous proof leaves no step to the reader's goodwill.
normal.cn: 严密的证明不把任何一步留给读者的善意。

normal.en: Rigorous training is remembered in the body, not in the notes.
normal.cn: 严酷的训练被记在身体里，而不是记在笔记里。

normal.en: Vigorous is about energy and rigorous is about stiffness, though they sound alike.
normal.cn: 「强健的」讲精力，「严格的」讲僵硬，尽管读音相似。

abstract.en: Strictness is a promise that the result will not depend on who was watching.
abstract.cn: 严格是一种承诺：结果不取决于当时谁在看。

abstract.en: The same stiffness that protects a result can freeze a field for a generation.
abstract.cn: 保护结果的那种僵硬，也可能把一个领域冻住一代人。

abstract.en: A rigorous standard is expensive, which is why it is often replaced by its description.
abstract.cn: 严格的标准很贵，所以常被它的描述所取代。

examples.en: The claim survived rigorous testing by three independent laboratories.
examples.cn: 这一主张经受了三家独立实验室的严苛测试。

examples.en: Her analysis was rigorous, and it questioned the survey's own assumptions.
examples.cn: 她的分析很严谨，也质疑了调查自身的假设。

examples.en: Rigorous enforcement, not new rules, reduced the accident rate.
examples.cn: 降低事故率的是严格执行，而不是新规则。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞格若斯」：规矩「硬」得像冻住的关节，一步也不肯弯，检查才做得严

root: 源于拉丁语表示「僵直」的动词，其名词义为「僵硬、严酷」，后起形容词再经法语进入英语。同族有表示「严格」「僵硬的」「刚性」的词；形近而表示「精力充沛」的词出自表示「有生气」的另一词根。十六世纪进入英语；各技术短语首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses turn stiffness into method: a thorough procedure, demanding tests, gapless proofs, hard training, standards without shortcuts, self-checking analysis, strict selection, and full enforcement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把「僵硬」变成方法：彻底的流程、严苛的测试、无缺口的证明、艰苦的训练、不许走捷径的标准、自查假设的分析、严格筛选与完整执行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two signatures on every sheet, and a whole batch is redone if one line is missing.
core.cn: 核心意象：每张记录上两个签名，少一行就整批重做。

branches.en: THE STIFF PROCEDURE: care that refuses convenience in every ordinary step.
branches.cn: 僵硬的程序：在每个寻常步骤上都不为方便让步。

branches.en: THE HARD TEST AND THE HARD DRILL: strict conditions, and training built under them.
branches.cn: 严苛的测试与艰苦的训练：严格的条件，以及在条件下筑起的训练。

branches.en: THE CLOSED ARGUMENT: proofs and analyses with no step left to goodwill.
branches.cn: 封闭的论证：不把任何一步留给善意的证明与分析。

branches.en: THE UNBENDING RULE: standards and enforcement that admit no exceptions.
branches.cn: 不肯弯的规则：不容例外开的标准与执行。

branches.en: THE NARROW GATE: selection that only lets the tested through.
branches.cn: 窄门：只让过关者进入的筛选。

intro.en: Rigorous is a Latin stiffness noun with an adjective ending; its family covers rigidity, strictness and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「僵硬」名词加形容词尾；词族覆盖刚性、严格与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin rigere and rigor supply the stiffness, and the later adjective rigorosus gives the English form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「僵直」与「僵硬」提供词干，后起形容词给出英语形态。

items.example: It forms rigorousness.

definition_en: great size or importance, or the size of a quantity measured on a scale
core_image: 同一把刻度尺同时量山的高度与地震的力量，标记一路向上
scene: 地震台值班员盯着纸带上跳动的曲线，把刚测到的数字写进记录表。 The seismologist logged a magnitude of six point two after the tremor.
sceneCN: 这里指「地震释放能量的大小等级」（第 4 个义项：按对数标尺给出的震级数值）；句意为地震学家在震动之后记录到六点二级。图中可辨识物件：记录纸带、曲线笔、值班台、墙上的地震仪。

senses.title: Great size or extent
senses.definition: the great size or extent of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物在体积或范围上的巨大
senses.example: The magnitude of the ice sheet surprised the survey team.
senses.exampleCN: 冰盖的巨大规模让勘测队吃惊。
senses.why: Latin magnitudo named greatness in general, from magnus 'great' plus -tudo, a suffix for a state.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 magnitudo 泛指「大」，由 magnus「大的」加表状态的后缀 -tudo 构成。

senses.title: Importance or seriousness
senses.definition: the importance or seriousness of an event or problem
senses.definitionCN: 事件或问题的重要程度与严重性
senses.example: Few understood the magnitude of the decision at the time.
senses.exampleCN: 当时很少有人明白这个决定有多重要。
senses.why: greatness of size turned into greatness of consequence, so a large event is one of large magnitude.
senses.whyCN: 规模之大转而指后果之大，因此重大的事件就是 magnitude 大的事件。

senses.title: Size of a measured quantity
senses.definition: the size of a quantity expressed as a number
senses.definitionCN: 以数字表示的量的大小
senses.example: The current rises in magnitude as the resistance falls.
senses.exampleCN: 电阻下降时，电流的量值上升。
senses.why: science needed a neutral word for how large a number is, whatever its unit.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要一个中性的词来指数字本身有多大，而不论其单位。

senses.title: Earthquake magnitude
senses.definition: a number on a logarithmic scale that expresses the energy released by an earthquake
senses.definitionCN: 按对数标尺表示地震释放能量的数值
senses.example: The quake reached a magnitude of seven and toppled the old wall.
senses.exampleCN: 地震达到七级，震倒了那道旧墙。
senses.why: the general sense of measured size was fixed to the seismic scale, where each step is a large jump in energy.
senses.whyCN: 「可量的大小」这一泛义被固定到地震标尺上，那里的每一级都代表能量的大幅跃升。

senses.title: Stellar magnitude
senses.definition: a number expressing the brightness of a star, with smaller numbers for brighter stars
senses.definitionCN: 表示恒星亮度的数值，星越亮数值越小
senses.example: The faint star has a magnitude of nine and needs a telescope.
senses.exampleCN: 那颗暗星是九等，需要望远镜才能看到。
senses.why: the ancient star catalogue ranked stars by brightness, and that ranking was later kept as a reversed numerical scale.
senses.whyCN: 古代星表按亮度给星排序，这一排序后来被保留为数值越小越亮的倒序标尺。

senses.title: Length of a vector
senses.definition: the length of a vector, considered apart from its direction
senses.definitionCN: 向量的长度，不考虑其方向
senses.example: The force has a magnitude of twelve newtons and points north.
senses.exampleCN: 这个力的大小是十二牛顿，方向朝北。
senses.why: mathematics separated how much from which way, and called the first part the magnitude.
senses.whyCN: 数学把「多大」与「朝哪」分开，并把前者称作 magnitude。

senses.title: Strength of a sound
senses.definition: the strength of a sound as measured in decibels
senses.definitionCN: 以分贝计量的声音强度
senses.example: The magnitude of the noise made sleep impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 噪声的强度让人无法入睡。
senses.why: acoustics reused the measured-size sense for sound energy, again on a logarithmic scale.
senses.whyCN: 声学把「可量的规模」这一义用于声能，同样落在对数标尺上。

senses.title: Rank of importance
senses.definition: a rank or order of importance, as in a problem of the first magnitude
senses.definitionCN: 重要性的等级，如「头等重要的问题」
senses.example: They treated the leak as an issue of the first magnitude.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把这次泄漏当作头等重要的问题。
senses.why: the star scale supplied a ready idiom in which rank is expressed by magnitude.
senses.whyCN: 星等标尺提供了一个现成的说法，用 magnitude 来表达等级。

intro.en: Magnitude comes from Latin magnitudo 'greatness, size', built on magnus 'great' and the state suffix -tudo. The word entered English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: magnitude 来自拉丁 magnitudo「巨大、规模」，由 magnus「大的」与表状态的后缀 -tudo 构成，经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Magnus meant 'great, large, powerful'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the common link suggested to *meg- 'great' is a reconstructed root, not a proven source.
items.cn: magnus 意为「大的、广阔的、有力的」。其更深来源不确定；常被提到的 *meg-「大」是重构词根，并非已证实的来源。

items.en: Magnus plus -tudo produced magnitudo 'greatness, size, extent', a third-declension noun.
items.cn: magnus 加 -tudo 构成 magnitudo「巨大、规模、范围」，是第三变格法名词。

items.en: Old French magnitude carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, first as a general term for greatness.
items.cn: 古法语 magnitude 在十四世纪把该词带入英语，最初泛指「巨大」。

items.en: From the seventeenth century magnitude was used for the size of a measurable quantity, especially in astronomy.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，magnitude 被用于可测量量的大小，尤其在天文学中。

items.en: The seismological sense dates from the twentieth century, when magnitude was fixed to a logarithmic energy scale.
items.cn: 地震学义始于二十世纪，当时 magnitude 被固定到对数能量标尺上。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): magnus has no established Indo-European ancestor, and any form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：magnus 没有已确定的印欧祖先，凡为其提出的形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin root that look alike but mean different things; group two holds near-meaning size words.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词根、形近而义异的词；第二组是语义相近的「大小」词。

entries.definition: From magnus plus -ficare 'to make': to make something appear larger, not to be large itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由 magnus 加 -ficare「使」构成：使某物看起来更大，而不是自身巨大。

entries.definition: Magnus plus -ficent 'doing': splendid in appearance, close to grand rather than to measurable size.
entries.definitionCN: magnus 加 -ficent「做」：外观壮丽，接近「宏伟」，而非可测的规模。

entries.definition: Magnus plus animus 'mind': great-souled, generous, with nothing to do with physical size.
entries.definitionCN: magnus 加 animus「心」：心胸宏大的、宽厚的，与物理大小无关。

entries.definition: A graded set of numbers for brightness or energy; the compound names the instrument, while magnitude names the number.
entries.definitionCN: 表示亮度或能量的分级数值体系；复合词指这套标尺，而 magnitude 指其中的数值。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for how large a thing is; magnitude is its formal and technical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指物体有多大的日常词；magnitude 是其正式、技术化的对应词。

entries.definition: The degree to which something covers an area or reaches a limit, stressing spread rather than bulk.
entries.definitionCN: 某物覆盖面积或达到界限的程度，强调铺展而非体积。

entries.definition: The level at which something operates, as on a scale from small to large; magnitude is the reading on that scale.
entries.definitionCN: 事物运作的相对层级，如由小到大的标尺；magnitude 是标尺上的读数。

entries.definition: The harshness or seriousness of something bad; it adds the idea of harm that magnitude alone does not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 坏事之严酷或严重；多了「造成伤害」的意思，而 magnitude 本身不含此意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin morphemes and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语素与真实固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: magnus 'great' plus -tudo 'state' gives 'state of being great'.
normal.cn: magnus「大」加 -tudo「状态」即「大的状态」。

normal.en: Order of magnitude marks a jump of about ten times.
normal.cn: 数量级标记约十倍的跃升。

normal.en: Earthquake magnitude and stellar magnitude are both logarithmic scales.
normal.cn: 震级与星等都是对数标尺。

normal.en: Of the first magnitude means of the highest rank.
normal.cn: 头等重要的，即最高等级。

normal.en: The family runs magnitude, magnify, magnificent, magnification, magnanimous.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 magnitude、magnify、magnificent、magnification、magnanimous。

abstract.en: Picture one ruler long enough to measure both a mountain and a quake.
abstract.cn: 想象一把足够长的尺，既能量山，也能量地震。

abstract.en: Picture a star chart where the brightest star is given the smallest number.
abstract.cn: 想象一张星图，最亮的星反倒标着最小的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour that grows until nobody can ignore its size.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻越滚越大，大到没人能忽视。

examples.en: Nobody grasped the magnitude of the loss until the accounts were closed.
examples.cn: 直到账目结清，人们才明白损失有多大。

examples.en: Each step on the magnitude scale means roughly thirty times more energy.
examples.cn: 震级标尺上的每一级大约意味着三十倍的能量。

examples.en: The magnitude of the vector is independent of its direction.
examples.cn: 向量的大小与其方向无关。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「magni（大）+ tude（状态）」——大的状态就是「巨大、规模、量值」

root: 拉丁 magnus「大的」+ -tudo（表状态）→ magnitudo「巨大、规模」，经法语 magnitude 进入英语；magnus 更深来源不确定，*meg- 一说是重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all measure how much: bulk, consequence, number, seismic energy, starlight, vector length, sound and rank.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在量「有多大」：体积、后果、数值、地震能量、星光、向量长度、声音与等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single ruler marked from small to great, laid first against a mountain and then against a quake.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把由小到大的刻度尺，先量山，再量地震。

branches.en: SIZE AND WEIGHT: what is physically large becomes socially serious.
branches.cn: 体积与分量：物理上的大转化为社会意义上的重。

branches.en: NUMBER ON A SCALE: any measured strength can be read as a number.
branches.cn: 标尺上的数：任何可测的强度都能读成一个数。

branches.en: SEISMIC SCALE: the number is fixed to a logarithmic energy ladder.
branches.cn: 地震标尺：这个数被固定到对数能量阶梯上。

branches.en: STELLAR RANK: brightness becomes rank, and rank becomes an idiom.
branches.cn: 星等与等级：亮度变成等级，等级又变成成语。

branches.en: LENGTH ALONE: direction is stripped away, leaving pure size.
branches.cn: 只剩长度：方向被剥离，留下纯然的大小。

intro.en: Magnitude is one Latin root plus one state suffix, and that root also builds several common English words.
intro.cn: magnitude 是一个拉丁词根加一个状态后缀，这个词根还构成若干常用英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnus 'great' gives magnitude, magnify, magnificent and magnanimous; -tudo marks a state or quality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 magnus「大」衍生 magnitude、magnify、magnificent 与 magnanimous；-tudo 标记状态或性质。

items.example: Magnus is the root behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: magnus 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: The suffix turns an adjective into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成表状态的名词。

items.example: The magnitude of the task was clear.
items.exampleCN: 任务的规模很清楚。

items.example: The lens magnifies the print.
items.exampleCN: 镜片把字迹放大。

items.example: The hall was magnificent.
items.exampleCN: 大厅很宏伟。

items.example: The magnificence of the view silenced them.
items.exampleCN: 景色的壮丽让他们说不出话。

items.meaning: the act or degree of enlarging
items.example: The microscope has ten times magnification.
items.exampleCN: 这台显微镜有十倍放大。

items.example: He read the fine print with a magnifier.
items.exampleCN: 他用放大镜读小字。

items.example: She was magnanimous in victory.
items.exampleCN: 她胜而不骄，十分宽厚。

senses.title: The Linnaean system of two-part names
senses.titleCN: 林奈式的两段式命名体系
senses.definition: the biological system in which every species receives a two-part Latin name
senses.definitionCN: 给每个物种一个两段式拉丁学名的生物命名体系
senses.example: Binomial nomenclature replaced long descriptive phrases with stable two-word labels.
senses.exampleCN: 双名命名法用稳定的双词标签取代了冗长的描述性短语。
senses.why: Binomial supplies the two-part frame and nomenclature the whole system; together they name the practice that Linnaeus made standard.
senses.whyCN: binomial 提供「两部分」的框架，nomenclature 提供「整套体系」；合起来就是林奈使之标准化的那套做法。

senses.title: An actual two-part scientific name
senses.titleCN: 一个具体的两段式学名
senses.definition: a particular species name consisting of a genus name and a species epithet
senses.definitionCN: 由属名与种加词构成的某个具体物种名称
senses.example: The binomial nomenclature on the label was Panthera leo.
senses.exampleCN: 标签上的双名学名是 Panthera leo。
senses.why: The phrase can shift from the system to one product of the system, just as a language can mean a sentence in that language.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可以从体系转指体系的一个产物，正如一种语言也可指该语言中的一个句子。

senses.title: The formal code governing names
senses.definition: the set of international rules that determine which two-part name is valid
senses.definitionCN: 决定哪个两段式名称有效的国际规则
senses.example: Binomial nomenclature forbids using the same species epithet for two different genera in one publication.
senses.exampleCN: 双名命名法规禁止在同一出版物中把同一个种加词用于两个不同的属。
senses.why: A naming system needs arbitration; the phrase absorbs the rulebook that settles priority and validity.
senses.whyCN: 命名体系需要仲裁；这个短语也吸收了解决优先权与有效性的那本法规。

senses.title: The Latin-form name on a specimen label
senses.titleCN: 标本标签上的拉丁形式学名
senses.definition: the two-part Latin name printed on a specimen or collection label
senses.definitionCN: 印在标本或藏品标签上的两段式拉丁名称
senses.example: The students copied the binomial nomenclature from the herbarium sheet.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们从腊叶标本纸上抄下双名学名。
senses.why: In the herbarium the system becomes a line of ink on paper, and that line is what the phrase points to.
senses.whyCN: 在标本馆里，体系变成纸上的一行墨迹，而这一行正是短语所指的东西。

senses.title: The naming practice within taxonomy
senses.titleCN: 分类学内部的命名实践
senses.definition: the naming practice that taxonomy performs after a specimen has been identified
senses.definitionCN: 分类学在标本被鉴定之后所执行的命名实践
senses.example: Identification came first; binomial nomenclature followed once the genus was settled.
senses.exampleCN: 先鉴定，属确定之后才进行双名命名。
senses.why: Taxonomy has an order: decide what the thing is, then apply the two-part name according to the code.
senses.whyCN: 分类学有先后：先判断这是什么东西，再按法规给出两段式名称。

senses.title: A standard topic in biology teaching
senses.titleCN: 生物学教学中的标准课题
senses.definition: the curricular topic in which students learn to write and read two-part names
senses.definitionCN: 学生学习书写与认读两段式名称的课程主题
senses.example: Binomial nomenclature is taught alongside cell structure in the first term.
senses.exampleCN: 双名命名法与细胞结构在第一学期同时讲授。
senses.why: A practice that every biologist must use becomes a lesson, and the phrase then names the lesson itself.
senses.whyCN: 每位生物学家都必须使用的做法会成为课程，短语于是也指这门课的内容。

senses.title: A two-part key in collection databases
senses.titleCN: 馆藏数据库中的两段式索引键
senses.definition: the two-part name field used to index specimens and records in a database
senses.definitionCN: 用于索引标本与记录的两段式名称字段
senses.example: The museum stores binomial nomenclature in a single searchable field.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把双名学名存放在一个可检索字段中。
senses.why: Digital collections turn the name into a key, so the phrase also labels the indexing convention.
senses.whyCN: 数字馆藏把名称变成索引键，短语于是也标记这种编目约定。

senses.title: A historical reform of biological naming
senses.titleCN: 生物学命名史上的一次改革
senses.definition: the historical shift from long descriptions to stable two-part names
senses.definitionCN: 从冗长描述转向稳定两段式名称的历史转变
senses.example: Binomial nomenclature made earlier polynomial names obsolete.
senses.exampleCN: 双名命名法使更早的多词名称被淘汰。
senses.why: Before the reform a species could carry a whole sentence of description; the phrase names the reform that ended that.
senses.whyCN: 改革之前，一个物种可能带着一整句描述；这个短语指的就是终结那种做法的改革。

intro.en: Binomial nomenclature joins a Late Latin adjective meaning having two names to a Latin noun meaning a calling of names; the phrase itself is a modern English combination, not a Latin formula.
intro.cn: binomial nomenclature 把晚期拉丁形容词「有两个名字的」与拉丁名词「呼名、名称清单」合在一起；短语本身是现代英语的组合，并非拉丁语原句。

items.en: Binomius, from bini two each and nomen name, described something carrying two names.
items.cn: binomius 由 bini「各两个」与 nomen「名字」构成，描述携带两个名字的事物。

items.en: Nomenclatura, from nomen and calator caller, meant the calling of names and then a list of names.
items.cn: nomenclatura 由 nomen 与 calator「呼名者」构成，先指呼名动作，后指名称清单。

items.en: Linnaeus made the two-part name standard in the eighteenth century, although he did not use the English phrase now attached to it.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪使两段式名称成为标准，尽管他本人并未使用今天附着其上的这个英语短语。

items.en: The English phrase binomial nomenclature spread in the nineteenth century as biology became a taught science with international codes.
items.cn: 随着生物学成为有国际法规的讲授学科，英语短语 binomial nomenclature 在 19 世纪传播开来。

items.en: Modern botanical and zoological codes still regulate the phrase's practice, deciding priority, validity and permissible changes.
items.cn: 现代植物学与动物学法规仍管辖这一实践，决定优先权、有效性与允许的更改。

items.era: UNCERTAIN DETAILS (FIRST DATE AND PHRASE ORIGIN)
items.en: Source uncertain as to the exact first use of the English phrase and the person who coined it; the component roots are clear, but the date is usually given only approximately, and no single originator is documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与短语来源）：英语短语的确切首用与首创者均无定论；各构词成分的词根清楚，但年代通常只给约数，也没有确凿的创制者。

note.en: Group one holds phrases that look similar but name different levels of classification; group two holds neighbouring terms in the vocabulary of biological naming.
note.cn: 第一组是形式相似但指不同分类层级的短语；第二组是生物命名词汇中相邻的术语。

entries.definition: The two-part name produced by the system; it is the product, while binomial nomenclature is the practice or system.
entries.definitionCN: 由该体系产出的两段式名称；它是产物，而 binomial nomenclature 指做法或体系。

entries.definition: The algebraic rewriting of a two-term expression; it shares the adjective but belongs to mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 对含两个项的表达式作代数展开；共享形容词，但属于数学。

entries.definition: Any formal name used in science; only the biological two-part kind falls under binomial nomenclature.
entries.definitionCN: 科学中使用的任何正式名称；只有生物学的两段式名称属于双名命名法。

entries.definition: The ordinary local name of an organism, which is not governed by binomial nomenclature at all.
entries.definitionCN: 生物在日常地方上的俗称，完全不受双名命名法管辖。

entries.definition: The whole science of grouping organisms, within which binomial nomenclature is the naming step.
entries.definitionCN: 对生物分组的整门科学，双名命名法是其中的命名步骤。

entries.definition: Any system of names; the phrase narrows this general word to the biological two-part case.
entries.definitionCN: 任何命名体系；这个短语把该泛称收窄到生物学的两段式情形。

entries.definition: A level such as genus or species; binomial nomenclature uses two of these ranks in one name.
entries.definitionCN: 属、种之类的层级；双名命名法在一个名称中使用其中两个层级。

entries.definition: The physical specimen that anchors a name; the name is binomial nomenclature, the anchor is the type.
entries.definitionCN: 为一个名称提供依据的实物标本；名称属双名命名法，依据则是模式标本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Binomial gives two parts, nomenclature gives the system: two-part naming as a practice.
normal.cn: binomial 给出两部分，nomenclature 给出体系：作为做法的两段式命名。

normal.en: The two parts are genus and species, always written in that order.
normal.cn: 两部分是属名与种名，永远按这个顺序书写。

normal.en: Linnaeus is the name attached to the reform, even though he did not coin the English phrase.
normal.cn: 林奈是与这场改革相连的名字，尽管英语短语并非他创制。

normal.en: International codes decide priority, so the phrase has a legal flavour.
normal.cn: 国际法规决定优先权，因此这个短语带有法律色彩。

normal.en: Herbarium sheets, museum labels and database fields all display the same two-part key.
normal.cn: 腊叶标本纸、博物馆标签与数据库字段都展示同一个两段式索引键。

abstract.en: Picture a plant wearing a two-word nametag at a conference.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物在会议上戴着两个词的胸牌。

abstract.en: Picture a library where every book has a shelf mark and a title joined as one code.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每本书的架号与书名合成一个编码。

abstract.en: Picture a law that begins before the trial and decides what the case may be called.
abstract.cn: 想象一部在审判之前就生效、决定案件可以如何命名的法律。

examples.en: Binomial nomenclature requires italics for the genus and species in print.
examples.cn: 双名命名法要求在印刷时把属名与种名排成斜体。

examples.en: Without binomial nomenclature, a species could carry a phrase as long as a sentence.
examples.cn: 没有双名命名法，一个物种可能带着像句子一样长的名称。

examples.en: The course began with binomial nomenclature and ended with phylogenetics.
examples.cn: 这门课从双名命名法开始，以系统发生学结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「bi 两 + nomen 名字 + calare 呼叫」——用两个名字呼叫每个物种 → 双名命名法

root: 现代英语短语 = 晚期拉丁 binomius「有两个名字的」+ 拉丁 nomenclatura「呼名；名称清单」；两部分词根均清楚，短语首见年代与首创者不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a system to its product, its rulebook, its ink on a label, its place in taxonomy, its classroom form, its database key and its history.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从体系走向产物、法规、标签上的墨迹、分类学中的位置、课堂形态、数据库索引键，最后走向历史。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one specimen, one card, two Latin words that together identify the species.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件标本、一张卡片、两个拉丁词合起来识别这个物种。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND PRODUCT: the practice and the name it produces are two faces of the same phrase.
branches.cn: 体系与产物：做法与它产出的名称是同一短语的两面。

branches.en: CODE: international rules decide which two-part name is valid.
branches.cn: 法规：国际规则决定哪个两段式名称有效。

branches.en: VISIBLE KEY: on paper or in a database, the name becomes a searchable line.
branches.cn: 可见索引：无论在纸上还是数据库里，名称都变成可检索的一行。

branches.en: ORDER OF WORK: identify first, name second, and teach the practice to the next generation.
branches.cn: 工作次序：先鉴定，再命名，并把做法教给下一代。

branches.en: REFORM: the phrase also remembers the change from long descriptions to stable names.
branches.cn: 改革：短语还记住了从冗长描述到稳定名称的转变。

intro.en: The phrase is made of two learned Latin borrowings; pulling them apart shows how biology assembled a modern term from old parts.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个学术拉丁借词构成；把它们拆开，就能看出生物学如何用旧部件组装出一个现代术语。

latinIntro.en: Latin binomius supplies the two-part adjective; Latin nomenclatura supplies the system noun, built on nomen and calator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 binomius 提供「两部分」的形容词；拉丁 nomenclatura 提供「体系」名词，由 nomen 与 calator 构成。

items.example: The prefix fixes the count at two.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把数量固定为二。

items.example: Nomen is the root behind both halves of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: nomen 是短语两部分的共同词根。

items.example: The adjective entered English as binomial.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词以 binomial 进入英语。

items.example: The calling of names is the literal sense.
items.exampleCN: 「把名字叫出来」正是其字面义。

items.meaning: a calling of names; a list of names
items.example: Nomenclatura became English nomenclature.
items.exampleCN: nomenclatura 变成英语 nomenclature。

items.example: Binomial names have two parts.
items.exampleCN: 双名有两个部分。

items.example: Nomenclature follows a code.
items.exampleCN: 命名体系遵循一部法规。

items.example: Nomenclatural rules were cited.
items.exampleCN: 命名规则被引用了。

items.example: The binomial name was written in italics.
items.exampleCN: 双名学名用斜体书写。

latinEntries.meaning: a calling of names; a list

definition_zh: 体温调节；温度调控（把温度维持在所需范围内的过程）
definition_en: the control of temperature within a required range, especially the keeping of body temperature near a set point
core_image: 一只恒温箱与一具身体并排：箱内温度计的指针被按在一格不动，箱外昼夜与四季不断变化
scene: 沙漠里，正午最热时蜥蜴从晒热的石块挪到岩缝的阴影里，把身体贴在凉的一方。 Desert lizards rely on behaviour for temperature regulation when the midday heat peaks.
sceneCN: 这里 temperature regulation 指「靠行为把体温维持在可承受范围」（第 2 个义项：行为性体温调节）；句意为正午最热时，沙漠蜥蜴靠行为进行体温调节。图中可辨识物件：岩缝阴影、抬起的头、晒热的石块、远处沙丘。

pos.zh: 体温调节；温度调控（不可数；指具体机制时可数，复数 temperature regulations）

derivatives.zh: thermo-（希腊 thermē「热」）+ regulation → 以生理手段维持体温的过程
thermoregulation + -ory（形容词后缀）→ 与体温调节有关的
regulate + -or（施动者后缀）→ 执行调节的器件或主体
regulator + -y（形容词后缀）→ 具有调节或监管性质的
regula（拉丁「直尺、规则」）+ -ate → 按规则把某量校准到范围内

senses.title: Physiological control of core temperature
senses.titleCN: 维持核心体温的生理调节
senses.definition: the internal process that keeps an animal's core temperature near a set point whatever the weather does
senses.definitionCN: 无论外界天气如何，把动物核心体温维持在接近设定值的内部过程
senses.example: Sweating and shivering are the two ends of human temperature regulation.
senses.exampleCN: 出汗与发抖是人类体温调节的两个端点。
senses.why: Temperature names a measured degree of heat and regulation names rule-bound correction, so the phrase means holding a degree of heat inside a rule.
senses.whyCN: temperature 指测得的冷热程度，regulation 指按规则校正，因此这个短语就是「把冷热程度守在规则之内」。

senses.title: Behavioural control by moving or posturing
senses.titleCN: 靠移动位置与姿态的行为性调节
senses.definition: the use of shade, sun, posture or grouping rather than internal chemistry to adjust body heat
senses.definitionCN: 不靠体内化学变化，而靠阴影、日照、姿态或结群来调整体温
senses.example: Desert lizards rely on behaviour for temperature regulation when the midday heat peaks.
senses.exampleCN: 正午最热时，沙漠蜥蜴靠行为进行体温调节。
senses.why: Behaviour is the cheapest thermostat: an animal changes where it stands instead of changing how its body burns fuel.
senses.whyCN: 行为是最省力的恒温器：动物改变站位，而不必改变身体燃烧燃料的方式。

senses.title: Control of temperature inside a building or machine
senses.titleCN: 建筑或设备内部的温度控制
senses.definition: the engineering maintenance of a chosen temperature in a room, vehicle or instrument
senses.definitionCN: 在房间、载具或仪器中把温度维持在选定值的技术性工作
senses.example: The server room needs precise temperature regulation to keep the drives from overheating.
senses.exampleCN: 这间服务器机房需要精确控温，以免硬盘过热。
senses.why: The same word moves from bodies to rooms because both are systems that must hold a set value against a changing surroundings.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从身体转到房间，因为两者都是要在变化的环境中守住设定值的系统。

senses.title: Thermal buffering by water, forest or soil
senses.titleCN: 水体、森林或土壤对周边温度的缓冲
senses.definition: the moderating effect a large body of water, woodland or moist soil has on the air around it
senses.definitionCN: 大片水体、林地或湿土对周围空气温度的缓和作用
senses.example: The lake provides temperature regulation for the valley, softening summer heat and winter frost.
senses.exampleCN: 这片湖为山谷起到温度调节作用，缓和了夏热与冬霜。
senses.why: A lake holds heat longer than air does, so it acts like a regulator fitted to the whole valley.
senses.whyCN: 湖水比空气更能存住热量，因此它像装在整个山谷上的一只调节器。

senses.title: A particular mechanism or set of structures
senses.titleCN: 一套具体的调节机制或结构（可数用法）
senses.definition: one identifiable mechanism, organ or reflex that contributes to keeping the body at its set point
senses.definitionCN: 参与把身体维持在设定值的某一可辨识机制、器官或反射
senses.example: Each species has evolved its own temperature regulation, from panting to blubber.
senses.exampleCN: 每个物种都演化出自己的温度调节方式，从喘气散热到皮下脂肪保温。
senses.why: Once the process is treated as a countable thing, the phrase can name one device in the body's control kit.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把这一过程当作可数的物件，这个短语就能指身体调控装备中的某一件。

senses.title: Collective control in a social insect colony
senses.titleCN: 社会性昆虫群体的集体调温
senses.definition: the coordinated fanning, clustering or evaporating by which a colony holds its nest at a steady temperature
senses.definitionCN: 蜂群或蚁群通过扇风、结团或蒸发协调把巢温维持在稳定值
senses.example: Honeybees achieve temperature regulation by fanning the hive in waves.
senses.exampleCN: 蜜蜂靠一波接一波地扇风来实现蜂巢的温度调节。
senses.why: The regulators here are not organs but workers acting together, so the phrase shifts from physiology to collective behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 这里的调节者不是器官，而是共同行动的工蜂，因此这个短语从生理学转到集体行为。

senses.title: Clinical management of a patient's body heat
senses.titleCN: 临床对病人体温的管理
senses.definition: the warming or cooling of a patient by medical staff to keep the body within safe limits
senses.definitionCN: 医护人员对病人加温或降温，使体温保持在安全范围
senses.example: Nurses watched the patient's temperature regulation closely after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术后护士密切观察病人的体温调节情况。
senses.why: Medicine borrows the phrase when the body's own regulation fails and must be managed from outside.
senses.whyCN: 当身体自身的调节失效、必须由外部接管时，医学就借用了这个短语。

senses.title: Holding a fixed temperature in an experiment or facility
senses.titleCN: 实验或养殖场所的恒温控制
senses.definition: the maintenance of a constant temperature in a laboratory, hatchery or greenhouse for the sake of a procedure
senses.definitionCN: 为了某项实验或生产流程，在实验室、孵化场或温室中维持恒定温度
senses.example: The hatchery maintains temperature regulation at a constant level for the eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 孵化场为种蛋把温度调节维持在恒定水平。
senses.why: Here regulation means engineering control only: no organism is adjusting itself, the room is.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 regulation 只指工程控制：调节自身的不是生物，而是房间。

intro.en: Temperature reaches English through French from Latin temperatura 'a tempering, moderation', built on temperare 'to mix in due proportion, regulate'. Regulation comes from Latin regula 'straight stick, rule', a diminutive of regere 'to lead straight'. The two words were joined into an English phrase only in modern technical writing, so the exact first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: temperature 经法语来自拉丁 temperatura「调和、适度」，由 temperare「按比例掺和、调节」构成；regulation 来自拉丁 regula「直尺、规则」，是 regere「引直、统治」的指小形式。两词组合成英语短语只是近代技术文献中的事，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Temperare meant 'to mix in due proportion, to regulate'. It is generally connected with tempus 'time, season', on the idea of the right season or the right blend, but the deeper link is debated.
items.cn: temperare 意为「按适当比例掺和、调节」。一般认为它与 tempus「时间、时节」有关，取「合宜的时节、合宜的配比」之意，但更深层的联系仍有争议。

items.en: The noun temperatura named a tempering or moderation. Its use for a measured degree of heat belongs to later scientific English, not to classical Latin.
items.cn: 名词 temperatura 指「调和、适度」。用它表示测得的冷热程度，是后来科学英语的发展，并非古典拉丁的用法。

items.en: Regula was a straight piece of wood used as a rule; regere meant 'to lead straight, direct, rule'. Both descend from a root meaning 'to move in a straight line'.
items.cn: regula 是取直用的木条，即「尺、规则」；regere 意为「引直、指导、统治」。两者都出自表示「沿直线移动」的词根。

items.en: Temperature and regulation entered English by way of French and Latin in the sixteenth century, regulation first naming the act of making something regular.
items.cn: temperature 与 regulation 在十六世纪经法语和拉丁进入英语，regulation 最初指「使某物变得有规则」这一动作。

items.en: The pairing of a measured quantity with a control term is a modern habit; it settled in physiology and engineering writing in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, though the exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 把测得的量与一个控制词并置，是近代的构词习惯；它在十九至二十世纪的生理学与工程文献中固定下来，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Thermoregulation, built from Greek thermē 'heat', is the learned synonym coined in the twentieth century; the plainer phrase remains common in textbooks.
items.cn: 由希腊 thermē「热」构成的 thermoregulation，是二十世纪新造的书面对应术语；较朴素的短语仍常见于教科书。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same Latin stock that are easily confused; group two holds expressions for controlling heat with a different scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词干、容易混淆的形式；第二组是控制热量但适用范围不同的说法。

entries.definition: The technical synonym: thermo- 'heat' replaces the English noun temperature, but the process named is identical.
entries.definitionCN: 技术性同义词：用 thermo-「热」替换英语名词 temperature，所指过程完全相同。

entries.definition: From temperare plus -atus: 'kept within bounds', hence a mild climate or a restrained person, not a control process.
entries.definitionCN: 由 temperare 加 -atus 构成，意为「被守在限度内」，因此指温和的气候或克制的人，而非调控过程。

entries.definition: From Latin temperamentum 'due mixture': the old idea that a person's character is a blend of humours, not a thermal mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 temperamentum「合宜的混合」：旧说认为人的性情是体液的配比，与热调控机制无关。

entries.definition: The noun alone can name an official rule or the act of controlling; only with temperature does it become a thermal process.
entries.definitionCN: 这个名词单独用时可指正式规章或控制动作；只有与 temperature 连用才成为热学过程。

entries.definition: The everyday engineering phrase for holding a room or device at a chosen temperature; it rarely refers to a living body.
entries.definitionCN: 工程上的日常说法，指把房间或设备维持在选定温度；很少指活体。

entries.definition: Control of temperature together with humidity and air movement, a wider job than temperature alone.
entries.definitionCN: 连同湿度与气流一起控制，范围比单控温度更宽。

entries.definition: The engineering discipline of removing heat from components; it is about carrying heat away, not holding a set point.
entries.definitionCN: 把热量从元件排走的工程领域；重点在于导热出去，而非守住设定值。

entries.definition: The adjective describing structures or behaviours that serve thermoregulation, as in thermoregulatory sweating.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述服务于体温调节的结构或行为，如调节性出汗。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Temperature is a measured degree; regulation is rule-bound correction: a rule for the thermometer.
normal.cn: temperature 是测得的度数，regulation 是按规则校正：给温度计定一条规则。

normal.en: The family runs regulate, regulation, regulator, regulatory, thermoregulation, thermoregulatory.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 regulate、regulation、regulator、regulatory、thermoregulation、thermoregulatory。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: body temperature regulation, behavioural temperature regulation, precise temperature regulation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：体温调节、行为性体温调节、精确控温。

normal.en: Thermo- comes from Greek thermē 'heat', the same element seen in thermometer and thermostat.
normal.cn: thermo- 来自希腊 thermē「热」，同样出现在 thermometer 与 thermostat 中。

normal.en: The phrase splits naturally into a quantity and a control, which is exactly how a thermostat works.
normal.cn: 这个短语天然分成「量」与「控制」两半，恒温器正是这样工作的。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid against a thermometer and a hand pushing the mercury back whenever it climbs.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子贴在温度计上，水银一爬高就有一只手把它按回去。

abstract.en: Picture a lake breathing out cool air over a hot valley every afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象一片湖每天午后向炎热的山谷呼出凉气。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd of bees acting as one slow fan.
abstract.cn: 想象一大群蜜蜂合成一台缓慢转动的风扇。

examples.en: Sweating and shivering are the two ends of human temperature regulation.
examples.cn: 出汗与发抖是人类体温调节的两个端点。

examples.en: The lake provides temperature regulation for the valley, softening summer heat and winter frost.
examples.cn: 这片湖为山谷起到温度调节作用，缓和了夏热与冬霜。

examples.en: The server room needs precise temperature regulation to keep the drives from overheating.
examples.cn: 这间服务器机房需要精确控温，以免硬盘过热。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「温度 + 规章」——给温度定一条规章，不许它跑出范围 → 体温调节、温度调控

root: temperature 经法语来自拉丁 temperatura「调和、适度」，由 temperare「掺和、调节」构成（一般认为与 tempus「时间、时节」有关，更深来源不确定）；regulation 来自拉丁 regula「直尺、规则」，由 regere「引直、统治」加指小后缀构成。英语 temperature regulation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: a set point is held against a changing world. The gesture is first internal and chemical, then behavioural, then collective, then moved outward onto rooms, lakes, patients and hatcheries.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：在变化的世界里守住一个设定值。这个动作先发生在体内与化学层面，再转为行为、集体行为，最后外移到房间、湖泊、病人与孵化场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pointer held at one mark on a dial while the weather outside the box keeps moving.
core.cn: 核心意象：表盘上的指针被按在一格不动，箱外的天气却不断变化。

branches.en: INNER THERMOSTAT: the body senses, corrects and holds its own core value, whether as a process or as one named mechanism.
branches.cn: 体内恒温器：身体自行感知、校正并守住核心值，既可指过程，也可指某一具体机制。

branches.en: MOVING THE BODY: shade, posture and the fanning of a colony do the correcting without inner chemistry.
branches.cn: 挪动身体：阴影、姿态与蜂群扇风，不用体内化学也能完成校正。

branches.en: OUTWARD CONTROL: a room or hatchery is held at a chosen value by equipment, not by a living regulator.
branches.cn: 向外控制：房间或孵化场由设备守住选定值，调节者不是活物。

branches.en: BUFFERING LANDSCAPE: a lake stores heat and slows the swing of the air above it.
branches.cn: 缓冲的景观：湖泊存住热量，使上方气温的摆动变慢。

branches.en: BORROWED CONTROL: when the inner thermostat fails, staff take over the set point.
branches.cn: 借来的控制：体内恒温器失灵时，由医护人员接管设定值。

intro.en: The phrase is made of two Latin-derived nouns, each analysable into a root and a suffix, and each root also builds a family of English words.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁来源的名词构成，每个都可拆成词根与后缀，每个词根又各自衍生出一族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin temperare and its noun temperatura stand behind temperature; Latin regula and regere stand behind regulate and regulation. The Greek element thermo- supplies the technical synonym.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 temperare 及其名词 temperatura 是 temperature 的来源；拉丁 regula 与 regere 是 regulate、regulation 的来源；希腊成分 thermo- 提供技术性同义术语。

items.meaning: a tempering; a measured degree of heat
items.meaningCN: 调和的结果；测得的冷热程度
items.example: The temperature fell below zero before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 黎明前气温降到了零度以下。

items.example: The valve regulates the flow of steam.
items.exampleCN: 阀门调节蒸汽流量。

items.meaning: the act of controlling; an official rule
items.example: New regulations govern the discharge of warm water.
items.exampleCN: 新规章管束温水的排放。

items.example: A pressure regulator sits on the pipe.
items.exampleCN: 管子上装着一只压力调节器。

items.example: The agency has regulatory power over the plant.
items.exampleCN: 该机构对这座工厂拥有监管权。

items.meaning: the body's own control of heat
items.meaningCN: 身体自身对热量的调控
items.example: Thermoregulation fails first in the very old.
items.exampleCN: 高龄者的体温调节最先失灵。

items.example: Panting is a thermoregulatory reflex.
items.exampleCN: 喘气是一种体温调节反射。

items.example: The thermometer read forty degrees at noon.
items.exampleCN: 正午温度计读数为四十度。

items.meaning: a device that holds a set temperature
items.example: The thermostat keeps the room at nineteen degrees.
items.exampleCN: 恒温器把房间保持在十九度。

latinEntries.meaning: to mix in due proportion, regulate

definition_zh: 通气；曝气；充气（使空气或气体进入土壤、液体）
definition_en: the process of exposing something to air or of dissolving a gas into a liquid, so that soil, water or a drink takes in air
core_image: 把空气放进原本闷住的东西里
scene: 草坪踩得发硬，园丁推着带齿的滚筒来回走了一遍。 Aeration lets the roots breathe again.
sceneCN: 这里 aeration 是「通气」（第 1 个义项：让空气进入土壤或水体）；句意为通气让根部重新呼吸。核心画面是把空气放进原本闷住的东西里。

pos.zh: 通气；曝气；充气

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ion 的动词，义为「使通气；充气于」
过去分词作形容词，义为「充了气的；曝气的」
加 -or 构成，义为「曝气器；通气装置」

senses.title: Letting air reach soil or water
senses.definition: the process of making air available to soil, roots or water, so that oxygen can reach them
senses.definitionCN: 让空气进入土壤、根部或水体的过程，使氧气能够抵达
senses.example: Regular aeration prevents the pond from turning stagnant.
senses.exampleCN: 定期曝气可防止池塘变成死水。
senses.why: Aer means air, and the suffix -ation names a process, so aeration is simply the act of putting air where it was missing.
senses.whyCN: aer 意为「空气」，后缀 -ation 表示过程，所以 aeration 就是把空气放到原本缺空气的地方这一动作。

senses.title: Dissolving gas into a drink
senses.definition: the process of charging a liquid with a gas, especially carbon dioxide, to make it fizzy
senses.definitionCN: 把气体（尤指二氧化碳）压入液体使其起泡的过程
senses.example: The aeration of the water gives it a sharp bite.
senses.exampleCN: 水的充气处理让它带上刺激的口感。
senses.why: The same putting-air-in image moves from soil to liquid: here the air is forced in under pressure and stays as bubbles.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「把空气放进去」的意象从土壤移到液体：这里空气在压力下被强行压入，并以气泡形式留下。

intro.en: Aeration is air turned into a process noun: the Greek and Latin word for air plus the suffix that names an action.
intro.cn: aeration 是把「空气」变成过程名词：希腊语与拉丁语的「空气」加上表示动作的后缀。

items.en: Greek aer meant air or mist, and it is the source of the aero- prefix used across science.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气、雾气」，是科学术语中 aero- 前缀的来源。

items.en: Latin borrowed aer with the same meaning, and it declined as aeris, giving the stem aer-.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 aer，意义相同，其属格为 aeris，提供词干 aer-。

items.en: Scholarly Latin aerare meant to expose to the air, built directly on the noun aer.
items.cn: 学术拉丁语 aerare 意为「暴露于空气」，直接建立在名词 aer 上。

items.en: French aération named the process of airing, and English took the word in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 aération 表示透气的过程，英语在十六世纪借入该词。

items.en: English aeration now covers lawn care, sewage treatment and fizzy drinks alike, all sharing one idea of air entering.
items.cn: 现代英语 aeration 同时涵盖草坪养护、污水处理与碳酸饮料，都共享「空气进入」这一想法。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the aero- family; the near-meaning group lists other ways of saying that air or gas is being added.
note.cn: 形近组留在 aero- 词族；近义组列出其他表示「加入空气或气体」的说法。

entries.definition: To expose to air or to charge with gas.
entries.definitionCN: 使通气或充气于。

entries.definition: Existing or happening in the air.
entries.definitionCN: 存在于空气中或在空中发生的。

entries.definition: Exercise that keeps the body supplied with oxygen.
entries.definitionCN: 让身体持续获得氧气的运动。

entries.definition: The movement of fresh air through a space.
entries.definitionCN: 新鲜空气在空间中的流通。

entries.definition: The addition of oxygen to something.
entries.definitionCN: 向某物加入氧气。

entries.definition: The dissolving of carbon dioxide in a drink.
entries.definitionCN: 把二氧化碳溶入饮料。

normalIntro.en: Aeration is aer, air, plus -ation, a process: the process of adding air.
normalIntro.cn: aeration 就是 aer「空气」加 -ation「过程」：加空气的过程。

normal.en: Aerate plus -ion equals aeration, like operate plus -ion gives operation.
normal.cn: aerate 加 -ion 等于 aeration，正如 operate 加 -ion 得到 operation。

normal.en: Aero- always means air: aeroplane, aerosol, aeration all put air first.
normal.cn: aero- 永远表示空气：aeroplane、aerosol、aeration 都把空气放在前面。

normal.en: Think of a lawn spike: each hole is a tiny door for air, and all the holes together are aeration.
normal.cn: 想象草坪打孔器：每个孔都是空气的小门，所有孔合起来就是 aeration。

normal.en: Aerated water is fizzy water; aeration is what made it fizzy.
normal.cn: aerated water 是气泡水；aeration 就是让它起泡的那一步。

normal.en: The word is uncountable in most uses, so say aeration, not an aeration.
normal.cn: 这个词多数用法不可数，所以说 aeration，不说 an aeration。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed jar of soil and a needle that lets the sky in.
abstract.cn: 想象一罐密封的土，和一根让天空进来的针。

abstract.en: Imagine a pond holding its breath until a pump starts stirring.
abstract.cn: 想象一口池塘屏住呼吸，直到水泵开始搅动。

abstract.en: Think of bubbles as small parcels of air delivered into a liquid.
abstract.cn: 把气泡想成送进液体里的一小包空气。

examples.en: Aeration of the compacted soil took the gardener a whole afternoon.
examples.cn: 给板结的土壤通气花了园丁整整一个下午。

examples.en: The treatment plant uses aeration to break down waste.
examples.cn: 处理厂用曝气来分解废物。

examples.en: Gentle aeration improves the texture of the batter.
examples.cn: 轻度充气能改善面糊的质地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱儿瑞神」——爱（ae）儿（ra）瑞（tion）神，把空气这位神请进土里水里，就是通气、曝气。

root: 希腊语 aer「空气」经拉丁语 aer（属格 aeris）进入学术拉丁语 aerare「使暴露于空气」，加过程后缀 -ation 构成 aeration，字面即「空气进入的过程」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one action seen in two places: air is let into soil or water, or pushed into a drink, and the thing that was sealed becomes open.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一动作出现在两处：空气被放进土壤或水体，或被压入饮料，原本闷住的东西变得通畅。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: air put into something that was sealed
core.cn: 核心意象：把空气放进原本闷住的东西

branches.en: Air reaching roots through holes.
branches.cn: 空气经孔洞抵达根部。

branches.en: Air stirred into standing water.
branches.cn: 空气被搅入静止的水体。

branches.en: Gas forced into liquid under pressure.
branches.cn: 气体在压力下压入液体。

branches.en: Both end with something no longer sealed.
branches.cn: 两者都以「不再闷住」收尾。

branches.en: The added gas stays as visible bubbles.
branches.cn: 加入的气体以可见气泡留下。

intro.en: Aeration belongs to the large aero- family, where the root always means air and the suffix decides the part of speech.
intro.cn: aeration 属于庞大的 aero- 词族，词根永远表示空气，后缀决定词性。

latinIntro.en: Greek aer passed through Latin aer and the scholarly verb aerare before English added -ation.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 aer 经拉丁语 aer 与学术动词 aerare，再由英语加上 -ation。

definition_zh: 水生生物（生活在水中，包括淡水与海水中的生物）
definition_en: a living thing that lives in water, whether fresh, brackish or marine
core_image: 池塘边的一只小甲壳类在水草间穿行，鳃片一开一合，从水里取氧
scene: 取样瓶里的一只小甲壳类在淡水与海水混合的水中仍能活动。 Every aquatic organism needs dissolved oxygen to survive.
sceneCN: 这里 aquatic organism 指「生活在水中的生物」（第 1 个义项：涵盖淡水与海水的水生生物总称）；句意为每种水生生物都需要溶解氧才能生存。

pos.zh: 水生生物（可数，复数 aquatic organisms）

derivatives.zh: aqua（拉丁「水」）+ -aticus（形容词后缀）→ 水生的：生长或生活在水中的
aqua（水）+ -arium（场所后缀）→ 水族馆：养水生动植物的场所
aqua（水）+ cultura（栽培、养殖）→ 水产养殖：在水中养殖动植物
organon（希腊「器官」）+ -ismos → 生物体：有组织的活的躯体
aquatic（水生的）+ ecosystem（生态系统）→ 水生生态系统：水环境中的生物群落与环境整体

senses.title: Any water-dwelling organism
senses.titleCN: 水生生物总称：淡咸水皆可
senses.definition: an organism that lives in water of any salinity
senses.definitionCN: 生活在任何盐度水体中的生物
senses.example: Every aquatic organism needs dissolved oxygen to survive.
senses.exampleCN: 每种水生生物都需要溶解氧才能生存。
senses.why: aquatic means 'of water', not 'of the sea', so the phrase is wider than marine organism.
senses.whyCN: aquatic 意为「水的」，不是「海的」，因此这个短语比 marine organism 更宽。

senses.title: A freshwater organism
senses.titleCN: 淡水生物：河流、湖泊与湿地
senses.definition: an organism living in rivers, lakes, ponds or wetlands
senses.definitionCN: 生活在河流、湖泊、池塘或湿地的生物
senses.example: The aquatic organism in this pond never sees salt water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个池塘里的水生生物从未见过咸水。
senses.why: freshwater is the largest non-marine aquatic setting, so the phrase is often used where that contrast matters.
senses.whyCN: 淡水是最大的非海洋水环境，因此这个短语常用于需要这一对照的场合。

senses.title: A marine or brackish organism
senses.titleCN: 海水或半咸水中的水生生物
senses.definition: an organism living in seawater or in mixed estuarine water
senses.definitionCN: 生活在海水或河口混合水中的生物
senses.example: An aquatic organism in the estuary must tolerate changing salt.
senses.exampleCN: 河口的水生生物必须忍受盐度变化。
senses.why: aquatic includes the sea, so the phrase also covers marine and estuarine life when the emphasis is on water rather than ocean.
senses.whyCN: aquatic 包含海洋，因此当强调水而非海洋时，这个短语也涵盖海生与河口生物。

senses.title: A lifestyle category
senses.titleCN: 生活方式类别：漂浮、底栖、游泳
senses.definition: the organism classified by how it occupies the water column or bottom
senses.definitionCN: 按它如何占据水柱或水底来分类的生物
senses.example: An aquatic organism may drift, crawl or swim.
senses.exampleCN: 水生生物可以漂浮、爬行或游泳。
senses.why: water offers distinct zones, so aquatic organisms are often grouped by where and how they move.
senses.whyCN: 水提供不同的区域，因此水生生物常按所在位置与移动方式分组。

senses.title: Respiration and osmoregulation
senses.definition: the organism considered for gills, skin exchange and salt balance
senses.definitionCN: 从鳃、皮肤交换与盐分平衡来考虑的生物
senses.example: An aquatic organism uses gills or skin to take oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 水生生物用鳃或皮肤摄取氧气。
senses.why: water holds far less oxygen than air, so breathing and salt balance are the defining physiological problems.
senses.whyCN: 水中的氧远少于空气，因此呼吸与盐分平衡是决定性的生理难题。

senses.title: A water-quality indicator
senses.definition: the organism used to judge pollution or oxygen conditions
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断污染或溶氧状况的生物
senses.example: A sensitive aquatic organism disappears when the stream is polluted.
senses.exampleCN: 溪流受污染时，敏感的水生生物会消失。
senses.why: organisms tolerate pollution unequally, so their presence becomes a measurement of water quality.
senses.whyCN: 生物对污染的耐受程度不同，因此它们的有无成为水质的量度。

senses.title: A cultured or experimental subject
senses.definition: the organism bred in ponds or kept in tanks for study
senses.definitionCN: 在池塘养殖或在水槽中饲养供研究的生物
senses.example: The hatchery raises an aquatic organism for restocking.
senses.exampleCN: 孵化场养殖一种水生生物用于补充种群。
senses.why: aquaculture and laboratories turn the category into stock and subject, which is how the phrase is used in practice.
senses.whyCN: 水产养殖与实验室把这个类别变成养殖对象与实验对象，这是实际用法。

senses.title: A conservation or invasion unit
senses.titleCN: 保护与入侵语境中的单元
senses.definition: the organism considered as a protected native or a spreading invader
senses.definitionCN: 作为受保护的本土种或扩散中的入侵种来考虑的生物
senses.example: An introduced aquatic organism can crowd out native species.
senses.exampleCN: 引入的水生生物可能排挤本土物种。
senses.why: management works species by species, so the general phrase becomes a unit in protection and invasion policy.
senses.whyCN: 管理按物种逐一进行，因此这个总称成为保护与入侵政策中的单位。

intro.en: Aquatic organism joins a Latin adjective to a Greek-derived noun. Aquatic comes from Latin aqua 'water' through aquaticus, borrowed into English via French aquatique. Organism comes from Greek organon 'organ'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: aquatic organism 把拉丁形容词接在希腊语源名词上。aquatic 经拉丁 aquaticus 来自 aqua「水」，又经法语 aquatique 进入英语。organism 来自希腊 organon「器官」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aqua meant 'water' and supplies aquarium, aqueduct and aquatic.
items.cn: aqua 意为「水」，提供 aquarium、aqueduct 与 aquatic。

items.en: Aquaticus meant 'living or growing in water', formed from aqua with the adjectival ending -aticus.
items.cn: aquaticus 意为「在水中生活或生长的」，由 aqua 加形容词词尾 -aticus 构成。

items.en: French aquatique carried the adjective into English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 aquatique 于十五世纪把这个形容词带入英语。

items.en: Organon meant 'tool, instrument, organ'; organism was formed in English from organ plus -ism.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具、器官」；organism 在英语中由 organ 加 -ism 构成。

items.en: Modern biology and limnology combined the two words to name water-dwelling life without committing to fresh or salt.
items.cn: 近代生物学与湖沼学把两个词组合，命名水生生物而不限定淡水或海水。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the exact phrase is recent and its earliest technical citation varies between references.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：这个确切短语出现较晚，其最早技术书证各家不一。

note.en: Group one holds the phrases most often confused with aquatic organism; group two holds the general habitat words.
note.cn: 第一组是常与 aquatic organism 混淆的短语；第二组是泛指栖息环境的词。

entries.definition: An organism of the sea; it excludes freshwater life, which aquatic organism includes.
entries.definitionCN: 海洋中的生物；不含淡水生物，而 aquatic organism 包含。

entries.definition: A plant living in or on water; it is one kingdom, not all water-dwelling life.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在水里或水面的植物；只是一个界，不是全部水生生物。

entries.definition: An animal living in water; it excludes algae and bacteria, which organism covers.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在水中的动物；不含藻类与细菌，而 organism 涵盖。

entries.definition: The community plus its water environment; one organism is a member, not the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 群落加上水环境；一个生物只是成员，不是整个系统。

entries.definition: Any living body; it needs a qualifier such as aquatic or marine to place it.
entries.definitionCN: 任何活的躯体；需要 aquatic 或 marine 之类限定词来定位。

entries.definition: An organism restricted to fresh water; aquatic organism also covers brackish and marine life.
entries.definitionCN: 局限于淡水的生物；aquatic organism 也涵盖半咸水与海水生物。

entries.definition: The organisms living on or in the bottom; it is one zone, not the whole water column.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在水底或底内的生物；只是一个区域，不是整个水柱。

entries.definition: The drifting organisms of the water column; it excludes swimmers and bottom dwellers.
entries.definitionCN: 水柱中漂移的生物；不含游泳者与底栖者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin root, a real Greek root and real habitat divisions, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的希腊词根与真实的栖息地划分，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: aqua is water, so aquatic covers pond and sea alike.
normal.cn: aqua 是水，因此 aquatic 同时涵盖池塘与海洋。

normal.en: marine is only the salty subset of aquatic, not a synonym.
normal.cn: marine 只是 aquatic 中咸水的那一部分，并非同义词。

normal.en: Three water zones: drifting, bottom, swimming, each with its own organisms.
normal.cn: 三个水区：漂浮、水底、游泳，各有自己的生物。

normal.en: Water holds little oxygen, so gills and skin do the work.
normal.cn: 水中氧少，因此靠鳃与皮肤工作。

normal.en: Sensitive species make living water-quality meters.
normal.cn: 敏感物种就是活的水质测量计。

abstract.en: An aquatic organism is a small private sea kept inside a membrane.
abstract.cn: 水生生物是一小片被膜围起来的私人海。

abstract.en: It breathes a medium that would drown us and calls it home.
abstract.cn: 它呼吸着会淹死我们的介质，并称之为家。

abstract.en: Water is both its weather and its architecture.
abstract.cn: 水既是它的天气，也是它的建筑。

examples.en: The lake survey recorded every aquatic organism in the shallows.
examples.cn: 湖泊调查记录了浅水区的每一种水生生物。

examples.en: An aquatic organism may tolerate both fresh and brackish water.
examples.cn: 一种水生生物可能同时耐受淡水与半咸水。

examples.en: The lab cultures an aquatic organism to test toxicity.
examples.cn: 实验室培养一种水生生物来测试毒性。

dict_mnemonic.text: aquatic（水的）+ organism（生物）＝水生生物；比 marine 更宽，淡水海水都算，靠鳃或皮肤取氧。

root: aquatic（拉丁 aqua「水」→ aquaticus）+ organism（希腊 organon「器官」+ -ismos）；短语为近代生物学所立。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one water-dwelling body: the whole category, freshwater and marine cases, three lifestyles, its breathing and salt balance, its role as an indicator, its cultured form and its place in conservation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿水中一个躯体展开：总类别、淡水与海水情形、三种生活方式、呼吸与盐分平衡、指示作用、养殖形态，以及保护中的地位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small body moving among water plants, taking oxygen through gills.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小躯体在水草间移动，用鳃取氧。

branches.en: ONE CATEGORY, THREE SALINITIES: any water, then fresh, then marine or brackish.
branches.cn: 一个类别，三种盐度：先是任何水，再是淡水，再是海水或半咸水。

branches.en: LIFESTYLES: drifting, bottom-living and swimming divide the water.
branches.cn: 生活方式：漂移、底栖与游泳划分水体。

branches.en: PHYSIOLOGY: oxygen is scarce and salt must be managed.
branches.cn: 生理：氧稀少，盐必须管理。

branches.en: INDICATOR AND STOCK: the organism measures water quality and becomes cultured stock.
branches.cn: 指示与养殖：生物测量水质，也成为养殖对象。

branches.en: POLICY UNIT: native or invader, it is counted one species at a time.
branches.cn: 政策单位：无论本土或入侵，都按物种逐一计数。

intro.en: Aquatic organism joins a Latin-derived adjective to a Greek-derived noun; each half has a productive family in English.
intro.cn: aquatic organism 把拉丁语源形容词与希腊语源名词组合，两半在英语中都有能产词族。

latinIntro.en: Aqua and aquaticus are the Latin entries. Greek organon supplies organism, with no native Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: aqua 与 aquaticus 是拉丁条目。希腊 organon 提供 organism，在拉丁语中没有本土同族词。

items.structure: aqua, aquae (Latin noun, feminine, first declension)
items.example: Aqua is the Latin word for water.
items.exampleCN: aqua 是拉丁语的「水」。

items.example: Aquaticus became English aquatic.
items.exampleCN: aquaticus 变成英语 aquatic。

items.example: Aquatic plants fill the marsh.
items.exampleCN: 水生植物长满沼泽。

items.example: The aquarium holds local aquatic species.
items.exampleCN: 水族馆饲养本地水生种。

items.example: Aquaculture supplies half the seafood eaten.
items.exampleCN: 水产养殖提供所吃海鲜的一半。

items.example: Organon is the root of organism.
items.exampleCN: organon 是 organism 的词根。

items.example: A single organism can change a pond.
items.exampleCN: 一个生物体就能改变一座池塘。

items.example: The pond teems with aquatic organisms.
items.exampleCN: 池塘里满是水生生物。

items.example: Freshwater species cannot cross the strait.
items.exampleCN: 淡水物种无法越过海峡。

items.example: Marine organisms are a subset of aquatic ones.
items.exampleCN: 海洋生物是水生生物的一个子集。

definition_zh: 磨难；严峻考验；痛苦的经历
definition_en: a long and painful experience that tests a person to the edge of what can be borne
core_image: 一个人从没灯的小屋里走出来，脸上还留着里面的黑
scene: 那场手术持续了九个小时，家人守在走廊里，谁都不说话。 The operation lasted nine hours, and the family sat in the corridor without speaking, an ordeal none of them would repeat.
sceneCN: 这里 ordeal 指痛苦的煎熬（第 2 个义项：痛苦的经历）；句意为手术持续九小时，家人守在走廊里沉默不语，那是谁都不愿再经历一次的煎熬。

pos.zh: 磨难；严峻考验；痛苦经历

derivatives.zh: 考验（近义）
艰苦（近义）
痛苦（近义）

senses.title: A severe test
senses.definition: an event that measures how much a person can endure
senses.definitionCN: 检验一个人能承受多少的事件
senses.example: The climb was an ordeal that few finished.
senses.exampleCN: 那次攀登是一场很少有人完成的考验。
senses.why: The word weighs endurance, not difficulty alone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词衡量的是承受力，不只是难度。

senses.title: A painful experience
senses.definition: a stretch of time that hurts and cannot be shortened
senses.definitionCN: 一段疼着又无法缩短的时间
senses.example: The operation lasted nine hours and was an ordeal for the family.
senses.exampleCN: 手术持续九小时，对家人是一场煎熬。
senses.why: Here the pain belongs to those waiting as much as to the patient.
senses.whyCN: 这里的痛苦，等候的人承受得不比病人少。

senses.title: A drawn-out trial
senses.definition: a process so long that the length itself becomes the hardship
senses.definitionCN: 过程长到「长」本身成了苦
senses.example: The appeal dragged on for years, an ordeal of letters and delays.
senses.exampleCN: 上诉拖了多年，成了信件与拖延构成的折磨。
senses.why: Duration is a kind of weight; the word lets time do the pressing.
senses.whyCN: 时长是一种重量；这个词让时间来施压。

senses.title: Trial by ordeal
senses.definition: a historical test in which a person's fate was decided by fire, water or combat
senses.definitionCN: 历史上以火、水或格斗决定命运的裁判方式
senses.example: In the old accounts, the accused walked over hot iron in an ordeal.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧记载里，被控者要在神判中走过烧红的铁。
senses.why: This is the word's legal origin: the body is asked to answer a question for God.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的法律源头：让身体替神回答一个问题。

senses.title: An emotional trial
senses.definition: a period of fear, shame or grief that keeps the mind at full stretch
senses.definitionCN: 恐惧、羞耻或悲伤把心拉满的一段时间
senses.example: Waiting for the verdict was an ordeal of its own.
senses.exampleCN: 等待裁决本身就是一场煎熬。
senses.why: The word does not require a body; the mind can be tested alone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不要求身体在场；心也可以独自受审。

senses.title: A medical trial
senses.definition: the pain and fatigue of treatment rather than of the illness
senses.definitionCN: 来自治疗而非疾病本身的疼痛与疲惫
senses.example: The treatment was an ordeal, and she counted the days.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗是一场折磨，她一天天数着。
senses.why: Modern medicine gives the word a new home, where cure and suffering arrive together.
senses.whyCN: 现代医学给这个词一个新住处：治愈与痛苦一起来。

senses.title: The ordeal of waiting
senses.definition: the special strain of a time in which nothing can be done
senses.definitionCN: 一段什么也做不了的时间特有的紧绷
senses.example: The three days before the result were pure ordeal.
senses.exampleCN: 结果出来前那三天，纯粹是煎熬。
senses.why: Helplessness is the active ingredient; waiting is only its form.
senses.whyCN: 无助才是有效成分；等待只是它的形状。

senses.title: A rite one must pass
senses.definition: a hard passage that marks entry into a group or a new stage
senses.definitionCN: 标示进入某群体或新阶段的艰难通行
senses.example: The first winter served as the young doctor's ordeal.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个冬天成了这位年轻医生的过关磨难。
senses.why: The word can be almost neutral here: the pain is the price of belonging.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词近乎中性：痛苦是归属的价钱。

intro.en: Ordeal began as a word for judgement, then narrowed to one kind of judgement done to the body.
intro.cn: ordeal 起初是「判决」的词，后来收窄为对身体的某一种判决。

items.en: Ordælan meant 'to deal out, to allot', and also 'to judge' a case.
items.cn: ordælan 意为「分派、分配」，也意为「审判」一桩案件。

items.en: Ordæl meant 'a judgement, a verdict, a fate dealt out'.
items.cn: ordæl 意为「判决、裁决、分派给某人的命运」。

items.en: Medieval law used the word for tests by fire or water, which left the verdict to God.
items.cn: 中世纪法律用这个词指火判与水判，把裁决留给神。

items.en: By the seventeenth century any severe trial could be called an ordeal, with no court involved.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，任何严峻考验都可称为 ordeal，与法庭无关。

items.en: Today the word covers illness, waiting, grief and long processes of every kind.
items.cn: 今天这个词涵盖疾病、等待、悲伤与各种漫长的过程。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the ord- sound; the near-meaning group separates testing, suffering and length.
note.cn: 形近组保留 ord- 的读音；近义组把「考验」「受苦」与「漫长」分开。

entries.definition: more than one severe trial.
entries.definitionCN: 不止一场严峻考验。

entries.definition: to appoint or decree formally.
entries.definitionCN: 正式任命或规定。

entries.definition: arrangement or a command.
entries.definitionCN: 次序；命令。

entries.definition: an official rule.
entries.definitionCN: 官方条例。

entries.definition: a test of strength or patience.
entries.definitionCN: 对力量或耐心的检验。

entries.definition: deep trouble and suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 深重的苦难。

entries.definition: lasting difficulty and lack.
entries.definitionCN: 长期的艰难与匮乏。

entries.definition: prolonged, deliberate pain.
entries.definitionCN: 长久而刻意的痛苦。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a dark room one has to walk all the way through.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「必须从头走穿的一间黑屋」的画面。

normal.en: Ordeal comes from an old word for a verdict: a fate dealt out, not chosen.
normal.cn: ordeal 来自一个意为「裁决」的古词：命运是被分派的，不是自己选的。

normal.en: Think of a corridor with no light at either end.
normal.cn: 想象一条两端都没有光的走廊。

normal.en: Or-deal: a bad deal handed to you by the day.
normal.cn: or-deal：日子分给你的一笔坏交易。

normal.en: Say aw-DEEL; the long vowel stretches like the hours inside it.
normal.cn: 读成 aw-DEEL，长元音像里面那些被拉长的小时。

normal.en: Pair it with survive: one survives an ordeal, one does not enjoy it.
normal.cn: 把它和 survive 配对：人熬过 ordeal，而不是享受它。

abstract.en: An ordeal is measured from the inside; from the outside it may look like an ordinary week.
abstract.cn: 磨难度量于内；从外面看，它可能只是一个普通的一周。

abstract.en: The old word for judgement survives in the modern sense: something is still deciding what you are.
abstract.cn: 古老「判决」义活在现代义里：仍有东西在裁定你是什么样的人。

abstract.en: What makes an ordeal is not the event but the absence of any way to hurry it.
abstract.cn: 造成煎熬的不是事件，而是没有任何办法催它快点。

examples.en: The operation lasted nine hours and was an ordeal for the family.
examples.cn: 手术持续九小时，对家人是一场煎熬。

examples.en: The three days before the result were pure ordeal.
examples.cn: 结果出来前那三天，纯粹是煎熬。

examples.en: In the old accounts, the accused walked over hot iron in an ordeal.
examples.cn: 在旧记载里，被控者要在神判中走过烧红的铁。

dict_mnemonic.text: or（古英语「裁决」）+ deal（分派）：命运分派给你的一份苦，就是「磨难」。

root: 古英语 ordǣl（判决、命运），源自动词 ordǣlan（分派、审判）

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses run from a court of God to a hospital corridor: a test, a pain, a length, a fire, a fear, a cure, a wait and a passage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从神的法庭一路走到医院走廊：考验、疼痛、漫长、火、恐惧、治疗、等待与过关。

core.en: THE DARK ROOM ONE MUST WALK THROUGH
core.cn: 必须走穿的那间黑屋

branches.en: A test of endurance and a fear that tests without a body.
branches.cn: 对承受力的考验，以及无需身体在场的恐惧考验。

branches.en: Pain endured and pain given by treatment.
branches.cn: 承受的痛苦与治疗带来的痛苦。

branches.en: Length as weight, and waiting as the purest form of it.
branches.cn: 以长为重，以及作为其最纯粹形态的等待。

branches.en: The historical judgement left to fire and water.
branches.cn: 留给火与水的历史裁决。

branches.en: A hard passage that admits a person into something.
branches.cn: 把人送入某处的艰难通行。

intro.en: The ord- family is about ordering and allotting: order arranges, ordain appoints, ordeal hands out a fate.
intro.cn: ord- 词族关乎排序与分派：order 安排，ordain 任命，ordeal 分派命运。

latinIntro.en: English kept its own word here; the Latin entries below are the neighbouring vocabulary of lot and judgement, not the source.
latinIntro.cn: 这里英语保留了自己的词；下面这些拉丁条目是「命运」与「审判」的邻近词汇，而不是它的来源。

items.example: The ordeal lasted days.
items.exampleCN: 这场磨难持续了数日。

items.example: He spoke of his ordeals.
items.exampleCN: 他谈起自己的磨难。

items.example: The church ordained him.
items.exampleCN: 教会任命了他。

items.example: Keep the files in order.
items.exampleCN: 把文件按顺序放好。

items.example: The city passed an ordinance.
items.exampleCN: 市里通过了一条条例。

items.example: An ordinary morning.
items.exampleCN: 一个平常的早晨。

items.example: The room was in disorder.
items.exampleCN: 房间一片混乱。

items.example: An inordinate delay.
items.exampleCN: 过度的拖延。
