definition_zh: 证实；佐证；以证据支持（说法、理论、证词）
definition_en: to strengthen a statement or a finding by adding independent evidence
core_image: 一根细木柱旁再立一根粗橡木，两根顶住同一块石板，石板便不再晃动
scene: 两名独立目击者的记录摆上桌面，关键时间点彼此吻合。 Two independent records corroborate the driver's account of the accident.
sceneCN: 这里指用独立材料支持某项陈述（第 1 个义项：以独立证据证实某个说法）；句意：两份独立记录证实了司机对这起事故的陈述。

pos.zh: 证实；佐证；支持

derivatives.zh: 证实；佐证
佐证性的
起证实作用的（罕用）
提供佐证者

senses.title: To confirm a statement with other evidence
senses.definition: to support a person's account by producing evidence that did not come from that person
senses.definitionCN: 用并非出自陈述者之手的证据来支持其说法
senses.example: Two independent records corroborate the driver's account of the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 两份独立记录证实了司机对这起事故的陈述。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to strengthen, and a statement is strengthened when something outside it holds it up.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为使强壮，当陈述之外的东西把它撑住，它就被加强了。

senses.title: To support a theory with further evidence
senses.definition: to give a hypothesis additional support from data or experiment
senses.definitionCN: 用数据或实验为假说提供额外支持
senses.example: Later observations corroborated the model's prediction.
senses.exampleCN: 后来的观测印证了该模型的预测。
senses.why: A theory is a load-bearing claim, so evidence that holds it up is pictured as physical support.
senses.whyCN: 理论是一项承重的断言，因此支撑它的证据被想象成物理支撑。

senses.title: To strengthen physically (old sense)
senses.titleCN: 使身体或结构变强壮（古义）
senses.definition: in older usage, to make a body or a structure stronger
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，指使身体或结构更强壮
senses.example: The old tonic was said to corroborate the constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的补药据说能强健体质。
senses.why: The literal sense survives from Latin, where the root named strength itself, and medicine kept it longest.
senses.whyCN: 字面义来自拉丁语，那里的词根就指力量，医学把它保留得最久。

senses.title: To back a witness's testimony in law
senses.definition: in law, to support a witness's testimony with independent proof so that it can be relied on
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上以独立证明支持证人证词，使其可以采信
senses.example: The passport record corroborates her account of the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 护照记录印证了她对那次行程的叙述。
senses.why: Courts distrust a single voice, so a second source that supports it has a fixed name and a fixed role.
senses.whyCN: 法庭不相信孤立的一家之言，因此支持它的第二个来源有固定名称与固定作用。

senses.title: To confirm a result by replication
senses.definition: to confirm a result by obtaining it again independently
senses.definitionCN: 通过独立地再次得到同一结果来证实它
senses.example: Three laboratories corroborated the original finding.
senses.exampleCN: 三家实验室证实了最初的结果。
senses.why: Replication is the modern form of adding a second pillar under a slab.
senses.whyCN: 重复实验就是给石板再加一根支柱的现代形式。

senses.title: To back a rumour or suspicion with facts
senses.titleCN: 用事实支撑传闻或怀疑
senses.definition: to give a rumour enough factual support that it can no longer be dismissed
senses.definitionCN: 给传闻足够的真实依据，使其不再能被轻易否定
senses.example: Phone records corroborated the suspicion that had circulated for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 通话记录支持了流传数周的怀疑。
senses.why: The verb is neutral about the claim's truth; it reports that the support is there.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词对说法是否真实保持中立，只报告支撑确实存在。

senses.title: To support someone's version of events
senses.titleCN: 支持某人对事件的叙述
senses.definition: to confirm the particular version of events that one person has given
senses.definitionCN: 确认某个人所给出的那一版事件经过
senses.example: Two neighbours corroborated his version of the night.
senses.exampleCN: 两位邻居印证了他对那一夜的叙述。
senses.why: The object is a person's version rather than a fact, which is why the verb so often takes an account as its object.
senses.whyCN: 宾语是某人的版本而不是一个事实，因此这个动词常以叙述为宾语。

senses.title: Of a detail that fits and strengthens
senses.definition: of a small detail, to fit the rest of the picture so well that it strengthens the whole
senses.definitionCN: 指某个小细节与整体情况吻合得足以加强整体
senses.example: The date on the ticket corroborates the story in one small point.
senses.exampleCN: 票上的日期在一个小点上印证了那套说法。
senses.why: A single detail can act as a second pillar if it is independent and precise.
senses.whyCN: 只要独立而精确，一个细节也能充当第二根支柱。

intro.en: Corroborate comes from a Latin verb meaning to strengthen, built on the Latin word for oak and for strength. English took it in the sixteenth century, and law and science later specialized its use.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个表示使强壮的拉丁动词，其词根指橡木，也指力量。英语在十六世纪借入，法律与科学后来把它的用法专门化。

items.en: Robur meant oak and, by extension, strength or the strongest part of anything.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词指橡木，引申指力量，或任何事物最坚固的部分。

items.en: The prefix com- added intensity, so the compound meant to strengthen thoroughly.
items.cn: 前缀加强语气，因此复合词意为彻底使强壮。

items.en: The Latin verb meant to give strength, and it could be used of bodies, buildings and arguments alike.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为给予力量，既可用于身体与建筑，也可用于论证。

items.en: English borrowed it in the sixteenth century, when strengthening a claim with proof was already a courtroom habit.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，当时用证据加固说法已是法庭习惯。

items.en: Testimony, then experiment, gave the word its two technical homes.
items.cn: 先是证词，后是实验，给了这个词两个技术归宿。

items.en: Replication turned the old image of a second pillar into the standard test of a finding.
items.cn: 重复实验把「第二根支柱」的古老意象变成检验研究结果的标准做法。

note.en: The first group shares the oak-and-strength root or looks close to it; the second group names nearby kinds of proof. Corroborate adds independent support, whereas correlate only reports that two things vary together, and a correlation by itself proves nothing about cause.
note.cn: 第一组共享橡木与力量的词根或字形相近；第二组是相邻的证明方式。本词指加上独立支撑，而相关类词只报告两事物共同变化，单靠相关并不能证明因果。

entries.definition: The independent support that makes a claim hold.
entries.definitionCN: 使说法立得住的独立支撑。

entries.definition: Serving as such support, as in corroborative detail.
entries.definitionCN: 起这种支撑作用的，如佐证性的细节。

entries.definition: Strong and hard to break; it describes the object, not the proof.
entries.definitionCN: 强壮而不易损坏；描述对象本身，而非证明。

entries.definition: The person or source that supplies the support.
entries.definitionCN: 提供支撑的人或来源。

entries.definition: To make a claim certain; it reports the result, while this word reports the added support.
entries.definitionCN: 使说法确定；报告结果，而本词报告外加的支撑。

entries.definition: To check that something is true; the checking is the point, not the added strength.
entries.definitionCN: 核查某事是否属实；重点在核查，而非加固。

entries.definition: To give a claim enough substance to stand; it stresses material rather than a second pillar.
entries.definitionCN: 给说法足够的实质使其站住；强调实质，而非第二根支柱。

entries.definition: To hold something up generally; it is the wider word behind the technical one.
entries.definitionCN: 一般性地撑住某物；是技术词背后更宽泛的说法。

entries.definition: To establish that something is sound or acceptable, often by a formal procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 确认某物可靠或可接受，常通过正式程序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the oak-and-strength root, the real family and the legal phrases that fix the word's role.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用橡木与力量的词根、真实同族词，以及固定其作用的法律搭配。

normal.en: The root names oak, the hardest wood, so the verb means to give a claim the strength of oak.
normal.cn: 词根指橡木这种最硬的木材，因此动词意为给说法以橡木般的力量。

normal.en: The family runs corroboration, corroborative, corroborator and the related adjective robust.
normal.cn: 同族词有佐证、佐证性的、提供佐证者，以及同根的「强壮」形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: corroborate a story, corroborate testimony, corroborating evidence.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：证实说法、印证证词、佐证材料。

normal.en: The courtroom is its oldest home: a second source under a single voice.
normal.cn: 法庭是它最早的主场：给孤证再加一个来源。

normal.en: Replication is its laboratory form: the same result found again elsewhere.
normal.cn: 重复实验是它的实验室形态：别处再次得到同一结果。

abstract.en: Picture a leaning wall held up by a second beam placed beside the first.
abstract.cn: 想象一面将倒的墙，被并与第一根梁的第二根梁撑住。

abstract.en: Picture two witnesses who never met telling the same small detail.
abstract.cn: 想象两个从未见面的证人说出同一个细节。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge cable that only holds when a second cable takes the strain.
abstract.cn: 想象一根桥索只有在第二根分担拉力时才撑得住。

examples.en: The letters corroborate her account of the escape.
examples.cn: 这些信件印证了她对那次出逃的叙述。

examples.en: No independent source corroborates the claim.
examples.cn: 没有独立来源能佐证这一说法。

examples.en: Two experiments corroborated the earlier result.
examples.cn: 两项实验证实了早先的结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可」加「若伯」——再立一根橡木柱子顶住，说法就稳了：证实、佐证

root: 拉丁语「橡木、力量」一词加加强前缀构成「使强壮」，十六世纪进入英语；先用于证词，后用于实验与证据。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all add a second support: a statement, a theory, an old body, a witness, a replicated result, a rumour, a personal version and a single detail.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在加第二重支撑：说法、理论、旧时的身体、证人、被重复的结果、传闻、个人叙述与单个细节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second pillar of hard oak placed beside the first under one stone slab, and the slab stops shaking.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细木柱旁再立一根粗橡木，两根顶住同一块石板，石板便不再晃动。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNT: a statement or a person's version held up from outside.
branches.cn: 叙述：一个说法或某人的版本由外部撑住。

branches.en: THE THEORY: a hypothesis supported, and a result found again elsewhere.
branches.cn: 理论：假说得到支持，结果在别处再次得到。

branches.en: THE OLD BODY: the literal sense of making a constitution stronger.
branches.cn: 旧时的身体：使体质变强的字面义。

branches.en: THE COURT: a single voice given a second independent source.
branches.cn: 法庭：孤立的一家之言得到第二个独立来源。

branches.en: THE SMALL SUPPORT: a rumour backed by facts, or one precise detail that fits.
branches.cn: 细小支撑：传闻得到事实支持，或一个精确吻合的细节。

intro.en: Corroborate is a Latin verb of strength, and its family supplies the noun of support, the adjective of supporting detail and the related adjective for sheer toughness.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示力量的拉丁动词，其词族提供表示支撑的名词、描述佐证细节的形容词，以及描述单纯坚固的同根形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin robur and the intensive prefix are the two pieces of the verb; the English endings are added on top.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示橡木与力量的词，加上加强前缀，构成这个动词的两个构件，英语词尾再加在外面。

items.example: It makes the strengthening thorough.
items.exampleCN: 它使「加强」变得彻底。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of hardness.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供坚硬之意。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: It gives the Latin stem an English verb shape.
items.exampleCN: 它给拉丁词干披上英语动词外形。

items.example: It builds the name of the added support.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示外加支撑的名词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for evidence that supports.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述支持性证据的形容词。

items.example: It builds a rare adjective of the same kind.
items.exampleCN: 它构成同类的罕见形容词。

items.example: It builds the name of the supporting source.
items.exampleCN: 它构成提供支撑者的名称。

items.example: The verb almost always works on proof or on a statement.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词几乎总是作用于证明或说法。

definition_zh: 研究电与电磁现象，并设计发电、输电、配电及各类电气设备的工程学科
definition_en: the branch of engineering that studies electricity and electromagnetism and designs power systems, machines and electrical equipment
core_image: 变电站里，母线、开关柜与电缆连成一条供电通路，电流从发电机一端送到用户一端
scene: 变电站控制室里，值班工程师核对线路负荷后合上开关，让电流送入城区电网。 The electrical engineering team redesigned the substation relay.
sceneCN: 这里指负责电力与电气设备设计的工程学科及其团队（第 1 个义项：研究电与电磁现象并设计电力与电气设备的工程学科）；句意：电气工程团队重新设计了变电站的继电器。

pos.zh: 电气工程；电气工程学

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语「琥珀」经新拉丁语形容词进入英语，义为「电的」
由「电的」加表示性质的名词词尾构成，义为「电、电学」
由「电的」加表示从业者的词尾构成，义为「电工」
由「电的」加表示「使成为」的动词词尾构成，义为「使带电、使电气化」
由拉丁语「天赋、巧思」经法语进入英语，义为「工程师」
由「工程师」加表示活动的词尾构成，义为「工程、工程学」
由「电子」加形容词词尾构成，义为「电子的」

senses.title: The discipline itself
senses.definition: the branch of engineering concerned with the study and application of electricity, electromagnetism and electrical devices
senses.definitionCN: 研究并应用电、电磁现象与电气设备的工程分支
senses.example: She chose electrical engineering because she wanted to design power systems.
senses.exampleCN: 她选择电气工程，是因为她想设计电力系统。
senses.why: Electrical marks the force, engineering marks the organised profession, so the phrase names the whole discipline.
senses.whyCN: 「电气的」标出所研究的力，「工程」标出有组织的专业，因此这个词组命名了整个学科。

senses.title: Generation, transmission and distribution
senses.definition: the design and operation of the networks that produce and deliver electric power
senses.definitionCN: 生产并输送电力的网络之设计与运行
senses.example: Electrical engineering keeps the national grid balanced minute by minute.
senses.exampleCN: 电气工程让全国电网逐分钟保持平衡。
senses.why: The largest application of the discipline is the power network, so the phrase often means that network's engineering.
senses.whyCN: 该学科最大的应用是电力网络，因此这个词组常指这张网络的工程。

senses.title: Design of building services
senses.definition: the design of wiring, lighting, sockets and protective systems inside buildings
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物内布线、照明、插座与保护系统的设计
senses.example: Electrical engineering covers the lighting and wiring of the new library.
senses.exampleCN: 电气工程涵盖新图书馆的照明与布线。
senses.why: Every building needs a safe electric path, so the discipline extends from power stations into rooms.
senses.whyCN: 每栋建筑都需要安全的电路，因此该学科从电站延伸到房间。

senses.title: Electric machines and drives
senses.definition: the study and design of motors, generators and the drives that control them
senses.definitionCN: 电动机、发电机及控制它们的驱动装置的研究与设计
senses.example: Electrical engineering made the factory motor quieter and more efficient.
senses.exampleCN: 电气工程让工厂电机更安静、更高效。
senses.why: Machines that convert electricity and motion are a core object of the discipline.
senses.whyCN: 在电与运动之间转换的机器是该学科的核心对象。

senses.title: Protection, earthing and safety
senses.definition: the design of relays, fuses, breakers and earthing so that faults do not spread
senses.definitionCN: 设计继电器、熔断器、断路器与接地，使故障不致扩散
senses.example: Electrical engineering specifies the breaker size and the earthing route.
senses.exampleCN: 电气工程规定断路器规格与接地路径。
senses.why: Power is dangerous when it escapes, so the discipline includes the devices that stop it.
senses.whyCN: 电一旦失控便危险，因此该学科包含阻止它外泄的装置。

senses.title: A degree programme
senses.definition: the university course of study that trains students in the discipline
senses.definitionCN: 在大学里培养该学科学生的课程体系
senses.example: He finished electrical engineering in four years and then joined a utility.
senses.exampleCN: 他用四年读完电气工程，随后进入一家电力公司。
senses.why: A discipline becomes a named programme, so the phrase also labels the degree.
senses.whyCN: 学科会成为命名的课程，因此这个词组也指学位。

senses.title: Site practice and commissioning
senses.definition: the practical work of installing, testing and switching on electrical plant
senses.definitionCN: 安装、试验并给电气设备送电的现场工作
senses.example: Electrical engineering on site means checking every cable before energising.
senses.exampleCN: 现场的电气工程意味着在送电前检查每根电缆。
senses.why: Designs must be carried out in the field, and that field work keeps the discipline's name.
senses.whyCN: 设计必须在现场落实，而这种现场工作仍沿用学科之名。

senses.title: Codes and standards
senses.definition: the body of rules that fixes how electrical work must be designed and inspected
senses.definitionCN: 规定电气工作如何设计与验收的规则体系
senses.example: Electrical engineering students must learn the local wiring code.
senses.exampleCN: 电气工程学生必须学习当地的布线规范。
senses.why: Safety is written into rules, so the discipline is also the standard it enforces.
senses.whyCN: 安全被写进规则，因此该学科也是它所执行的规范。

intro.en: Electrical engineering pairs an adjective from the Greek word for amber with a noun from Latin ingenium, the root of engineer; the pairing names a profession built on the behaviour of charge.
intro.cn: 「电气工程」把一个源自希腊语「琥珀」的形容词，与一个源自拉丁语「天赋、巧思」的名词配对；后者正是「工程师」的词根，整个词组命名了一门以电荷行为为基础的专业。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, the resin that attracts light objects when rubbed; this Greek word is the direct source, while its earlier root is uncertain and the link to a word for the beaming sun remains a suggested reconstruction.
items.cn: 这个希腊语名词指琥珀，即摩擦后能吸引轻小物体的树脂；它是本词的直接来源，其更早词根存疑，与表示「闪耀太阳」之词的关联只是重构性推测。

items.en: Latin electrum named amber and also a pale gold alloy, keeping the Greek word alive in learned writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语用这个词既指琥珀，也指一种淡金色合金，使这个希腊词在学术写作中存续。

items.en: Sixteenth-century scholars coined electricus for the amber effect, and English electric followed in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十六世纪学者为琥珀的吸引现象造出「电的」这一新拉丁语形容词，英语随后在十七世纪出现「电的」。

items.en: The adjective gained a fuller ending in the nineteenth century, when electricity became an industry rather than a curiosity.
items.cn: 十九世纪，当电从奇观变成工业时，这个形容词获得了更完整的词尾。

items.en: Ingenium meant natural ability or cleverness; French turned it into engin, a clever device, and English engineer named the person who built such devices.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语名词指天赋或巧思；法语把它变成指精巧装置的名词，英语的「工程师」则指建造这类装置的人。

items.era: MODERN PROFESSIONAL PAIRING · FIRST RECORD DATE UNCERTAIN
items.en: In the nineteenth century the two words were joined to name the branch that designs power networks and electrical machines; the exact year of first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 十九世纪，这两个词被组合起来，用以命名设计电力网络与电机的工程分支；具体首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the amber root; the second group names neighbouring engineering branches.
note.cn: 第一组共享「琥珀」词根；第二组是相邻的工程分支。

entries.definition: Driven by electricity; the shorter adjective often describes a single device.
entries.definitionCN: 由电驱动的；较短的形式常描述单台设备。

entries.definition: Working through electrons in circuits rather than through heavy current.
entries.definitionCN: 靠电路中电子运作，而非大电流。

entries.definition: A tradesperson who installs and repairs wiring; not the designer.
entries.definitionCN: 安装与维修线路的技术工人；不是设计者。

entries.definition: The physical phenomenon itself rather than the profession.
entries.definitionCN: 电这一物理现象本身，而非专业。

entries.definition: The part of the field that deals with large-scale generation and grids; narrower than the target.
entries.definitionCN: 该领域中处理大规模发电与电网的部分；比目标词窄。

entries.definition: The branch built on small signals and semiconductor devices rather than heavy current.
entries.definitionCN: 以弱信号与半导体器件而非大电流为基础的分支。

entries.definition: The act of bringing electricity to a place or process, not the discipline that plans it.
entries.definitionCN: 把电引入某地或某过程的行为，而非规划它的学科。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real fixed terms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The first half goes back to amber rubbed with cloth, the first known electric effect.
normal.cn: 前半可追到用布摩擦琥珀，那是已知最早的电现象。

normal.en: The second half goes back to ingenium, cleverness, the root of engineer.
normal.cn: 后半可追到表示巧思的拉丁词，它是「工程师」的词根。

normal.en: The family runs electric, electricity, electrician, electrify, electronic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括电的、电、电工、使带电、电子的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: electrical engineering department, electrical engineering practice.
normal.cn: 固定搭配可标记它：电气工程系、电气工程实务。

normal.en: Power stations, substations and wiring codes are its three familiar homes.
normal.cn: 电站、变电站与布线规范是它三个熟悉的场所。

abstract.en: Picture a river of charge that must be dammed, channelled and switched.
abstract.cn: 想象一条电荷之河，必须被筑坝、引流与开关。

abstract.en: Picture a city whose nerves are copper cables running under every street.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市，神经是每条街下的铜缆。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that never touches the wire yet decides where it goes.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从不碰电线，却决定电线的走向。

examples.en: Electrical engineering turned the waterfall into a steady supply for the town.
examples.cn: 电气工程把瀑布变成了小镇的稳定电源。

examples.en: The electrical engineering course begins with circuits and ends with grid control.
examples.cn: 这门电气工程课程从电路开始，到电网控制结束。

examples.en: She works in electrical engineering, checking relays before every storm season.
examples.cn: 她从事电气工程，在每个风暴季前检查继电器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「琥珀」引来电流，「巧思」造出工程——电与匠心的组合

root: 形容词一半源自希腊语「琥珀」，名词一半源自拉丁语「巧思」并经法语成为「工程师」；琥珀一词更早的来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one path: charge is generated, moved, protected and finally written into rules. The same phrase covers the theory, the grid, the building, the machine and the code book.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条路径展开：电被发出、被输送、被保护，最后被写成规则。同一个词组覆盖理论、电网、建筑、机器与规范手册。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a current entering at one end of a network and leaving at the other, with every joint designed and every fault guarded.
core.cn: 核心意象：电流从网络一端进入、从另一端输出，每个接点都经过设计，每处故障都有防护。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE AND ITS LARGEST OBJECT: the study of charge, and the generation and delivery network.
branches.cn: 学科与其最大对象：对电荷的研究，以及发电与输送网络。

branches.en: THE BUILDING VERSION: wiring, lighting and sockets inside a structure.
branches.cn: 建筑版本：建筑物内的布线、照明与插座。

branches.en: THE MACHINE VERSION: motors and generators converting between current and motion.
branches.cn: 机器版本：在电流与运动之间转换的电动机与发电机。

branches.en: THE GUARD VERSION: relays, breakers and earthing that stop a fault spreading.
branches.cn: 防护版本：阻止故障扩散的继电器、断路器与接地。

branches.en: THE PROFESSIONAL WRAPPER: the degree, the site work and the written standards.
branches.cn: 职业外壳：学位、现场工作与成文规范。

intro.en: The phrase is half Greek and half Latin: amber for the force, cleverness for the profession.
intro.cn: 这个词组一半希腊、一半拉丁：用「琥珀」指电，用「巧思」指专业。

intro.en: Disarmament adds dis- and -ment to armament, from Latin armamenta, equipment, from arma, weapons.
intro.cn: disarmament 是在 armament 上加 dis- 与 -ment；armament 来自拉丁语 armamenta（装备），armamenta 又来自 arma（武器）。

items.en: Arma meant weapons.
items.cn: arma 意为武器。

items.en: Armamenta named equipment and tackle.
items.cn: armamenta 指装备与索具。

items.en: English armament meant a force of weapons.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语 armament 指武装力量。

items.en: Disarm reversed the equipping.
items.cn: 十七世纪 disarm 反转了「装备」这件事。

items.en: Disarmament named the undoing of armament.
items.cn: 十九世纪 disarmament 指军备的撤销。

items.en: It became the name of arms-control policy.
items.cn: 二十世纪它成为军控政策的名称。

normal.en: Armament builds up, disarmament takes down.

normal.en: Nuclear disarmament is the common phrase.

normal.en: Arms control limits; disarmament removes.

senses.title: A collection treated as one unit
senses.titleCN: 作为一个整体处理的数据集合
senses.definition: related records grouped together so that they can be handled, moved or described as one thing
senses.definitionCN: 把相关记录归在一起，以便作为一件东西处理、搬运或描述
senses.example: The dataset holds ten years of rainfall for one valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这份数据集收录了某个山谷十年的降雨记录。
senses.why: data plus set: a set is a group counted as one, so the compound's core sense is data handled as a single unit.
senses.whyCN: data 加 set：集合是被当作一个来数的组，因此核心义是被当成一个单位处理的数据。

senses.title: The unit fed to a model
senses.definition: the body of examples used to train or evaluate a machine-learning model
senses.definitionCN: 用于训练或评估机器学习模型的样本总体
senses.example: The model saw only a small dataset before it was tested.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型在测试前只见过一份小数据集。
senses.why: machine learning needs a fixed body of examples per run, and that body is naturally named with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 机器学习每次运行需要一份固定的样本总体，这份总体自然沿用同一个词。

senses.title: A benchmark for comparison
senses.definition: a standard collection on which competing methods are scored so that results can be compared
senses.definitionCN: 让不同方法在同一批数据上打分、从而可比结果的标准化集合
senses.example: Every team reported accuracy on the same benchmark dataset.
senses.exampleCN: 每个团队都在同一个基准数据集上报告准确率。
senses.why: fair comparison requires a shared collection, and that shared collection becomes a named dataset.
senses.whyCN: 公平比较需要共享的集合，这份共享集合就成了具名的数据集。

senses.title: Observations from a study
senses.definition: the records collected in a survey, experiment or field study
senses.definitionCN: 在调查、实验或实地研究中收集的记录
senses.example: The survey dataset covers four thousand households.
senses.exampleCN: 这份调查数据集覆盖四千个家庭。
senses.why: statistics has long spoken of a data set as the observations gathered for one analysis, independent of computers.
senses.whyCN: 统计学早就把为一次分析收集的观测称为数据集，这与计算机无关。

senses.title: A published, reusable collection
senses.titleCN: 公开发布可复用的集合
senses.definition: a collection released with documentation so that others can reuse it
senses.definitionCN: 连同说明文档一起发布、供他人复用的集合
senses.example: The open dataset has a licence and a version number.
senses.exampleCN: 这份开放数据集有许可证和版本号。
senses.why: shared research made the collection itself a citable object, so the word now names a published artifact.
senses.whyCN: 共享研究使集合本身成为可引用的成果，因此这个词也指公开发布的产物。

senses.title: One split of a larger collection
senses.definition: one of the parts into which data are divided, such as a training or test portion
senses.definitionCN: 数据被分成的某一份，如训练部分或测试部分
senses.example: The validation dataset was kept apart until the final week.
senses.exampleCN: 验证数据集一直单独留到最后一周。
senses.why: when one collection is split, each part is still called a dataset, with an adjective naming its role.
senses.whyCN: 一份集合被切开后，每一份仍叫 dataset，只加形容词标明它的角色。

senses.title: A structured file with schema
senses.definition: a file whose rows and fields are declared and described by accompanying metadata
senses.definitionCN: 行与字段已声明、并有随附元数据说明的文件
senses.example: The dataset ships with a schema for every column.
senses.exampleCN: 这份数据集为每一列附带了结构说明。
senses.why: a collection becomes usable only when its structure is stated, so the file plus its description is treated as the dataset.
senses.whyCN: 集合只有说清结构才可用，因此文件连同说明一起被当作数据集。

senses.title: A citable item in a repository
senses.definition: a named, identified collection that can be cited by a persistent identifier
senses.definitionCN: 带有持久标识、可被引用的具名集合
senses.example: The paper cites a dataset archived outside the journal.
senses.exampleCN: 论文引用了一份存档在期刊之外的数据集。
senses.why: repositories gave collections identities, and an identified collection is spoken of as a dataset rather than as data in general.
senses.whyCN: 数据仓库给集合以身份，而有了身份的集合就被称为某份数据集，而不是泛泛的数据。

intro.en: Dataset is a modern English compound of data, from Latin datum, and set, a native English noun. The two-word spelling data set is older than the joined form. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dataset 是现代英语复合词，由出自拉丁语 datum 的 data 与英语本族名词 set 组成。分开写的 data set 比连写形式更早。年代均为约数。

items.en: Datum, something given, is the neuter past participle of dare, to give; its plural data reached English as a mass of facts.
items.cn: datum「被给予的东西」是 dare「给予」的中性过去分词；其复数 data 以大量事实之意进入英语。

items.en: Set is native English, from Old English settan, to place or put; as a noun it means a group of things belonging together.
items.cn: set 是英语本族词，出自上古英语 settan「放置」；作名词时指归在一起的一组事物。

items.en: Statisticians spoke of a data set long before computing, meaning the observations gathered for one analysis.
items.cn: 统计学家早在计算机之前就说 data set，指为一次分析收集的观测。

items.en: The joined form dataset spread with machine-readable files in the late twentieth century, when the collection became a portable object.
items.cn: 连写形式 dataset 随机器可读文件在二十世纪后期扩散，此时集合成了可搬运的对象。

items.en: Training and test datasets gave the word a fixed role in modelling, and benchmark datasets made it citable.
items.cn: 训练与测试数据集让这个词在建模中获得固定角色，基准数据集又使它成为可引用的对象。

items.en: The first half from Latin datum and the second from Old English settan are both documented. The date at which the joined spelling became common is approximate, and any older Indo-European source for dare or settan is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：前半出自拉丁语 datum，后半出自上古英语 settan，两段都有文献依据；连写形式普及的年代只有约数，dare 与 settan 更早的印欧语来源属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is the same data family plus near-spellings; the second group names neighbouring collections used in analysis.
note.cn: 第一组是数据词族及形近词；第二组是分析中使用的相邻集合概念。

entries.definition: The same thing written as two words; the spaced form is older and still used in statistics writing.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个东西的分写形式；分写更早，统计写作中仍在使用。

entries.definition: A running store that holds and queries many records; a dataset is usually one prepared collection taken from such stores.
entries.definitionCN: 保存并查询大量记录的运行系统；dataset 通常是从这类库中取出的一份准备好的集合。

entries.definition: A short document listing the specifications of a product; it describes equipment, not research records.
entries.definitionCN: 列出一件产品规格的短文档；它描述设备，不描述研究记录。

entries.definition: A set contained within a larger one; a subset of a dataset is still a dataset only when handled as a unit.
entries.definitionCN: 包含在更大集合里的集合；数据集的一部分只有在被整体处理时才仍叫数据集。

entries.definition: A body of texts assembled for linguistic study; a dataset may hold numbers, images or texts, so corpus is narrower.
entries.definitionCN: 为语言研究汇编的文本总体；dataset 可含数字、图像或文本，corpus 更窄。

entries.definition: A part chosen to represent a whole; a dataset may be a complete collection rather than a sample.
entries.definitionCN: 为代表整体而选出的部分；dataset 可能是完整集合，而不只是样本。

entries.definition: Any group of gathered items; dataset adds the expectation of records meant for analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 任何收集起来的一组物品；dataset 多了「供分析用的记录」这一预期。

entries.definition: Data arranged in rows and columns; many datasets are tables, but a dataset can also be images or text.
entries.definitionCN: 按行列排列的数据；许多数据集是表，但数据集也可以是图像或文本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real two halves, the real statistical history and the real modelling phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的两个构件、真实的统计史与真实的建模搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Data plus set: a set is a group counted as one, so a dataset is data handled as one thing.
normal.cn: data 加 set：集合是被当作一个来数的组，所以数据集就是被当成一件东西处理的数据。

normal.en: The family runs data, dataset, database, subset and metadata.
normal.cn: 同族词有 data、dataset、database、subset 与 metadata。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the modelling roles: training dataset, test dataset, benchmark dataset.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出建模角色：训练数据集、测试数据集、基准数据集。

normal.en: Statisticians used data set before computers, so the word is not originally a computing term.
normal.cn: 统计学家在计算机之前就用 data set，所以这个词原本不是计算机术语。

normal.en: A database runs and answers queries; a dataset is a fixed collection you can hand to someone.
normal.cn: database 运行并回答查询；dataset 是可以交到别人手里的固定集合。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of forms that knows exactly how many rows it has.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠表格，清楚知道自己有多少行。

abstract.en: Picture a bucket of observations poured out one row at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一桶观测，一次倒出一行。

abstract.en: Picture a name tag pinned to a pile of numbers so it can be cited.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆数字被别上名牌，于是可以被引用。

examples.en: The dataset contains images labelled by three independent raters.
examples.cn: 这份数据集包含由三位独立评分者标注的图像。

examples.en: They split the dataset into training and test halves.
examples.cn: 他们把数据集分成训练与测试两半。

examples.en: A dataset without documentation is hard to reuse.
examples.cn: 没有说明文档的数据集很难复用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得（da）他（ta）赛（set）」——得到他那套比赛用的材料，就是数据集

root: 拉丁 dare「给予」→ datum → 复数 data「数据」；上古英语 settan「放置」→ 名词 set「一组」；data 与 set 合为 dataset。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the collection from a plain unit of records to a model input, a benchmark, survey observations, a published artifact, one split, a structured file and a citable repository item.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着「集合」走：从素朴的记录单位，到模型输入、基准、调查观测、公开发布物、某一划分、结构化文件，再到可引用的仓库条目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of tidy tables on a long desk, one record per row, one field per column.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌上一叠整齐的表格，每行一条记录，每列一个字段。

branches.en: ONE UNIT: related records grouped so they can be moved and described together.
branches.cn: 一个单位：相关记录归在一起，可以整体搬运与描述。

branches.en: MODELLING: one body to train on, and one part held back to test.
branches.cn: 建模：一份用来训练，一份留作测试。

branches.en: SHARED REFERENCE: a benchmark everyone scores on, released openly and citable.
branches.cn: 共享参照：人人都在上面打分的基准，公开释放且可引用。

branches.en: OBSERVATION: the records a survey or experiment actually gathered.
branches.cn: 观测：调查或实验实际收集到的记录。

branches.en: OBJECT WITH STRUCTURE AND NAME: schema and identifier turn rows into a reusable artifact.
branches.cn: 有结构有名字的对象：结构说明与标识把行变成可复用的成果。

intro.en: Dataset joins a Latin-derived plural to a native English noun; neither half carries an affix, and the compound is held together by English word order.
intro.cn: dataset 把一个拉丁来源的复数与一个英语本族名词接在一起；两半都不带词缀，复合靠英语词序维系。

latinIntro.en: Only data is Latin; set is native English. There is no Latin compound behind dataset, which is why its structure is so transparent.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 data 来自拉丁语；set 是英语本族词。dataset 背后没有拉丁复合词，所以结构才这么透明。

items.example: The verb explains why data are called given.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词解释了数据为什么被称为「被给予的」。

items.example: One observation is one datum.
items.exampleCN: 一条观测就是一个数据点。

items.example: The plural became an English mass noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个复数成了英语的不可数名词。

items.example: The verb is the root of the noun set.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词 set 的词根。

items.example: A set counts as one.
items.exampleCN: 一个集合被算作一个。

items.example: The compound names a portable collection.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指可搬运的集合。

items.meaning: a set inside a larger set
items.meaningCN: 包含在更大集合中的集合
items.example: A subset is still made of records.
items.exampleCN: 子集仍然由记录构成。

items.example: Metadata describes the columns of a dataset.
items.exampleCN: 元数据描述数据集的各列。

items.example: The bank image stresses storage rather than size.
items.exampleCN: bank 的意象强调存储而非规模。

definition_zh: 反对的；厌恶的；不愿的
definition_en: having a strong dislike of or opposition to something
core_image: 身体往后一转，把脸从某物上挪开
scene: 父亲把菜推向桌子另一头。 He was averse to any dish with cilantro.
sceneCN: 这里 averse 指「厌恶的、不愿的」（第 1 个义项：强烈反感）；句意：他讨厌任何加香菜的菜。

pos.zh: 厌恶的；反对的；不愿的（常作表语）

derivatives.zh: 厌恶；反感（averse + -ion 的名词化）
反感地；不利地（averse + -ly）
令人反感的（心理学用语，averse + -ive）

senses.title: Feeling strong dislike
senses.definition: feeling firm dislike or repugnance toward something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物怀有坚定反感或厌恶
senses.example: She was averse to discussing salaries at dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 她反感在饭桌上谈工资。
senses.why: The Latin root means turned away: dislike as the body turning from a thing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根义为「转开」：厌恶即身体从某物上转过去。

senses.title: Opposed in attitude
senses.definition: opposed to a proposal, practice, or course of action
senses.definitionCN: 对提案、做法或行动路线持反对态度
senses.example: The board was averse to the merger from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会从一开始就反对这桩并购。
senses.why: Turning away extends from feelings to positions taken.
senses.whyCN: 「转开」从情绪延伸到所持立场。

senses.title: Unwilling to do something
senses.definition: reluctant or unwilling, as in not averse to helping
senses.definitionCN: 不情愿、不肯做，如 not averse to helping
senses.example: He is not averse to an extra shift when the pay doubles.
senses.exampleCN: 工资翻倍的话，他并不介意多加一个班。
senses.why: In the litotes not averse, the turning away is only mild.
senses.whyCN: 在低调说法 not averse 中，「转开」的程度很轻。

senses.title: Avoiding risk in economics
senses.definition: preferring certainty over gambles, as in risk-averse investors
senses.definitionCN: 宁取确定而回避赌博，如 risk-averse 投资者
senses.example: Risk-averse buyers chose the fixed-rate loan.
senses.exampleCN: 规避风险的买家选择了固定利率贷款。
senses.why: The turning-away image fits decision theory: turning from variance.
senses.whyCN: 「转开」意象契合决策论：从波动前转开身去。

senses.title: In psychology, producing avoidance
senses.definition: describing stimuli that organisms work to avoid, via the adjective aversive
senses.definitionCN: 指生物体极力回避的刺激，经由 aversive 一词
senses.example: Aversive shocks shaped the rats' learned avoidance.
senses.exampleCN: 厌恶电击塑造了大鼠习得的回避行为。
senses.why: The turning-away became a technical term for what drives it.
senses.whyCN: 「转开」变成了驱动回避行为的术语。

senses.title: Turned away in older English
senses.definition: in older or technical use, physically turned in a direction away from something
senses.definitionCN: 旧式或技术用法中，身体或器官背向某物
senses.example: Older botany texts described leaves averse to the stem.
senses.exampleCN: 旧植物学文献描述叶片背向茎干。
senses.why: This is the literal root sense that the moral senses grew away from.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根的字面本义，道德义项正是从它长出去的。

senses.title: Averse to novelty
senses.definition: disinclined toward new ideas, methods, or technology
senses.definitionCN: 对新观念、新方法或新技术不感兴趣甚至抵触
senses.example: The workshop proved averse to digital record-keeping.
senses.exampleCN: 那间作坊始终不愿改用数字记账。
senses.why: Attachment to the familiar is aversion pointed at the new.
senses.whyCN: 恋旧即厌恶指向了新事物。

senses.title: Aversely, in an unfavorable direction
senses.definition: in the adverb aversely, affecting something negatively or disadvantageously
senses.definitionCN: 副词 aversely 中，以负面或不利的方式影响某事
senses.example: The ruling bore aversely on small lenders.
senses.exampleCN: 这项裁决对小贷机构不利。
senses.why: Turned against a thing can mean acting against its interest.
senses.whyCN: 「转而背对」也可意味着对其利益不利。

intro.en: Averse comes from Latin aversus, turned away, the past participle of avertere, from ab, away, plus vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: averse 出自拉丁语 aversus「转开的」，是动词 avertere 的过去分词，由 ab（离开）+ vertere（转）构成。

items.en: The turn-root goes back to a reconstructed stem wer- meaning to bend or turn.
items.cn: 「转」的词根可追溯至重构词干 wer-「弯、转」。

items.en: averted, from ab, away, plus vertere, to turn, meant to turn something away.
items.cn: 拉丁语 avertere 由 ab「离开」+ vertere「转」构成，意为使转开。

items.en: aversus described a thing or face turned away; morally, turned against.
items.cn: aversus 描述背转的脸或物；道德层面即「反对」。

items.en: English took averse in the late sixteenth century, first literal, soon figurative.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪末借入 averse，先取字面义，很快转为比喻义。

items.en: The pattern averse to fixed in place, and risk aversion later entered economics.
items.cn: averse to 搭配固定下来，「风险规避」后来进入经济学。

items.en: Today averse is almost only predicative: people are averse to things.
items.cn: 如今 averse 几乎只作表语：人对事物 averse。

note.en: Group one gathers the vertere family and its spelling traps; group two gathers words of dislike.
note.cn: 第一组收 vertere 词族及拼写陷阱；第二组收厌恶义场的词。

entries.definition: unfavorable or harmful, acting against; describes conditions, not feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 不利的、有害的（起反作用）；形容条件而非心情，勿与 averse 混用。

entries.definition: the noun: a strong dislike.
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式：强烈的厌恶。

entries.definition: to turn upside down; shares vertere with averse.
entries.definitionCN: 使倒转；与 averse 同享 vertere 词根。

entries.definition: unwilling and hesitating; milder than averse.
entries.definitionCN: 不情愿、犹豫；语气比 averse 温和。

entries.definition: unwilling out of dislike; also predicative, as loath to admit.
entries.definitionCN: 因厌恶而不愿；同样常作表语，如 loath to admit。

entries.definition: not minded to do something; formal and mild.
entries.definitionCN: 无意于做某事；正式而温和。

entries.definition: naturally opposed in feeling; stronger and more settled than averse.
entries.definitionCN: 天性相斥的；比 averse 更强、更持久。

entries.definition: actively unfriendly; aversion turned into aggression.
entries.definitionCN: 怀敌意的；厌恶转为攻击性的状态。

normalIntro.en: Break it as a-verse: your body turns a verse away, the opposite direction from the thing.
normalIntro.cn: 拆成 a-verse 记：身体像翻页一样把某物翻到背面去。

normal.en: av- from ab- means away: averse turns away, adverse turns against.
normal.cn: av- 出自 ab-「离开」：averse 是转身躲开，adverse 是迎面作对。

normal.en: Risk-averse is the fixed economic collocation.
normal.cn: risk-averse 是经济学固定搭配：规避风险的。

normal.en: not averse to is the polite way of saying quite willing.
normal.cn: not averse to 是「还挺乐意」的礼貌说法。

normal.en: The family holds together: avert, aversion, aversive all carry the same turning.
normal.cn: 词族提示：avert、aversion、aversive 都带同一个「转」。

normal.en: Averse needs a person; adverse needs weather, effects, conditions.
normal.cn: averse 用于人，adverse 用于天气、效果、条件。

abstract.en: Feel your shoulders angle away from the offer.
abstract.cn: 感觉肩膀朝提议的反方向偏过去。

abstract.en: Averse is a no spoken with the whole spine.
abstract.cn: averse 是用整条脊柱说出的「不」。

abstract.en: Picture a compass needle swinging off north and holding there.
abstract.cn: 想象罗盘针偏开正北并停在那里。

examples.en: Conservative savers are averse to putting money in equities.
examples.cn: 保守的储户不愿把钱投入股市。

examples.en: He was not averse to a little flattery now and then.
examples.cn: 他偶尔也不排斥听两句恭维。

examples.en: The committee remained averse to any delay in the schedule.
examples.cn: 委员会反对日程出现任何延误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恶我死」——那东西一靠近他就喊「恶我死」，赶紧把脸转开

root: 出自拉丁语 aversus「转开的」，为 avertere 的过去分词，由 ab-（离开）+ vertere（转）构成，与 reverse、convert、divert 同属 vertere 词族。16 世纪末进入英语，先表「背向」后转指心理上的「厌恶、反对」，如今几乎只作表语形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from the one root image of turning away: dislike, opposition, unwillingness, risk avoidance, and the technical senses in psychology and older prose.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「转开」这一根意象展开：厌恶、反对、不情愿、规避风险，以及心理学与旧文体中的技术义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body pivoting so its face no longer meets the thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体转过去，脸不再迎向那事物。

branches.en: THE FEELING SIDE: dislike and the opposition it becomes.
branches.cn: 情感一面：反感及其化成的反对。

branches.en: THE WILLINGNESS SIDE: mild turning in not averse to.
branches.cn: 意愿一面：not averse to 中的轻度转开。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL SIDE: risk economics and avoidance learning.
branches.cn: 技术一面：风险经济学与回避学习。

branches.en: THE LITERAL SIDE: turned away in old botany and anatomy.
branches.cn: 字面一面：旧植物学、解剖学中的背向。

branches.en: THE SET SIDE: habit turned from novelty, effect turned against interest.
branches.cn: 定型一面：习惯背对新事物，作用背离利益。

intro.en: Averse is ab- plus versus: the prefix says away, the participle says turned.
intro.cn: averse 的结构是 ab-（离开）加 versus（转开的）。

latinIntro.en: The vertere family is one of Latin's most productive: every turn in English often hides it.
latinIntro.cn: vertere 词族是拉丁语最高产的词族之一：英语里许多「转」都藏着它。

items.exampleCN: 缺席、戒除、转移

items.exampleCN: 拉丁散文中的 vertere

items.example: aversus in classical texts
items.exampleCN: 古典文献中的 aversus

items.example: avert one's eyes
items.exampleCN: 移开目光

items.exampleCN: 恶劣天气

items.exampleCN: 撤销决定

items.exampleCN: 兑换货币

items.exampleCN: 厌恶刺激

definition_zh: 便利设施；舒适宜人的环境；愉快；（amenities）礼节
definition_en: a desirable or useful feature of a place; pleasantness; courtesies of social life
core_image: 酒店大堂那张舒服的沙发和免费的咖啡角：让日子过得舒服的小东西
scene: 新建的公寓楼下有健身房、花园和全天便利店。 The building offers every modern amenity a resident could want.
sceneCN: 这里的 amenity 是「便利设施」（第 1 个义项：提高生活舒适度的设施）；句意是这栋楼提供住户想要的各种现代化便利设施。

pos.zh: 便利设施；舒适设备
宜人；舒适
（复数）社交礼节

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，常指成套的便利设施或社交礼节
同源近族词（词源关系存疑），义为「顺从的；乐于配合的」，注意区分

senses.title: A useful or pleasant feature of a place
senses.titleCN: 便利设施：让生活舒适方便的配置
senses.definition: a feature of a building or place that makes life there easier or more pleasant
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物或场所中使生活更方便舒适的配置
senses.example: The apartment complex includes a pool and other amenities.
senses.exampleCN: 这个公寓小区配有游泳池等便利设施。
senses.why: From the idea of pleasantness, real estate narrowed the word to the things that supply it.
senses.whyCN: 从「宜人」这个抽象概念出发，房地产行业把这个词具体化为提供舒适感的各种设施。

senses.title: The pleasant quality of a place or climate
senses.titleCN: 宜人：环境或气候的舒适特质
senses.definition: the pleasantness or attractiveness of surroundings or weather
senses.definitionCN: 环境或天气的舒适宜人之处
senses.example: Visitors praise the amenity of the coastal climate.
senses.exampleCN: 游客称赞沿海气候的宜人。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the quality itself before any object supplying it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：先有「宜人」这种性质，才有提供这种性质的物件。

senses.title: Pleasant social relations
senses.titleCN: 社交融洽：人际间的和乐
senses.definition: the pleasant quality of social interaction among people
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间交往的和乐融洽
senses.example: Office amenity improved once the managers stopped shouting.
senses.exampleCN: 经理们不再吼叫后，办公室气氛融洽多了。
senses.why: Pleasantness of place extends naturally to pleasantness among the people in it.
senses.whyCN: 场所的宜人很自然地延伸为场所中人与人相处的宜人。

senses.title: Courtesies and polite conventions
senses.titleCN: 社交礼节：复数形式的客套规范
senses.definition: in the plural, the polite conventions observed in social or diplomatic life
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式，指社交或外交场合遵循的客套礼节
senses.example: Despite the dispute, the two delegations observed the amenities.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管有分歧，两个代表团仍遵守外交礼节。
senses.why: Politeness is pleasantness maintained between strangers, so the word covers its rituals.
senses.whyCN: 礼貌就是陌生人之间维持的「宜人」，于是礼节也被这个词覆盖。

senses.title: Small complimentary items of comfort
senses.titleCN: 免费小用品：酒店洗漱包等
senses.definition: small complimentary items provided for comfort, such as toiletries in hotels
senses.definitionCN: 为舒适而提供的免费小物件，如酒店洗漱用品
senses.example: The room came with towels and complimentary amenities.
senses.exampleCN: 房间配有毛巾和免费洗漱用品。
senses.why: The hospitality industry shrank the broad sense to the tangible giveaways guests take home.
senses.whyCN: 酒店业把宽泛的「设施」义缩小到客人能带走的实物赠品上。

senses.title: Legal comfort interests in land
senses.titleCN: 法律上的环境舒适利益
senses.definition: in property law, the non-material benefits of land such as views or quiet
senses.definitionCN: 财产法中土地的非实体利益，如景观、安静
senses.example: The court weighed the loss of amenity caused by the new highway.
senses.exampleCN: 法院权衡了新高速公路造成的环境舒适损失。
senses.why: Law needs a word for comfort that has no price tag but has value.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一个词指称那些没有标价却有价值的舒适利益。

intro.en: Amenity comes through Old French from Latin comitas-related roots of pleasantness; its link to amare, to love, is generally assumed.
intro.cn: amenity 经古法语来自拉丁语表示「宜人」的词，一般认为与表示「爱」的 amare 词根相关（关系存疑）。

items.en: amaenitas, pleasantness or charm, generally connected with amoenus, pleasing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 amaenitas「宜人、魅力」，一般与 amoenus「令人愉悦的」相关。

items.en: amoenus may derive from amare, to love, though some scholars prefer an older Mediterranean word.
items.cn: amoenus 可能源自 amare「爱」，也有学者认为来自更古老的地中海语词（存疑）。

items.en: amenite, pleasantness, borrowed from Latin learned vocabulary.
items.cn: 古法语 amenite「宜人」，借自拉丁书面语。

items.en: English amenity first meant pleasantness of place or manner.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语 amenity 首先表示地点或举止的宜人。

items.en: The plural amenities widened to social courtesies, then to convenient facilities.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪复数 amenities 先扩为社交礼节，再转为便利设施。

items.en: Now the standard word for comfort features in real estate, hotels, and urban planning.
items.cn: 如今是房地产、酒店与城市规划中表示舒适设施的标准用词。

note.en: Separate amenity from its look-alike amenable and from rival words for comfort and convenience.
note.cn: 把 amenity 与形近词 amenable 区分开，也要与表示舒适便利的近义词区分。

entries.definition: willing to cooperate; a different root despite the shared opening letters.
entries.definitionCN: 顺从配合的；与 amenity 开头拼写相近但词根不同。

entries.definition: friendly in manner; from Latin amare, to love.
entries.definitionCN: 和蔼可亲的；源自拉丁语 amare「爱」。

entries.definition: rhyming abstract noun of -ity; dignity is worth, amenity is comfort.
entries.definitionCN: 同韵 -ity 抽象名词：dignity 是尊严，amenity 是舒适。

entries.definition: a space or equipment serving a function; more functional, less cozy.
entries.definitionCN: 设施、场所；偏功能性，少了「舒适」意味。

entries.definition: ease of use or access; stresses saving effort.
entries.definitionCN: 便利；强调省时省力。

entries.definition: physical ease and wellbeing; broader than a single feature.
entries.definitionCN: 舒适；泛指身心安适，范围比单一设施更宽。

normalIntro.en: Tie amenity to the pleasant little extras that make life easy.

senses.title: Reasoning from the general to the particular
senses.titleCN: 演绎推理：从通则推到个案
senses.definition: the process of drawing a particular conclusion from general premises
senses.definitionCN: 从一般前提出发得出特定结论的过程
senses.example: The argument proceeds by deduction from two general principles.
senses.exampleCN: 该论证从两条一般原则出发，通过演绎推进。
senses.why: Latin deducere means 'to lead away or down'. Reasoning is pictured as leading a conclusion down from higher premises to the case at hand.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 deducere 意为“引开、引下”。推理被描绘成把结论从更高的前提一路引到眼前个案。

senses.title: The conclusion reached
senses.titleCN: 推出的结论：演绎的产物
senses.definition: the particular conclusion that results from such reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 由这种推理得出的特定结论
senses.example: Her deduction surprised the investigators.
senses.exampleCN: 她推出的结论让调查人员吃惊。
senses.why: The act and its product share one noun: what is led down is both the leading and the thing that arrives at the bottom.
senses.whyCN: 行为与产物共用同一个名词：被引下来的既是“引”的过程，也是最终抵达下面的那个东西。

senses.title: Subtraction in arithmetic
senses.definition: the arithmetic operation of taking one number away from another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个数中减去另一个数的算术运算
senses.example: The final step is a simple deduction of five from the total.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一步是从总数中减去五。
senses.why: The same 'lead away' image works for numbers: an amount is led away from the total, leaving a smaller figure behind.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“引开”意象也适用于数字：一笔数额被从总数中引走，留下更小的数。

senses.title: A tax deduction
senses.titleCN: 税收扣除：从应税收入中减去
senses.definition: an amount allowed to be subtracted from taxable income
senses.definitionCN: 允许从应税收入中减去的款项
senses.example: The tax deduction lowered her annual bill by two thousand dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 这项税收扣除让她的年度税单少了两千美元。
senses.why: Tax law leads certain expenses away from income before the rate is applied, so the amount is literally deducted from the taxable base.
senses.whyCN: 税法在适用税率前把某些支出从收入中引走，因此这笔款项确实是从应税基数中扣除的。

senses.title: A payroll deduction
senses.titleCN: 工资扣款：发薪前先扣走
senses.definition: an amount withheld from wages before payment
senses.definitionCN: 发薪前从工资中预先扣下的款项
senses.example: The payslip lists three deductions, including pension contributions.
senses.exampleCN: 工资单列出三项扣款，包括养老金缴款。
senses.why: The employer leads money away from gross pay before the worker receives it. The noun names both the act and the sum withheld.
senses.whyCN: 雇主在工人拿到工资前把钱从应发额中引走。这个名词既指行为，也指被扣下的金额。

senses.title: The act of subtracting
senses.titleCN: 扣除行为：减法这个动作本身
senses.definition: the act of taking something away from a whole or an amount
senses.definitionCN: 从整体或数额中拿走某物的行为
senses.example: The deduction of the agency fee happens at the end of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 代理费的扣除在月底进行。
senses.why: When the focus is on the operation rather than the sum, deduction names the taking-away itself, parallel to subtraction as an activity.
senses.whyCN: 当焦点在操作而非金额时，deduction 命名的是“拿走”本身，与作为活动的 subtraction 平行。

senses.title: The deductive method
senses.titleCN: 演绎法：以演绎为主的推理方式
senses.definition: a method of inquiry that works from general theory to specific predictions
senses.definitionCN: 从一般理论推出具体预测的研究方法
senses.example: The course contrasts the deductive and inductive methods.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程对比演绎法与归纳法。
senses.why: Deduction as a method is reasoning treated as a procedure: start at the general level and lead the conclusion down to the data.
senses.whyCN: 作为方法的演绎，是把推理当作程序：从一般层面出发，把结论一路引到数据。

senses.title: A price reduction
senses.titleCN: 减价：从标价中减去的部分
senses.definition: an amount taken off a price or quoted sum
senses.definitionCN: 从价格或报价中减去的数额
senses.example: The dealer offered a deduction of five per cent for cash payment.
senses.exampleCN: 经销商对现金付款提供了百分之五的减价。
senses.why: Commerce leads a part of the quoted price away as an allowance, so the word covers discounts as well as tax and wage deductions.
senses.whyCN: 商业把报价的一部分作为让利引走，因此这个词也覆盖折扣，不只税收与工资扣款。

intro.en: Deduction comes from Latin deductio 'a leading away', from deducere 'to lead down or away'. The logical sense is a later, figurative extension of a physical leading.
intro.cn: deduction 来自拉丁 deductio“引开”，源自 deducere“引下、引走”。逻辑义是物理“引导”意象后来的比喻延伸。

items.en: deducere joins de- 'down, away' with ducere 'to lead'. Its literal picture is leading someone or something from one place to another, often downhill.
items.cn: deducere 由 de-“向下、离开”与 ducere“引导”组成。其字面画面是把人或物从一处引到另一处，常含向下之意。

items.en: deductio 'a leading away' covered both physical escorting and, in rhetorical and legal writing, the drawing out of an argument.
items.cn: deductio“引开”既指实际的护送，也指修辞与法律写作中对论点的引出。

items.en: Medieval and early modern logic used the Latin word for drawing a conclusion from premises; English deduction took this sense in the 16th century. The exact route is roughly dated.
items.cn: 中世纪与近代早期逻辑学用这个拉丁词表示从前提引出结论；英语 deduction 在16世纪取得此义。具体路径年代为约数。

items.en: The sense 'subtraction' and later 'amount subtracted' developed in parallel, since taking a number away is also a leading away. Tax and wage uses are modern extensions.
items.cn: “减法”义及后来的“扣除额”义平行发展，因为拿走一个数字同样是“引开”。税收与工资用法是现代的延伸。

items.en: In the 19th and 20th centuries deduction became the standard name for the general-to-particular method, opposed to induction.
items.cn: 19、20世纪，deduction 成为“从一般到个别”方法的标准名称，与 induction（归纳）相对。

items.en: The precise date when the logical sense entered English is uncertain, and the deeper PIE origin of ducere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 逻辑义进入英语的确切年代存疑，ducere 的更早印欧语来源属重构。

note.en: The first group contains related forms that differ in part of speech or prefix; the second contains reasoning and subtraction terms with different directions.
note.cn: 第一组是词性或前缀不同的相关形式；第二组是方向不同的推理与减法术语。

entries.definition: The adjective describing reasoning of this kind; deduction is the noun for the process or result.
entries.definitionCN: 描述这类推理的形容词；deduction 是过程或结果的名词。

entries.definition: To subtract an amount; it is the verb used for tax and wages, not for logical inference.
entries.definitionCN: 减去一笔金额；用于税收与工资，不用于逻辑推断。

entries.definition: To reach a conclusion by reasoning; it is the verb that pairs with deduction in the logical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 通过推理得出结论；与逻辑义的 deduction 搭配的动词。

entries.definition: Any conclusion drawn from evidence; it covers both deduction and induction, so it is broader.
entries.definitionCN: 从证据得出的任何结论；同时覆盖演绎与归纳，因此更宽。

entries.definition: The end point of an argument; it names the result, while deduction can name the process too.
entries.definitionCN: 论证的终点；命名的结果，而 deduction 也可命名过程。

entries.definition: The arithmetic operation of taking one number from another; it lacks the logical and financial senses.
entries.definitionCN: 从一个数减去另一个数的算术运算；没有逻辑与金融义。

entries.definition: A partial refund paid back after a payment; a deduction is taken off before payment.
entries.definitionCN: 付款后返还的部分款项；deduction 是付款前先减去。

entries.definition: An amount allowed for a purpose; in tax contexts it functions like a deduction but stresses permission.
entries.definitionCN: 为某用途允许的额度；在税务语境中作用类似扣除，但强调“允许”。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin morphology, standard collocations and the ducere word family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实拉丁构词、标准搭配与 ducere 词族。

normal.en: de- 'down/away' + ducere 'lead': a deduction leads the conclusion down from general premises.
normal.cn: de-“向下／离开”+ ducere“引导”：deduction 把结论从一般前提引下来。

normal.en: The same 'lead away' image gives the money sense: an amount is led away from the total.
normal.cn: 同一个“引开”意象给出金钱义：一笔数额被从总数中引走。

normal.en: Learn tax deduction, logical deduction and payroll deduction; these show the three main branches.
normal.cn: 记住 tax deduction、logical deduction、payroll deduction；它们展示三个主要分支。

normal.en: deduce is for logic, deduct is for money: keep the pair apart.
normal.cn: deduce 用于逻辑，deduct 用于金钱：把这组分开。

normal.en: deduction, deductive, deduce, deduct and duct all carry the duc- 'lead' core.
normal.cn: deduction、deductive、deduce、deduct、duct 都带有 duc-“引导”核心。

abstract.en: Picture a chain pulled down from a high hook, each link a premise, ending at one small conclusion.
abstract.cn: 想象一条链从高处钩子被拉下，每一环是一个前提，末端是一个小结论。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of coins with one coin slid off the edge: subtraction is the same leading away.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠硬币中有一枚被滑出边缘：减法就是同一种“引开”。

abstract.en: Picture a payslip with three lines struck out before the final figure is printed.
abstract.cn: 想象工资单上在最终数字打印前划掉三行。

examples.en: From the two premises, the detective made a deduction about the time of the crime.
examples.cn: 侦探从两个前提推断出作案时间。

examples.en: The standard deduction reduces the income on which tax is calculated.
examples.cn: 标准扣除额减少了计税所依据的收入。

examples.en: A deduction of ten per cent applies to orders paid in advance.
examples.cn: 预付订单可享受百分之十的减价。

dict_mnemonic.text: “de（向下）+ duc（引导）+ tion”——把结论从上往下引出来，也把钱从总数里引走 → deduction 推论、扣除

root: 拉丁 deducere“引下、引走”（de-“向下／离开”+ ducere“引导”）；deduct- 词干 + -ion 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one gesture: leading something away. Logic leads a conclusion down from premises; arithmetic, tax and payroll lead an amount away from a total.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个动作：把某物引开。逻辑把结论从前提引下；算术、税收与工资则把一笔数额从总数引走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain pulled down from a high point to a single end link.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条链从高处被拉下，最后落到单独一环。

branches.en: LOGIC: reasoning from premises and the deductive method are the same downward leading, one as an act and one as a procedure.
branches.cn: 逻辑：从前提推理与演绎法，是同一种向下引导，一个是行为，一个是程序。

branches.en: RESULT: the conclusion is what arrives at the bottom of the chain.
branches.cn: 结果：结论就是抵达链条底端的东西。

branches.en: ARITHMETIC: subtraction and the act of subtracting are the same taking-away seen as operation and activity.
branches.cn: 算术：减法与扣除行为，是同一“拿走”在运算与活动两个层面的呈现。

branches.en: MONEY: tax deductions and payroll deductions both lead an amount away before the final figure is fixed.
branches.cn: 金钱：税收扣除与工资扣款，都在最终数字确定前把一笔金额引走。

branches.en: PRICE: a deduction from a quoted price is the same allowance applied at the point of sale.
branches.cn: 价格：从报价中减去的部分，是在销售环节应用的同一让利。

intro.en: Deduction is deduct + -ion, on the Latin participle stem deduct-. The base verb is deducere; the prefix de- and the root duc- are fossilized inside it.
intro.cn: deduction 是 deduct + -ion，建立在拉丁分词词干 deduct- 上。词基动词是 deducere；前缀 de- 与词根 duc- 已凝固在其内部。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere 'to lead' yields a large family: conduct, produce, reduce, introduce, induce, educate and deduct. The prefixed forms each specify a direction of leading.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere“引导”衍生出庞大词族：conduct、produce、reduce、introduce、induce、educate、deduct。每个带前缀形式都指定一种引导方向。

items.meaning: a leading away; a conclusion or an amount removed
items.meaningCN: 引开；推论；扣除（-ion 名词后缀）
items.example: The deduction follows from the second premise.
items.exampleCN: 这个推论由第二个前提得出。

items.meaning: to reach a conclusion by reasoning
items.meaningCN: 推断；演绎（de-“向下”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: We can deduce the age of the rock from its layers.
items.exampleCN: 我们可以从岩层推断岩石的年龄。

items.meaningCN: 扣除；减去（de-“离开”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: The fee is deducted from the first payment.
items.exampleCN: 费用从首笔付款中扣除。

items.meaning: relating to reasoning from general to particular
items.example: The deductive step is valid but the premise is false.
items.exampleCN: 演绎步骤有效，但前提是假的。

items.meaning: able to be subtracted; an amount paid before insurance covers the rest
items.meaningCN: 可扣除的；保险免赔额（-ible“可……的”）
items.example: The policy has a five-hundred-dollar deductible.
items.exampleCN: 该保单有五百美元免赔额。

items.example: The conclusion is deducible from the data.
items.exampleCN: 该结论可从数据推断出来。

items.meaning: to lead into a state or belief
items.meaningCN: 诱导；引起（in-“进入”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: The drug induces sleep within minutes.
items.exampleCN: 这种药几分钟内就能引起睡意。

items.meaning: to lead back; to make smaller
items.meaningCN: 减少；使变小（re-“回”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: The new rules reduced waste by a third.
items.exampleCN: 新规定使浪费减少了三分之一。

items.meaning: to lead or guide; to carry out
items.meaningCN: 引导；进行（con-“一起”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: She conducted the experiment twice.
items.exampleCN: 她把实验做了两次。
