senses.definitionCN: 汇集证据与方法以复原某一过去时期气候的研究过程
senses.example: The climate reconstruction took five years and three field seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 这次气候重建花了五年和三个野外季节。
senses.why: The noun names the activity first, because the phrase literally describes building again something that no longer exists.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词首先指活动，因为该短语字面上就是把已经不存在的东西再次建造起来。

senses.title: The resulting series
senses.definition: the ordered sequence of past temperatures or rainfall values produced by the work
senses.definitionCN: 由重建工作产出的过去温度或降水数值的有序序列
senses.example: The published climate reconstruction runs from the tenth century to the present.
senses.exampleCN: 发表的那条气候重建序列从十世纪一直延续到今天。
senses.why: A finished reconstruction is a line of numbers through time, so the same noun names the output.
senses.whyCN: 完成的重建是一条贯穿时间的数字曲线，因此同一个名词也指成果。

senses.title: A proxy-based method
senses.definition: a technique that converts tree rings, ice, corals or sediments into climate information
senses.definitionCN: 把树木年轮、冰、珊瑚或沉积物转成气候信息的技术
senses.example: The team used a climate reconstruction built on tree rings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队采用了一种建立在树木年轮上的气候重建。
senses.why: Since no thermometer reaches the past, the phrase often labels the method that substitutes natural archives for instruments.
senses.whyCN: 没有温度计能抵达过去，因此这个短语常指用自然档案替代仪器的方法。

senses.title: A regional reconstruction
senses.definition: a reconstruction limited to one region, such as a basin, a coast or a plateau
senses.definitionCN: 限于一个区域的重建，如某个盆地、海岸或高原
senses.example: Their regional climate reconstruction covers the whole Mediterranean basin.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的区域气候重建覆盖整个地中海盆地。
senses.why: Evidence is local, so the phrase is routinely narrowed to a named area before it is widened.
senses.whyCN: 证据是局地的，所以这个短语常先收窄到某个具体地区，再向外推广。

senses.title: A global reconstruction
senses.definition: a reconstruction that merges records from many regions into a single world-wide picture
senses.definitionCN: 把许多地区的记录并成一幅全球图景的重建
senses.example: A global climate reconstruction combines records from every continent.
senses.exampleCN: 一次全球气候重建把各大洲的记录合并起来。
senses.why: One region cannot answer a planetary question, so the phrase scales up to the whole globe.
senses.whyCN: 一个区域回答不了行星尺度的问题，于是这个短语扩展到整个地球。

senses.title: A year-by-year reconstruction
senses.definition: a reconstruction fine enough to give one value for each year or each season
senses.definitionCN: 精细到每年或每季给出一个数值的重建
senses.example: The annual climate reconstruction resolves every single year.
senses.exampleCN: 这条年度气候重建能分辨每一年。
senses.why: Resolution is the quality that matters most, so the phrase is modified by the time step it can resolve.
senses.whyCN: 分辨率是最要紧的品质，因此这个短语常受它能分辨的时间步长修饰。

senses.title: One member of an ensemble
senses.definition: a single reconstruction among several that differ in proxies, methods or assumptions
senses.definitionCN: 在代用资料、方法或假设上有所不同的若干重建中的一套
senses.example: Each climate reconstruction in the set uses slightly different proxies.
senses.exampleCN: 这一组里的每一套气候重建都使用了略有差异的代用资料。
senses.why: Science rarely trusts one curve, so the phrase is counted and compared as one member of a family.
senses.whyCN: 科学很少只信一条曲线，因此这个短语会被当作一族中的一员来计数与比较。

senses.title: A reconstruction used to test models
senses.definition: a past-climate series employed as a target against which climate simulations are judged
senses.definitionCN: 用作目标、用来评判气候模拟结果的过去气候序列
senses.example: The model was checked against a climate reconstruction of the last millennium.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型对照过去一千年的气候重建接受了检验。
senses.why: A simulation needs an independent past to beat or match, and the phrase supplies the yardstick.
senses.whyCN: 模拟需要一个独立的过去来比较，这个短语就提供了那把尺子。

intro.en: The phrase joins climate, from Greek klima through Latin clima, to reconstruction, from Latin struere, to pile up, through construere, to build, plus re-, again, and -ion, a noun ending. The whole phrase is a twentieth-century formation; the exact year of first use is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个短语把「climate」与「reconstruction」接在一起：前者从希腊语「klima」经拉丁语「clima」而来；后者来自拉丁语「struere」「堆起」，经「construere」「建造」，再加表示「再次」的前缀与名词词尾。整短语是二十世纪构造，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Klima named a slope or a zone of the earth, since the sun's angle was thought to shape each region.
items.cn: 这个词指斜坡或地表的地带，因为太阳角度被认为塑造了每个区域。

items.en: Latin clima kept the zone sense, and English climate slowly narrowed to the weather of a region.
items.cn: 拉丁语「clima」保留了地带之意，英语「climate」则慢慢收窄为某一地区的天气。

items.en: Struere meant to pile up or arrange, the plain act of stacking material into a structure.
items.cn: 这个词意为堆起、排列，即把材料堆成结构的朴素动作。

items.en: Construere added the idea of bringing pieces together, and English construct came from it.
items.cn: 这个词加上了把各件东西聚拢的意思，英语的「construct」由此而来。

items.en: The prefix re- means again and the ending -ion makes a noun of action or result, giving reconstruction.
items.cn: 前缀表示「再次」，词尾把动作或结果变成名词，于是有了「reconstruction」。

items.en: The full phrase climate reconstruction belongs to the twentieth century; the exact year of first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 完整的短语「climate reconstruction」属于二十世纪，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like climate reconstruction; the second group names neighbouring ideas of past-climate evidence and model testing.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「climate reconstruction」相近；第二组是与「过去气候证据、模型检验」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The act or result of building something again, the noun inside the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指再次建造的动作或结果，是短语内部的名词。

entries.definition: To build again from evidence, the verb behind the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指依据证据重新构建，是短语背后的动词。

entries.definition: Serving to rebuild, often used of surgery or of historical work.
entries.definitionCN: 指用于重建的，常用于外科手术或历史工作。

entries.definition: The act of building, without the idea of doing it a second time.
entries.definitionCN: 指建造的动作，但不含「再一次」的意思。

entries.definition: The long-term weather of a region, the first half of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个地区的长期天气，是短语的前一半。

entries.definition: A natural archive that stands in for direct climate measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 指代替直接气候测量的自然档案。

entries.definition: The ancient climate itself, which a reconstruction aims to recover.
entries.definitionCN: 指古代气候本身，正是重建工作要复原的对象。

entries.definition: The sequence of past climates, close to the result sense of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指过去气候的序列，接近这个短语的结果义。

entries.definition: A model run aimed at a past period, the operation that consumes a reconstruction.
entries.definitionCN: 指针对过去时段运行模型，正是使用重建结果的操作。

entries.definition: A reconstruction of recent climate built by combining observations with models.
entries.definitionCN: 指把观测与模型结合、重建近代气候的产品。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the literal pieces of the phrase, its real evidence and its real modelling use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个短语的字面成分、真实证据与真实建模用途。

normal.en: Climate plus reconstruction: you build the weather of the past a second time from what it left behind.
normal.cn: 气候加重建：用过去留下的东西，把当年的天气再建一次。

normal.en: The Latin struere meant to pile up, which is exactly what a reconstruction does with dated points.
normal.cn: 拉丁语的「struere」意为堆起，而重建正是把有年代的散点堆叠起来。

normal.en: A climate reconstruction is usually built from tree rings, ice cores, corals and lake mud.
normal.cn: 气候重建通常由树木年轮、冰芯、珊瑚与湖泥搭成。

normal.en: High-resolution climate reconstruction is the phrase used when every year can be told apart.
normal.cn: 当每一年都能分辨时，用的说法就是高分辨率气候重建。

normal.en: A reconstruction of the last millennium is the standard target for testing climate models.
normal.cn: 过去一千年的重建是检验气候模型的标准靶子。

abstract.en: A reconstruction is a bridge built from both ends: evidence from the past, questions from the present.
abstract.cn: 重建是一座从两端搭起的桥：一端是过去的证据，一端是现在的问题。

abstract.en: The past left no thermometer, only scraps; reconstruction is the act of reading a line into those scraps.
abstract.cn: 过去没有留下温度计，只留下碎片；重建就是把这些碎片读成一条线。

abstract.en: Each curve is a second building of something that can never be visited again.
abstract.cn: 每条曲线都是对一座再也无法到访的建筑的二次建造。

examples.en: The climate reconstruction relies on corals from the tropical Pacific.
examples.cn: 这次气候重建依靠热带太平洋的珊瑚。

examples.en: They compared every climate reconstruction available for the last two thousand years.
examples.cn: 他们比较了过去两千年所有可用的气候重建。

examples.en: A good climate reconstruction must state its uncertainty clearly.
examples.cn: 一份好的气候重建必须清楚说明自身的不确定性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「克莱美特 瑞肯斯特拉克申」——气候被拆成零件，再按年代重新搭回去：气候重建。

root: 「climate」源于希腊语「klima」「倾斜、地带」，经拉丁语「clima」进入英语；「reconstruction」来自拉丁语「struere」「堆起、建造」，经「construere」「堆在一起、建造」得「construct」，再加表示「再次」的前缀与名词词尾；整短语属二十世纪，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the work itself to its output, its proxy method, a region, the globe, a yearly resolution, one member of an ensemble, and a yardstick for models.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从重建工作本身走向它的成果、代用资料方法、一个区域、全球、逐年分辨率、多套中的一套，以及检验模型的尺子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered dated points on a long table are joined into one temperature curve.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌上散落的有年代的点，被接成一条温度曲线。

branches.en: THE WORK: hands and methods assemble evidence until a past climate can be stated.
branches.cn: 重建工作：双手与方法汇集证据，直到过去的气候可以被陈述。

branches.en: THE CURVE AND THE METHOD: the finished series, and the proxy technique that produced it.
branches.cn: 曲线与方法：完成的序列，以及产出它的代用资料技术。

branches.en: THE LOCAL AND THE PLANETARY: one basin filled in, then every continent joined together.
branches.cn: 局地与行星：先填满一个盆地，再把各大洲接成整体。

branches.en: THE FINE AND THE MANY: a year-by-year line, and one member among several competing lines.
branches.cn: 精细与多套：逐年的曲线，以及若干竞争曲线中的一套。

branches.en: THE YARDSTICK: the reconstructed past becomes the target a simulation must match.
branches.cn: 尺子：被重建的过去成为模拟必须对上的目标。

intro.en: Climate reconstruction joins a Greek-derived climate word to a Latin-derived building word and a noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊来源的「气候」词、拉丁来源的「建造」词与一个名词词尾接在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies clima for climate, struere and construere for building, and the prefix and ending that make reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示气候的「clima」、表示建造的「struere」与「construere」，以及构成「重建」的前缀与词尾。

items.example: The zone word became the climate word.
items.exampleCN: 这个地带词后来变成了气候词。

items.example: Latin carried the word into English usage.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个词带进了英语的用法。

items.example: It is the first half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个短语的前一半。

items.example: The verb names the act of stacking material.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把材料堆叠起来的动作。

items.example: English construct descends from this verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语的「construct」源自这个动词。

items.example: It marks the second building of the same thing.
items.exampleCN: 它标出对同一事物的第二次建造。

items.example: It turns the verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成名词。

items.example: It is the second half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个短语的后一半。

items.example: The shorter verb sits inside the longer noun.
items.exampleCN: 较短的动词包含在较长的名词里。

derivatives.zh: 由表示「再次」的前缀加「建造」的动词构成，义为「重建；复原」
由重建动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「重建；重建物」
由重建动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「重建的；复原性的」
由同一希腊词干经拉丁语而来，义为「气候」
由「气候」加形容词词尾构成，义为「气候的」

definition_zh: 地热的（与地球内部热量有关的，尤指可用来发电或供暖的地下热能）
definition_en: relating to the heat inside the earth, especially heat that can be used for power generation or heating
core_image: 钻头打到地下深处，热水与蒸汽沿井筒冲上来推动涡轮；地球内部缓慢衰变的放射性物质，就是那口永不熄火的灶
scene: 钻机在雪山上打到了热水层，白汽从井口冒出。 The geothermal plant draws steam from a reservoir two kilometres below the surface.
sceneCN: 这里 geothermal 指「与地下热能有关的」（第 1 个义项：热量来源属性）；句意为这座地热电厂从地表下两公里的储层取汽。

pos.zh: 地热的（作定语，无比较级与最高级；副词形式不常用，一般用介词短语表示方式）

derivatives.zh: geo-（希腊 gē「大地」）+ thermē（「热」）+ -ics（学科后缀）→ 地热学：研究地下热量的学科
geo- + thermo- + -metry（希腊 metron「测量」）→ 地温测量：用矿物或流体推算古温度
geo- + thermē + -ic（形容词后缀）→ 地热的（罕见变体，与 geothermal 同义）
thermē（希腊「热」）+ -al → 热的：与温度有关的
thermo- + -meter（希腊 metron「测量」）→ 温度计：测量热的仪器
hydro-（希腊 hydōr「水」）+ thermal → 热液的：地下热水参与形成的

senses.title: Of the earth's heat
senses.definition: relating to heat produced or stored beneath the earth's surface
senses.definitionCN: 与地表之下产生或储存的热有关
senses.example: The geothermal plant draws steam from a reservoir two kilometres below the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 这座地热电厂从地表下两公里的储层取汽。
senses.why: geo- is earth and thermē is heat: the adjective simply locates heat below ground.
senses.whyCN: geo- 是大地，thermē 是热：这个形容词只是把热定位在地下。

senses.title: The temperature gradient
senses.definition: the rise in rock temperature with depth, the physical reason geothermal heat is reachable
senses.definitionCN: 岩石温度随深度上升，这是地热可及的原因
senses.example: The geothermal gradient makes deep drilling a heat resource.
senses.exampleCN: 地温梯度使深钻成为一种热资源。
senses.why: heat is not evenly spread, and the gradient is what makes depth worth the cost.
senses.whyCN: 热并不均匀分布，正是这个梯度让深度值得付出成本。

senses.title: Geothermal energy
senses.definition: the heat extracted from the earth and counted as a renewable energy source
senses.definitionCN: 从地下取出的热，计为一种可再生能源
senses.example: Geothermal energy works whether or not the sun shines.
senses.exampleCN: 无论是否出太阳，地热能都能工作。
senses.why: the heat flows continuously from radioactive decay, so it qualifies as renewable.
senses.whyCN: 热量由放射性衰变持续流出，因此它算可再生能源。

senses.title: Shallow heat exchange
senses.definition: describing systems that use the stable temperature a few metres down to heat or cool buildings
senses.definitionCN: 用地下数米处稳定温度给建筑供暖或制冷的系统
senses.example: A geothermal heat pump uses the ground as a steady thermal battery.
senses.exampleCN: 地源热泵把土地当作一块稳定的热电池。
senses.why: the shallow ground stays near constant temperature, so the adjective covers low-temperature use as well as power.
senses.whyCN: 浅层地温几乎恒定，因此这个形容词也涵盖低温利用，不只发电。

senses.title: The reservoir
senses.definition: a body of hot water or steam trapped in permeable rock
senses.definitionCN: 困在可渗透岩石中的热水或蒸汽体
senses.example: The geothermal reservoir must be recharged by rain or magma.
senses.exampleCN: 地热储层必须由雨水或岩浆补给。
senses.why: to use the heat you need a medium that carries it, and that medium is the reservoir.
senses.whyCN: 要利用热量就需要搬运它的介质，这个介质就是储层。

senses.title: The power plant
senses.definition: describing flash, dry-steam or binary plants that turn steam into electricity
senses.definitionCN: 描述把蒸汽变成电的闪蒸、干蒸汽或双循环电厂
senses.example: Geothermal power plants run continuously, unlike solar farms.
senses.exampleCN: 地热电厂可以持续运行，不像光伏电站。
senses.why: the adjective before power plant names the fuel, which here is steam from rock.
senses.whyCN: 放在「发电厂」前的这个形容词命名燃料，而这里的燃料是来自岩石的蒸汽。

senses.title: Surface hot water
senses.definition: describing hot springs, geysers, fumaroles and other visible signs of underground heat
senses.definitionCN: 描述温泉、间歇泉、喷气孔等地下热的可见迹象
senses.example: Geothermal features attract visitors to the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 地热景观吸引游客来到这条山谷。
senses.why: before any drilling, the heat announces itself at the surface in water and steam.
senses.whyCN: 在钻探之前，热就通过水与蒸汽在地表自我宣告。

senses.title: Exploration and drilling
senses.definition: describing surveys, wells and resource assessment needed to find and reach the heat
senses.definitionCN: 描述寻找并到达热量所需的勘测、井与资源评估
senses.example: Geothermal exploration begins with mapping faults and hot springs.
senses.exampleCN: 地热勘探从测绘断层与温泉开始。
senses.why: heat has no market until a well proves it, so the adjective also labels the search phase.
senses.whyCN: 在井证明之前，热没有市场，因此这个形容词也标记寻找阶段。

senses.title: Sustainability and reinjection
senses.definition: describing the management of pressure, water and heat so a field lasts decades
senses.definitionCN: 描述对压力、水与热的管理，使地热田维持数十年
senses.example: Geothermal sustainability depends on returning water to the reservoir.
senses.exampleCN: 地热的可持续性取决于把水回灌到储层。
senses.why: heat can be mined out like any stock if the water is not returned.
senses.whyCN: 如果不把水送回，热也会像任何存量一样被采空。

intro.en: Geothermal is Greek gē 'earth' plus thermē 'heat', with the English adjective ending -al. The word is a nineteenth-century scientific coinage, formed when geologists began measuring temperature with depth; its exact first printed use is uncertain (source uncertain for the date only).
intro.cn: geothermal 是希腊 gē「大地」加 thermē「热」，再接英语形容词词尾 -al。这个词是十九世纪的科学造词，形成于地质学家开始测量温度随深度变化之时；它最早的印刷使用年代不确定（仅年代存疑）。

items.en: Gē meant earth or ground, and supplies the geo- of geology, geography and geothermal.
items.cn: gē 意为大地或地面，提供 geology、geography 与 geothermal 的 geo-。

items.en: Thermē meant heat, from thermos 'hot', and gives thermal, thermometer and thermos.
items.cn: thermē 意为热，源自 thermos「热的」，给出 thermal、thermometer 与 thermos。

items.en: Enlightenment science built compounds such as geography and geology from Greek geo-, accustoming English to the pattern.
items.cn: 启蒙时代的科学用希腊 geo- 构成 geography 与 geology 等复合词，使英语习惯了这个模式。

items.en: Nineteenth-century miners and geologists measured rock temperature in deep shafts and found it rising with depth.
items.cn: 十九世纪的矿工与地质学家在深井中测量岩石温度，发现它随深度上升。

items.en: Geothermal entered technical writing to describe that deep heat and later the systems built to use it.
items.cn: geothermal 进入技术写作，用来描述那种深部热量，后来也指利用它的系统。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the adjective's earliest printed use is usually placed in the nineteenth century, but no single year is settled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：这个形容词最早的印刷使用通常定在十九世纪，但没有公认的具体年份。

note.en: Group one holds the closely related forms and fixed phrases built on the same adjective; group two holds the neighbouring heat words with different sources.
note.cn: 第一组是基于同一形容词的近亲形式与固定搭配；第二组是来源不同的邻近热学词。

entries.definition: An uncommon synonym built with -ic instead of -al; it appears in older technical prose but is rarely used now.
entries.definitionCN: 用 -ic 而非 -al 构成的罕见同义词；见于较旧的技术文字，如今少用。

entries.definition: The heat resource itself; the adjective alone only describes something as belonging to underground heat.
entries.definitionCN: 热资源本身；单独形容词只描述某物属于地下热。

entries.definition: The rate at which temperature rises with depth; it is a quantity, not a category of energy.
entries.definitionCN: 温度随深度上升的速率；它是一个量，不是能源类别。

entries.definition: A machine that exchanges heat with the shallow ground; it uses geothermal conditions but is not the heat itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与浅层地下交换热量的机器；它利用地热条件，但不是热本身。

entries.definition: Relating to heat or temperature in general; it says nothing about where the heat comes from.
entries.definitionCN: 与热或温度有关，泛指；不说明热来自何处。

entries.definition: Relating to hot water circulating underground, as at vents and hot springs; geothermal is the broader heat term.
entries.definitionCN: 与地下循环的热水有关，如喷口与温泉；geothermal 是更宽的热量词。

entries.definition: Relating to volcanoes and magma; volcanism is one source of geothermal heat, not its definition.
entries.definitionCN: 与火山和岩浆有关；火山作用是地热的一个来源，而非其定义。

entries.definition: Describing heat-exchange systems that use the upper ground; it is the low-temperature branch of geothermal use.
entries.definitionCN: 描述利用上层地温的换热系统；它是地热利用中的低温分支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real Greek roots and the real depth-temperature relationship.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的希腊词根，以及真实的深度与温度关系。

normal.en: geo is earth, thermē is heat: the word is simply earth-heat.
normal.cn: geo 是大地，thermē 是热：这个词就是地下的热。

normal.en: The deeper you go, the hotter the rock: that is the gradient.
normal.cn: 越往深处，岩石越热：这就是梯度。

normal.en: Two uses: shallow heat pumps for buildings, deep steam for turbines.
normal.cn: 两种用途：浅层热泵给建筑用，深层蒸汽推涡轮。

normal.en: The heat comes from radioactive decay in rock, not from the sun.
normal.cn: 热量来自岩石中的放射性衰变，而不是太阳。

normal.en: A field lasts only if water goes back in.
normal.cn: 只有把水回灌，地热田才能维持。

abstract.en: Geothermal is a stove that was lit before the first fire.
abstract.cn: 地热是第一堆火之前就已点着的灶。

abstract.en: It is a well that brings up buried weather.
abstract.cn: 它是一口把埋藏的天气带上来的井。

abstract.en: The earth's heat is patient capital.
abstract.cn: 地球的热量是极有耐心的资本。

examples.en: Iceland heats most of its homes with geothermal water.
examples.cn: 冰岛用地下热水为大多数家庭供暖。

examples.en: Geothermal drilling is expensive before the first well proves the reservoir.
examples.cn: 在第一口井证明储层之前，地热钻探成本很高。

examples.en: The team mapped the geothermal potential of the valley.
examples.cn: 团队测绘了这条山谷的地热潜力。

dict_mnemonic.text: geo（大地）+ thermal（热的）＝地下的热；两种用途：浅层热泵与深层蒸汽发电。

root: geo-（希腊 gē「大地」）+ thermal（希腊 thermē「热」，源自 thermos「热的」）+ -al（拉丁 -alis）；词为十九世纪科学造词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses go from the general property to the field: earth heat, the gradient, the energy, shallow exchange, reservoirs, plants, surface features, exploration and reinjection.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一般属性走到具体地热田：地下热、梯度、能源、浅层换热、储层、电厂、地表景观、勘探，以及回灌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drill reaches hot rock, water flashes to steam, the steam spins a turbine, and the cooled water is sent back down.
core.cn: 核心意象：钻头到达热岩，水闪蒸成汽，汽推动涡轮，冷却的水又被送回地下。

branches.en: THE PROPERTY AND ITS PHYSICS: underground heat, then the gradient that makes depth useful.
branches.cn: 属性与物理：先是地下热，再是让深度变得可用的梯度。

branches.en: HIGH AND LOW TEMPERATURE: the energy resource, then shallow heat exchange.
branches.cn: 高温与低温：先是能源资源，再是浅层换热。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND THE PLANT: the reservoir, then the turbines it feeds.
branches.cn: 地热田与电厂：先是储层，再是它供给的涡轮。

branches.en: THE SURFACE SIGN: hot springs and geysers announcing heat before drilling.
branches.cn: 地表迹象：温泉与间歇泉在钻探之前宣告热的存在。

branches.en: FINDING AND KEEPING: exploration, then reinjection to make the field last.
branches.cn: 寻找与维持：先是勘探，再是让地热田持久的回灌。

intro.en: Geothermal is a Greek compound: earth plus heat, closed with the Latin-derived adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: geothermal 是希腊语复合词：大地加热，再用拉丁语源形容词词尾 -al 收束。

latinIntro.en: Both roots are Greek and have no native Latin cognates; Latin only supplied the adjective ending -alis.
latinIntro.cn: 两个词根都属希腊语，在拉丁语中无本土同族词；拉丁语只提供了形容词词尾 -alis。

items.example: Gē supplies the geo- of the word.
items.exampleCN: gē 提供这个词的 geo-。

items.example: Thermē supplies the thermal half.
items.exampleCN: thermē 提供 thermal 那一半。

items.example: Thermos is the adjective behind thermē.
items.exampleCN: thermos 是 thermē 背后的形容词。

items.example: -al turns the compound into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: -al 把复合词变成形容词。

items.meaning: relating to heat in the earth
items.example: Geothermal labels both the heat and its uses.
items.exampleCN: geothermal 既标记热，也标记其利用。

items.example: Geothermics grew with deep drilling.
items.exampleCN: 地热学随深钻发展起来。

items.example: Geothermometry reads minerals as thermometers.
items.exampleCN: 地温测量把矿物当作温度计来读。

items.example: Hydrothermal vents sit on the sea floor.
items.exampleCN: 热液喷口位于海底。

items.example: Thermal is the general adjective.
items.exampleCN: thermal 是泛指热的形容词。

definition_zh: 理解；领会；包含；抓住（古义）
definition_en: to grasp the meaning of something, or to include it within a whole
core_image: 手指把散落的小块拼成一整块，缺口终于对上。
scene: 一个孩子听完一段绕弯的故事后，忽然点头，把结局复述给旁边的同伴。 The child paused, then began to comprehend the ending well enough to retell it.
sceneCN: 这里 comprehend 指「把握住某段内容的意义」（第 1 个义项：把分散信息合成可理解的整体）；句意为孩子停顿之后开始理解结局，并能复述出来。可辨识物件：孩子、同伴、故事书、点头动作。

pos.zh: 理解；领会；包含
理解（较少单独使用）

derivatives.zh: 理解；理解力
可理解的
全面的；综合的
有理解力的
无法理解的

senses.title: Grasp the meaning of something
senses.definition: to take in the meaning of information and hold its parts together as one
senses.definitionCN: 接收信息的意义，并把各部分作为整体握在一起
senses.example: The child paused, then began to comprehend the ending well enough to retell it.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子停顿了一下，随后开始理解结局，并能复述出来。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to grasp together, so the mental act is pictured as a hand closing around all the parts.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「合起来抓」，因此心理动作被描绘成一只手把各部分合拢握住。

senses.title: Follow what is said or written
senses.definition: to understand a particular sentence or utterance as it is heard or read
senses.definitionCN: 听懂或读懂某一个具体的句子或话语
senses.example: She comprehended the announcement before the translator finished.
senses.exampleCN: 译员还没说完，她就听懂了那则通告。
senses.why: This is the most common object of the verb: a specific string of words must be turned into a message.
senses.whyCN: 这是该动词最常见的宾语情形：一串具体的词必须被转成一条信息。

senses.title: Take in an abstract idea
senses.definition: to grasp an idea, principle or situation that has no single visible form
senses.definitionCN: 把握没有单一可见形态的观念、原则或处境
senses.example: Few new employees comprehend why the rule exists.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有新员工领会这条规则为何存在。
senses.why: An idea has no edges for the hand, so the grasp must be mental, yet the same verb serves.
senses.whyCN: 观念没有可供手抓的边缘，因此抓取只能是心理的，但同一个动词仍然适用。

senses.title: Include something within a whole
senses.definition: to contain or include something as a part of a larger whole
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为更大整体的一部分容纳或包括进来
senses.example: The old estate comprehends both the orchard and the mill.
senses.exampleCN: 这份旧地产既包括果园，也包括磨坊。
senses.why: The original physical sense of holding everything inside a boundary survives in formal legal and descriptive writing.
senses.whyCN: 把一切收在边界之内的原始具体义，保存在正式的法律与描述性写作中。

senses.title: Seize with the hand
senses.definition: to seize or grasp something physically, an older use now largely replaced by grasp
senses.definitionCN: 用手抓取或握住某物，这一旧义如今大多已被同义的抓握动词取代
senses.example: In the old tale, the hero comprehends the rope and climbs.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个古老故事里，主人公抓住绳子向上攀。
senses.why: This is the literal root meaning before it was borrowed for the mind; the modern word keeps the image but not the action.
senses.whyCN: 这是借给心智使用之前最字面的词根义；现代词保留意象，却不再指手的动作。

senses.title: Hold the whole picture
senses.definition: to understand how the parts of a complex matter fit together as a system
senses.definitionCN: 理解一件复杂事情的各部分如何作为系统组合起来
senses.example: Only the lead engineer comprehended the whole design.
senses.exampleCN: 只有主管工程师把握了整个设计的全貌。
senses.why: Understanding a system is grasping many relations at once, which is the strongest form of the original image.
senses.whyCN: 理解一个系统就是同时握住许多关系，这是原有意象最强的一种形式。

senses.title: Take in a difficult situation
senses.definition: to come to understand and accept the reality of a situation, often after resistance
senses.definitionCN: 在抗拒之后逐渐理解并接受某一处境的现实
senses.example: He could not comprehend the loss until he saw the empty room.
senses.exampleCN: 直到看见空房间，他才真正理解这次失去。
senses.why: Here understanding includes an emotional acceptance, because the fact must be held, not merely noted.
senses.whyCN: 这里的理解包含情感上的接受，因为事实必须被握住，而不只是被注意到。

senses.title: Cover something by a rule or class
senses.definition: to fall within the scope of a rule, category or definition
senses.definitionCN: 落在某条规则、某个类别或定义的范围之内
senses.example: The clause comprehends every case of accidental damage.
senses.exampleCN: 这一条款涵盖所有意外损坏的情形。
senses.why: The inclusive sense is used in law and logic, where a rule is said to hold a case inside its scope.
senses.whyCN: 包含义用于法律与逻辑，那里说一条规则把某个情形收在其范围之内。

intro.en: Comprehend comes from Latin comprehendere, to grasp together, built from com-, together, and prehendere, to grasp.
intro.cn: comprehend 来自拉丁 comprehendere「合起来抓住」，由 com-「一起」与 prehendere「抓取」构成。

items.en: Prehendere meant to grasp or seize. Its deeper origin is generally considered to involve a reconstructed root whose exact form is not settled.
items.cn: prehendere 意为抓住、握取。其更早来源一般被认为涉及某个重构词根，确切形态尚无定论。

items.en: Com- plus prehendere made comprehendere, to grasp together or take in. The physical sense came first and the mental sense grew from it.
items.cn: com- 加 prehendere 构成 comprehendere「合起来抓住、收进来」。具体义先出现，心理义由它生长出来。

items.en: Old French comprehendre carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century, already with the mental sense of understanding.
items.cn: 古法语 comprehendre 在十四世纪把这个动词带入英语，当时已带有「理解」的心理义。

items.en: The inclusive sense, meaning to contain within a boundary, remained in legal and descriptive writing long after the physical sense faded.
items.cn: 表示「收在边界之内」的包含义，在具体义消退很久之后仍留在法律与描述性写作中。

items.en: Comprehend and understand now divide the work: comprehensions are often formal or textual, while understanding is the everyday verb.
items.cn: 如今 comprehend 与 understand 分工：comprehend 常偏正式或偏文本，understand 则是日常动词。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin of grasp): the earlier source of prehendere is a reconstructed form, and the exact date when the mental sense became dominant is not firmly fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（「抓取」义的拉丁语之前来源）：prehendere 的更早来源属重构形式；心理义成为主导的确切年代亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds family members that differ in meaning or word class; group two holds other verbs for understanding.
note.cn: 第一组是同族中含义或词性不同的词；第二组是其他表示「理解」的动词。

entries.definition: The act or power of understanding; the verb is the act, the noun is the act or the capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 理解的动作或能力；动词指动作，名词指动作或能力。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning complete or wide in scope; it never means able to understand.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为完整、范围广；它从不表示「能理解」。

entries.definition: Built with a prefix meaning toward; it can mean to seize or to understand, and now often means to fear.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀表示「朝向」；它可指抓住或领会，现今常指忧虑。

entries.definition: To be made up of or include; it shares the inclusive sense but comes through a different French form.
entries.definitionCN: 由……构成或包括；它共有包含义，但经另一个法语形式而来。

entries.definition: The general verb for grasping meaning; comprehend is its formal counterpart and often sounds more bookish.
entries.definitionCN: 把握意义的通用动词；comprehend 是它正式的对应词，常显得更书面。

entries.definition: To hold firmly, literally or mentally; grasping an idea is the plain image behind comprehend.
entries.definitionCN: 牢牢握住，可为具体或心理的；把握一个观念正是 comprehend 背后的朴素意象。

entries.definition: To keep pace with what is said or happening; it stresses sequence, while comprehend stresses the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 跟得上所说或所发生之事；它强调顺序，而 comprehend 强调整体。

entries.definition: To understand the worth or significance of something, often with approval; comprehend can be cooler.
entries.definitionCN: 理解某物的价值或意义，常带赞许；comprehend 可以更冷静。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the grasp root, the formal register and the difference from understand.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「抓取」词根、正式语域，以及与 understand 的区别。

normal.en: The prefix means together and the root means grasp: to comprehend is to hold all the parts at once.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「一起」，词根意为「抓」：理解就是同时握住所有部分。

normal.en: The family runs comprehend, comprehension, comprehensible, comprehensive and comprehensively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 comprehend、comprehension、comprehensible、comprehensive 与 comprehensively。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark difficulty: hard to comprehend, fail to comprehend, comprehend fully.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出难度：难以理解、未能理解、完全理解。

normal.en: The same root appears in apprehend, which adds a prefix meaning toward and shifts from seizing to fearing.
normal.cn: 同一词根还出现在 apprehend 中，它加上表示「朝向」的前缀，并从「抓住」转向「忧虑」。

normal.en: Comprehend often takes a whole clause as its object, as in comprehend why the rule exists.
normal.cn: comprehend 常以整个从句作宾语，如「领会这条规则为何存在」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing around several separate pieces until they click into one shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把几块分开的碎片合拢，直到它们咔哒一声拼成一个形状。

abstract.en: Picture a circle drawn around a scattered flock so that it becomes one herd.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圈把散开的羊群围住，使它们成为一群。

abstract.en: Picture a net lifted from the water with all its catch held inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网从水中提起，所有捕获都收在里面。

examples.en: The students could repeat the definition but not comprehend it.
examples.cn: 学生们能背出定义，却并不理解它。

examples.en: No one fully comprehends how the two systems interact.
examples.cn: 没有人完全理解这两个系统如何相互作用。

examples.en: The lease comprehends the garden as well as the house.
examples.cn: 这份租约既包括房屋，也包括花园。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把所有零散的部分合起来一把抓住，让它们成为一个整体 → 理解、包含

root: 拉丁 comprehendere「合起来抓住」= com-（一起）+ prehendere（抓取）；经古法语 comprehendre 入英语。prehendere 更早来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one grip: the hand closes around parts, and the same grip is then used for sentences, ideas, wholes, situations, legal scopes and the old physical act itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次握取展开：手把各部分合拢，这次握取随后被用于句子、观念、整体、处境、法律范围，以及古老的具体动作本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingers bringing scattered pieces together until the gap closes.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指把散落的块拼在一起，直到缺口合上。

branches.en: THE GRIP: meaning is held rather than merely met.
branches.cn: 握取：意义是被握住的，而非仅仅被遇见。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a sentence and an idea are both held, one by the ear and one by the mind.
branches.cn: 对象：句子与观念都被握住，一个靠耳朵，一个靠心智。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: a whole or a rule holds its parts inside a line.
branches.cn: 边界：整体或规则把各部分收在一条线内。

branches.en: THE OLD HAND: the literal grip survives in old stories and in the root itself.
branches.cn: 旧日的手：字面的握取留在古老故事与词根之中。

branches.en: THE WHOLE AND THE HARD CASE: a system, and then a loss, must be held before they are accepted.
branches.cn: 整体与难处：一个系统，随后是一次失去，都必须先被握住才谈得上接受。

intro.en: Comprehend is a Latin verb made of a prefix and a grasping root, and the same two pieces build a large English family.
intro.cn: comprehend 是由前缀与「抓取」词根构成的拉丁动词，同样这两部分构成一个庞大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin prehendere gives comprehend, apprehend, prehensile and the noun comprehension; com- adds the gathering sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 prehendere 衍生 comprehend、apprehend、prehensile 与名词 comprehension；com- 增添「收拢」义。

items.example: The prefix makes the grasping collective.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使抓取成为收拢一体的动作。

items.example: The root supplies the physical image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供具体意象。

items.example: She comprehends the rule now.
items.exampleCN: 她现在理解这条规则了。

items.example: Comprehension takes time.
items.exampleCN: 理解需要时间。

items.example: The note is comprehensible at a glance.
items.exampleCN: 这张便条一眼就能看懂。

items.example: A comprehensive list fills two pages.
items.exampleCN: 一份全面清单写满两页。

items.example: The comprehending reader notices the tone.
items.exampleCN: 有理解力的读者会注意到语气。

items.meaning: to seize; to understand; to fear
items.example: They apprehended the meaning slowly.
items.exampleCN: 他们慢慢领会了那层意思。

items.example: The animal has a prehensile tail.
items.exampleCN: 这种动物有一条能抓握的尾巴。

definition_zh: 统计学家；统计工作者；统计官员；数据统计人员
definition_en: a person who studies or applies statistics, or who prepares official statistical figures

scene: 试验开始之前，一位统计学家检查了抽样方案是否合理。 A statistician checked the sampling design before the trial began.
sceneCN: 这里指「以统计方法为专业的人」（第 1 个义项：统计学家）；句意为一位统计学家在试验开始前审查了抽样设计。可辨识物件：记录本、表格、计算器、抽样清单。

统计量

senses.title: A researcher in statistics
senses.definition: a person who develops or studies statistical theory and methods
senses.definitionCN: 发展或研究统计理论与方法的人
senses.example: A statistician checked the sampling design before the trial began.
senses.exampleCN: 一位统计学家在试验开始前审查了抽样设计。
senses.why: The personal ending -ian marks a practitioner of the field named by the base word.
senses.whyCN: 表示人的词尾标出一个以该学科为业的人。

senses.title: A practitioner in industry
senses.definition: a person employed to apply statistical methods to practical problems
senses.definitionCN: 受雇把统计方法用于实际问题的人
senses.example: The company hired a statistician to review its quality data.
senses.exampleCN: 公司聘用了一位统计人员来审查质量数据。
senses.why: Industry needs the methods more than the theory, so the same title covers applied work.
senses.whyCN: 工业更需要方法而非理论，因此同一个头衔也覆盖应用工作。

senses.title: A government statistical officer
senses.definition: an official who prepares or publishes state figures
senses.definitionCN: 编制或发布国家数字的官员
senses.example: The official statistician signed the annual report.
senses.exampleCN: 官方统计人员签署了年度报告。
senses.why: The word grew up beside the description of states, and the official role keeps that oldest setting.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与国家描述一同成长，官方职位保留了最古老的场景。

senses.title: A biostatistician in trials
senses.titleCN: 临床试验中的生物统计师
senses.definition: a statistician who designs and analyses medical studies
senses.definitionCN: 设计并分析医学研究的统计人员
senses.example: The biostatistician set the rule for stopping the trial early.
senses.exampleCN: 生物统计师定下了提前终止试验的规则。
senses.why: Medicine needs a specialist to judge evidence, so the field grows a compound title with its own duties.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要专人来判断证据，于是这一行发展出带专门职责的复合头衔。

senses.title: An actuarial statistician
senses.definition: a statistician who estimates risk for insurers or pension funds
senses.definitionCN: 为保险公司或养老基金估计风险的统计人员
senses.example: An actuarial statistician modelled the claims for the next decade.
senses.exampleCN: 一位精算统计人员为今后十年的理赔建模。
senses.why: Risk pricing is an old statistical trade, and the title marks the person who does it.
senses.whyCN: 为风险定价是一门古老的统计行业，这个头衔标出做这件事的人。

senses.title: A sports statistician
senses.definition: a person who records and interprets performance figures in sport
senses.definitionCN: 记录并解读体育表现数字的人
senses.example: The team's statistician tracked every pass in the match.
senses.exampleCN: 球队的统计员记录了比赛中的每一次传球。
senses.why: Where performance is counted, someone is employed to keep the count, and the name follows the task.
senses.whyCN: 凡表现被计数的地方，就有人受雇维持这份计数，名称也随之而来。

senses.title: A data analyst in modern usage
senses.titleCN: 现代用法中的数据统计人员
senses.definition: a person whose work is largely statistical even if the job title differs
senses.definitionCN: 工作实质以统计为主、即使职位名称不同的人
senses.example: The job advert asked for a statistician who could code.
senses.exampleCN: 招聘启事要招一位会写程序的统计人员。
senses.why: The title has widened with computing, since the same methods now run on large datasets.
senses.whyCN: 随着计算技术发展，这个头衔变宽了，因为同样的方法如今跑在大数据集上。

senses.title: A teacher or consultant in statistics
senses.definition: a person who teaches the subject or advises others on its use
senses.definitionCN: 教授这门学科、或就它的使用向他人提供建议的人
senses.example: They brought in a statistician to explain the results to the board.
senses.exampleCN: 他们请来一位统计人员向董事会解释结果。
senses.why: Explaining numbers to non-specialists is part of the trade, so teaching and advice fall under the same name.
senses.whyCN: 向非专业者解释数字也是这一行的一部分，因此教学与咨询都归在同一个名称下。

intro.en: Statistician is statistics with the personal ending -ian, which English borrows from Latin adjectives in -ianus. The word appears in the nineteenth century as the subject took shape.
intro.cn: statistician 是 statistics 加表示人的词尾 -ian 构成，这个结尾源自拉丁语以 -ianus 结尾的形容词。这个词随学科成形，出现在十九世纪。

items.en: Status 'standing, condition' is the base of the whole family, and it comes from stare 'to stand'.
items.cn: status「处境、状况」是整个词族的基础，出自 stare「站立」。

items.en: German Statistik named the systematic description of a state, and English borrowed it late in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 德语 Statistik 指对国家状况的系统描述，英语在十八世纪末借入。

items.en: The English noun first meant the descriptive study of states, then the numerical analysis of any data.
items.cn: 这个英语名词先指对国家的描述性研究，后指对任何数据的数值分析。

items.en: -ianus in Latin formed adjectives of belonging, and English turns such adjectives into personal nouns with -ian.
items.cn: 拉丁 -ianus 构成表示归属的形容词，英语把这类形容词变为以 -ian 结尾的人物名词。

items.en: Statistician appears as the discipline acquires practitioners with a recognised title; exact first citations are approximate.
items.cn: statistician 随这门学科出现而出现，从业者有了公认头衔；确切的最早书证只是约数。

items.en: Computing and applied fields widened the title in the twentieth century, though the dictionary sense remains the statistical specialist.
items.cn: 二十世纪的计算与应用领域使这个头衔变宽，但词典义仍是统计专门人才。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same statistics base; group two holds neighbouring job titles and specialists.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在同一 statistics 词基上的形式；第二组是邻近的职称与专门人才。

entries.definition: The name of the discipline, which takes a singular verb when it means the subject.
entries.definitionCN: 学科名称；指这门学科时接单数动词。

entries.definition: A single computed number, not a person and not the science.
entries.definitionCN: 一个计算出来的数值，既不是人，也不是学科。

entries.definition: Relating to statistics, with no reference to a person.
entries.definitionCN: 关于统计学的形容词，不指人。

entries.definition: By statistical means, as in statistically significant.
entries.definitionCN: 以统计方式，如「统计上显著」。

entries.definition: A person who interprets data, often without formal statistical training.
entries.definitionCN: 解读数据的人，未必受过正式统计训练。

entries.definition: A specialist who calculates insurance and pension risk, traditionally from the same mathematical stock.
entries.definitionCN: 计算保险与养老风险的专业人士，传统上出自同一数学渊源。

entries.definition: A person who studies the spread of disease in populations, a heavy user of statistics.
entries.definitionCN: 研究疾病在人群中传播的人，重度依赖统计学。

entries.definition: A person who studies populations and their structure, using many statistical figures.
entries.definitionCN: 研究人口及其结构的人，使用大量统计数字。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is the field plus the personal ending, so it means the person who works with the field.
normal.cn: 这个词是学科名加表示人的词尾，因此指以这门学科为业的人。

normal.en: One family runs statistics, statistic, statistical, statistically and statistician.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：统计学、统计量、统计的、从统计上看、统计学家。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the roles: medical statistician, official statistician, chief statistician.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出角色：医学统计学家、官方统计人员、首席统计师。

normal.en: The oldest setting is the state: the title grew beside the description of a country's people and resources.
normal.cn: 最古老的场景是国家：这个头衔与国家人口资源的描述一同成长。

normal.en: The ending is the same one that turns a subject into a person, as in musician or historian.
normal.cn: 这个词尾与把学科变成人的词尾相同，如同音乐家或历史学家。

abstract.cn: 想象一个人伏在长桌前，把一叠记录本变成一张干净的表格。

abstract.en: Picture a referee of evidence who can stop a trial early if the numbers say so.
abstract.cn: 想象一位证据的裁判，若数字如此显示，就能提前终止试验。

abstract.en: Picture someone explaining a curve to a board of directors who fear numbers.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人向害怕数字的董事会解释一条曲线。

examples.en: A statistician reviewed the survey before it was released.
examples.cn: 调查发布之前，一位统计学家审查了它。

examples.en: The hospital employs two biostatisticians.
examples.cn: 这家医院聘用两名生物统计师。

examples.en: She trained as a statistician and later became a data analyst.
examples.cn: 她受的是统计训练，后来成了数据分析师。

dict_mnemonic.text: 学科名加表示人的词尾：从事这门学问的人。它的词根原指「国家的状态」，因此最早的一批这样的人是在描述国家的人口与资源。

root: statistics 加表示人物的词尾 -ian（源自拉丁 -ianus）；statistics 出德语 Statistik（十八世纪造词），再上溯新拉丁 statisticum 与拉丁 status「状态、处境」，status 出自 stare「站立」。十九世纪出现，确切首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe one worker in different settings: a researcher, an industrial practitioner, a government officer, a trial specialist, an actuary, a sports recorder, a data analyst and a teacher. The title follows the task rather than the employer.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述同一种工作者在不同场景中的身份：研究者、业界从业者、政府官员、试验专家、精算人员、体育记录员、数据分析者与教师。这个头衔跟着任务走，而不跟着雇主走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a long table turning a stack of record books into one clean sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人伏在长桌前，把一叠记录本变成一张干净的表格。

branches.en: THE TRADE: research, industry and modern data work all apply the same methods.
branches.cn: 行业：研究、工业与现代数据工作都应用同样的方法。

branches.en: THE STATE: the oldest setting is the official description of a country.
branches.cn: 国家：最古老的场景是对一个国家的官方描述。

branches.en: HIGH-STAKES NUMBERS: medicine and insurance need specialists to judge risk.
branches.cn: 高风险数字：医学与保险需要专人来判断风险。

branches.en: THE RECORD: wherever performance is counted, someone keeps the count.
branches.cn: 记录：凡表现被计数的地方，就有人维持计数。

branches.en: THE ADVICE: teaching and consulting turn the trade outward.
branches.cn: 建议：教学与咨询把这门行业转向外部。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 status 给出 statistics；拉丁 -ianus 给出英语的人物词尾 -ian。

definition_zh: 条件作用；条件反射训练；调理；训练
definition_en: the process of training behaviour through repeated stimuli, or of bringing something into a desired condition
core_image: 反复按同一个按钮，让反应变成不假思索
scene: 这里指「条件作用」。 In the lab, the rat learned to press a lever because every press brought a food pellet, a clear case of operant conditioning.
sceneCN: 这里 conditioning 是「操作性条件作用」（第 2 个义项：通过结果强化塑造行为）；句意：实验室里，老鼠因为每次按杆都会得到食物丸而学会按杆，这是操作性条件作用的典型案例。图中可辨识物件：斯金纳箱、金属杆、食物丸、老鼠、记录曲线。

senses.title: Behavioural conditioning by repetition
senses.titleCN: 行为条件反射训练：重复塑形
senses.definition: the process of training a person or animal to respond in a particular way through repeated experience
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复经验把人或动物训练成特定反应的过程
senses.example: Years of conditioning made the dog sit whenever the bell rang.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的条件反射训练让这只狗一听到铃声就坐下。
senses.why: condition is the base and -ing makes it a process noun: conditioning is not one act but the repeated bringing of behaviour into a set condition.
senses.whyCN: condition 是词基，-ing 把它变成过程名词：conditioning 不是一次动作，而是把行为反复带入某个既定状态的过程。

senses.title: Operant conditioning: shaping by consequences
senses.titleCN: 操作性条件作用：用结果塑形
senses.definition: learning in which behaviour is shaped by rewards and punishments that follow it
senses.definitionCN: 由行为之后的奖励和惩罚来塑造行为的学习过程
senses.example: Operant conditioning rewarded the rat with food each time it pressed the lever.
senses.exampleCN: 操作性条件作用在老鼠每次按杆时用食物奖励它。
senses.why: Here -ing names the whole training loop: an action, a consequence, and a changed likelihood of repeating the action.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 -ing 命名的是整个训练回路：一个动作、一个结果，以及该动作再次发生的概率变化。

senses.title: Classical conditioning: pairing stimuli
senses.titleCN: 经典条件作用：把刺激配对
senses.definition: learning in which a neutral stimulus becomes linked to a reflexive response through repeated pairing
senses.definitionCN: 中性刺激通过反复配对而与反射性反应建立联系的学习过程
senses.example: Pavlov's classical conditioning paired a bell with food until the bell alone triggered salivation.
senses.exampleCN: 巴甫洛夫的经典条件作用把铃声与食物配对，直到铃声单独就能引发唾液分泌。
senses.why: The process noun describes pairing rather than reward: two things are repeatedly placed together until one comes to stand for the other.
senses.whyCN: 这个过程中名词描述的是“配对”而非奖励：两样东西被反复放在一起，直到其中一个能代表另一个。

senses.title: Physical conditioning: building fitness
senses.titleCN: 体能训练：把身体练到状态
senses.definition: exercise that trains the body for strength, endurance, or a particular sport
senses.definitionCN: 为增强力量、耐力或适应某项运动而进行的身体训练
senses.example: The team spent six weeks on physical conditioning before the season.
senses.exampleCN: 球队在赛季前进行了六周体能训练。
senses.why: The older sense of condition is 'to bring into good condition'. With -ing, the word names the ongoing work of putting the body into that state.
senses.whyCN: condition 较早的义项是“使处于良好状态”。加上 -ing，这个词命名的是把身体逐步带入该状态的持续工作。

senses.title: Hair and skin conditioning
senses.titleCN: 头发/皮肤调理：改善表面状态
senses.definition: treatment that makes hair or skin softer, smoother, and easier to manage
senses.definitionCN: 使头发或皮肤更柔软、顺滑、易打理的处理
senses.example: This shampoo includes a conditioning agent that smooths the hair.
senses.exampleCN: 这款洗发水含有一种能让头发顺滑的调理成分。
senses.why: The same process noun is applied to a surface: a conditioner is the agent, and conditioning is the action of bringing hair or skin into a better condition.
senses.whyCN: 同一个过程名词被用于表面：conditioner 是施动产品，conditioning 则是把头发或皮肤带入更好状态的动作。

senses.title: Air conditioning: controlling indoor air
senses.titleCN: 空气调节：控制室内空气状态
senses.definition: the process of controlling the temperature, humidity, and quality of air in a space
senses.definitionCN: 控制某一空间内空气温度、湿度和质量的过程
senses.example: The office air conditioning failed during the hottest week of summer.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室的空调在夏天最热的一周坏了。
senses.why: Air conditioning is a fixed phrase in which -ing still means 'bringing into a condition'; the object is simply the air of a room.
senses.whyCN: air conditioning 是固定短语，其中的 -ing 仍表示“使进入某种状态”，只不过作用对象变成房间里的空气。

senses.title: Conditioning as a general process
senses.titleCN: 条件化过程：让事物取决于条件
senses.definition: the general process by which something is made to depend on or conform to conditions
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物依赖或符合条件的一般过程
senses.example: The conditioning of new employees takes place through daily routines.
senses.exampleCN: 新员工的条件化过程通过日常惯例发生。
senses.why: This is the broadest use: the verb condition means 'to attach conditions to', and -ing turns that into the process of attaching or imposing them.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽泛的用法：动词 condition 意为“给……附加条件”，-ing 把它变成附加或施加条件的过程。

senses.title: Social conditioning
senses.titleCN: 社会条件塑造：环境长期训练
senses.definition: the influence of society that shapes a person's beliefs, habits, and behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 社会对个人信念、习惯和行为的影响与塑造
senses.example: Social conditioning taught her to apologize for asking questions.
senses.exampleCN: 社会条件塑造让她为提出问题而道歉。
senses.why: Society is treated as the trainer. The -ing process noun extends from laboratory training to the long, repeated shaping done by a culture.
senses.whyCN: 社会被当作训练者。这个 -ing 过程名词从实验室训练扩展到文化长期反复进行的塑造。

senses.title: Adaptation through training
senses.titleCN: 训练适应过程：身体逐步调整
senses.definition: the gradual adjustment of body or mind to repeated physical or mental demands
senses.definitionCN: 身体或心理对反复出现的体力或脑力要求逐步作出的调整
senses.example: Athletic conditioning improves recovery as well as performance.
senses.exampleCN: 运动训练既提高表现，也改善恢复能力。
senses.why: The -ing form highlights gradualness: repeated demands bring the body into condition, and the process continues rather than ending at one session.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形式突出渐进性：反复的要求把身体带入状态，而这个过程中持续进行，并不在某一次训练后结束。

intro.en: Conditioning is a derived process noun: the borrowed base condition receives the native -ing suffix. The psychological sense is recent and technical; the older senses are about bringing something into a condition. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: conditioning 是派生的过程名词：借入的词基 condition 接受本族语后缀 -ing。心理学义项较晚且属术语；较早的义项都是“把某物带入某种状态”。年代为大致估计。

items.en: The base is Latin condicio(nem) 'agreement, stipulation', from condicere 'to say together, agree upon'. The earliest meaning is a settled term, not a state of matter.
items.cn: 词基是拉丁 condicio(nem)“协议、约定”，来自 condicere“共同说定”。最早的意思是谈定的条款，而不是物质状态。

items.en: English first used condition as a noun, then as a verb meaning 'to subject to conditions' and later 'to train or accustom'. The verb is the door through which -ing enters.
items.cn: 英语先以 condition 作名词，后来用作动词，表示“使受条件制约”，再发展出“训练、使习惯”。动词是 -ing 进入这个词的入口。

items.en: The native -ing suffix forms nouns of action or process. Attaching it to condition yields 'the process of conditioning', which can name an ongoing activity rather than a single event.
items.cn: 本族语 -ing 后缀构成动作或过程名词。附着在 condition 上就得到“conditioning 的过程”，可命名持续活动而非单次事件。

items.en: In 19c. sport and horse training, conditioning meant bringing the body into condition through regular exercise. The -ing form names the work, not the finished state.
items.cn: 在 19 世纪的运动和马匹训练中，conditioning 指通过规律锻炼把身体带入良好状态。-ing 形式命名的是这项工作，而不是完成后的状态。

items.en: Pavlov's work on paired stimuli and later Skinner's work on consequences made conditioning a technical term. Here -ing names a learning process: classical or operant.
items.cn: 巴甫洛夫关于刺激配对的研究以及后来斯金纳关于结果的研究，使 conditioning 成为术语。这里的 -ing 命名的是学习过程：经典的或操作性的。

items.en: Air conditioning and hair conditioning spread the same process noun into technology and personal care. The core remains 'bringing something into a desired condition'.
items.cn: air conditioning 和 hair conditioning 把同一个过程名词扩展到技术与个人护理。核心仍然是“把某物带入理想状态”。

note.en: The look-alikes are built from the same condition base with other endings. The near-meaning words all describe shaping or training, but differ in mechanism and register.
note.cn: 形近词都由同一个 condition 词基加其他词尾构成。近义词都描述塑造或训练，但在机制和语体上不同。

entries.definition: A term, a state, or the act of training. It is the base from which conditioning is derived, not the process noun itself.
entries.definitionCN: 条件、状态，或训练这一动作。它是 conditioning 的词基，而不是过程名词本身。

entries.definition: Already trained or made dependent. It describes the result, while conditioning describes the process.
entries.definitionCN: 已被训练好的或受条件制约的。它描述结果，而 conditioning 描述过程。

entries.definition: A product or device that improves condition, such as hair conditioner or an air conditioner.
entries.definitionCN: 改善状态的产品或装置，如护发素或空调设备。

entries.definition: The general activity of teaching a skill or behaviour through practice. It is broader and less technical than conditioning.
entries.definitionCN: 通过练习教授技能或行为的一般活动。它比 conditioning 更宽泛，技术性更弱。

entries.definition: The gradual weakening of a response after repeated exposure to a stimulus. It reduces a reaction rather than builds one.
entries.definitionCN: 反复接触刺激后反应逐渐减弱。它是在削弱反应，而不是建立反应。

entries.definition: The process by which people learn the norms of a society. It overlaps with social conditioning but stresses norms and learning.
entries.definitionCN: 人们学习社会规范的过程。它与社会条件塑造重叠，但强调规范和习得。

entries.definition: Training or restoring something again after decline or damage. The re- prefix marks repetition or restoration.
entries.definitionCN: 在衰退或损坏之后重新训练或修复。re- 前缀标记重复或恢复。

entries.definition: Repeated mechanical practice. It stresses repetition of an exercise, not the shaping of a response by stimuli.
entries.definitionCN: 反复机械的操练。它强调练习的重复，而不是用刺激塑造反应。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real base verb, the real process suffix, and the real technical phrases that keep the word alive.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词基动词、真实的过程后缀，以及让这个词保持活力的真实术语搭配。

normal.en: condition + -ing: the suffix turns 'bring into a condition' into 'the process of bringing into a condition'.
normal.cn: condition + -ing：后缀把“使进入状态”变成“使进入状态的过程”。

normal.en: Classical and operant are the two main laboratory routes: pairing stimuli versus rewarding consequences.
normal.cn: 经典与操作性是实验室里的两条主要路径：配对刺激，对比奖励结果。

normal.en: Air conditioning is the same process noun applied to air, not a separate word.
normal.cn: air conditioning 是同一个过程名词用在空气上，并不是另一个词。

normal.en: A conditioner is the product; conditioning is the action it performs.
normal.cn: conditioner 是产品；conditioning 是它所执行的动作。

normal.en: Social conditioning is society playing the trainer, repeating its lessons until they feel natural.
normal.cn: 社会条件塑造就是社会扮演训练者，重复它的课程，直到这些课程显得理所当然。

abstract.en: Think of a path worn into grass: no single walk makes it, but repetition turns the route into the obvious one.
abstract.cn: 想象草地上被踏出的一条路：没有哪一次行走能造成它，是反复行走让这条路线变成显而易见的选择。

abstract.en: Think of a thermostat: it does not change the room once, it keeps bringing the room back to a set condition.
abstract.cn: 想象恒温器：它不是只改变房间一次，而是不断把房间带回设定状态。

abstract.en: Think of a bar of soap used again and again on the same spot: the surface slowly becomes smoother.
abstract.cn: 想象一块肥皂反复用在同一个部位：表面慢慢变得更光滑。

examples.en: Classical conditioning explains why the dog salivates at the sound of the bell.
examples.cn: 经典条件作用解释了为什么这只狗一听到铃声就分泌唾液。

examples.en: The coach designed a conditioning programme to build endurance before the finals.
examples.cn: 教练设计了一套体能训练方案，为决赛前建立耐力。

examples.en: Poor air conditioning made the packed train uncomfortable.
examples.cn: 糟糕的空调让拥挤的列车很不舒服。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯迪神宁”——肯（con）迪（di）神（tion）宁（ing）反复训练到条件反射 → conditioning 条件作用、调理

root: condition（拉丁 condicio“约定、条件”）+ -ing（过程名词后缀）；从“反复设定条件”引申为“训练成自动反应”与“调理、调节”。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of conditioning is a process, never a single act: something is repeatedly exposed, exercised, or treated until its state changes.
sensesIntro.cn: conditioning 的每个义项都是过程，而不是单次动作：某物被反复暴露、锻炼或处理，直到它的状态发生改变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same button pressed again and again until the response needs no thought.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个按钮被反复按下，直到反应不再需要思考。

branches.en: BEHAVIOUR: repetition, reward, or pairing installs a response that later appears on its own.
branches.cn: 行为：重复、奖励或配对安装出一种反应，之后它会自行出现。

branches.en: THE BODY: exercise repeatedly brings strength and endurance into condition, and adaptation is the gradual result.
branches.cn: 身体：锻炼反复把力量与耐力带入状态，适应则是逐渐产生的结果。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: shampoo and conditioner treat hair or skin until it reaches a better condition.
branches.cn: 表面：洗发与护发处理作用于头发或皮肤，直到达到更好的状态。

branches.en: THE AIR: a room is repeatedly adjusted until temperature and humidity stay at a set condition.
branches.cn: 空气：房间被持续调节，直到温度和湿度维持在设定状态。

branches.en: THE GENERAL AND SOCIAL: conditions are attached to people, and a culture repeats its lessons until they become habits.
branches.cn: 一般与社会：条件被附加到人身上，而文化重复它的课程直到其成为习惯。

intro.en: Conditioning is a native suffix on a borrowed base: condition + -ing. The suffix is fully productive and carries the process meaning; the base supplies the idea of a condition or state.
intro.cn: conditioning 是借入词基加本族语后缀：condition + -ing。后缀完全能产，承担“过程”意义；词基提供“条件、状态”的观念。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family behind the base is condicio and condicere, from dicere 'to say'. English relatives outside conditioning include condition, conditional, precondition and recondition.
latinIntro.cn: 词基背后的拉丁词族是 condicio 和 condicere，源头为 dicere“说”。conditioning 之外的英语同族词包括 condition、conditional、precondition、recondition。

items.meaning: the process of training or bringing into a state
items.meaningCN: 条件作用；训练或调理的过程（-ing 构成过程名词）
items.example: Conditioning takes time because it depends on repetition.
items.exampleCN: 条件作用需要时间，因为它依赖重复。

items.meaning: a term or state; to train or make dependent
items.example: The trainer conditions the horse to accept a saddle.
items.exampleCN: 驯马师训练这匹马接受马鞍。

items.meaning: a product or device that improves condition
items.meaningCN: 护发素；调节器（-er 表示施动者或器具）
items.example: Apply the conditioner and leave it on for two minutes.
items.exampleCN: 涂上护发素，停留两分钟。

items.meaningCN: 条件化的；受制约的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The conditioned response appeared as soon as the light flashed.
items.exampleCN: 灯光一闪，条件化反应就出现了。

items.example: The dog gave its owner unconditional trust.
items.exampleCN: 这只狗无条件地信任主人。

items.meaning: a condition that must be met first
items.example: Good sleep is a precondition for effective training.
items.exampleCN: 良好睡眠是有效训练的先决条件。

items.meaningCN: 翻新；重新训练（re-“再次”+ condition）
items.example: The workshop reconditions old engines for sale.
items.exampleCN: 这家工坊翻新旧发动机用于出售。

items.meaningCN: 条件性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The conditionality of the funding worried the researchers.
items.exampleCN: 资金附带的条件让研究人员担忧。

items.meaningCN: 装有空调的（air + conditioned 复合形容词）
items.example: The library is air-conditioned throughout the summer.
items.exampleCN: 整个夏天图书馆都开着空调。

latinEntries.meaning: to say together, agree on terms
a saying, a word, a delivery
